items.title: close during an in-flight connect can leak an open socket and resolve a closed transport
items.recommendation: Store the socket on the instance immediately after createConnection, or keep a connectingSocket field that close can destroy. In the connect event handler, re-check this.closed before resolving; if closed, destroy or end the socket and reject or settle consistently as a local close.
items.reproduction: Start transport.connect(handlers) without awaiting it, immediately call transport.close(), then allow the underlying socket or pipe connection to complete. The close path cannot destroy the local sock, and the connect handler does not re-check this.closed before assigning this.socket and resolving.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Unix lifecycle test awaits connect before calling close, and the Windows tests only exercise pre-socket owner-gate failures or unavailable connections. There is no test that calls close while connect is still pending.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a controllable mocked net.createConnection or delayed server accept path: call connect, call close before emitting connect, then emit connect and assert the connect promise does not resolve to an open transport and the socket is destroyed or ended.
items.minimumFixScope: Update both concrete transports' connect/close state handling for the pending-connect window and add one shared lifecycle regression pattern for each platform implementation.

items.title: Backpressured sends can resolve successfully after the transport drops
items.recommendation: Track pending backpressure writes as resolve/reject pairs, reject them on error or peer close, and only resolve them when the write is actually accepted under a still-open transport. Consider using the write callback as the success boundary instead of resolving immediately from the boolean return path.
items.reproduction: Connect to a server that accepts the socket or pipe but stops reading, call send with a large payload until write backpressure is hit, then close or destroy the peer before drain. The pending send promise resolves via fireClose instead of rejecting with an anvil-daemon-transport-drop error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix happy-path test sends one small line and waits for a normal round trip. The Windows tests do not create a pipe connection. None of the tests force write backpressure or close the transport while a send promise is pending.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add paired Unix and Windows/fake-socket tests that force socket.write to return false, trigger error or close before drain, and assert the pending send rejects with code anvil-daemon-transport-drop rather than resolving.
items.minimumFixScope: Update UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport pending-write bookkeeping and add focused transport tests for backpressure plus close/error ordering.

items.title: Codemod reports errors but still exits successfully
items.recommendation: Set `process.exitCode = 1` or throw when `totalErrors > 0`, and avoid printing the success message in that path. If partial rewrites are possible, make the summary explicitly distinguish applied changes from failed files.
items.reproduction: Run `anvil-codemod imports` against an input that makes `rewriteImportsInFile` return at least one error; the CLI prints the error count but completes without setting `process.exitCode`, so the shell observes success.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this CLI command, and the package scripts only define build/codemod commands rather than assertions about exit status.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI-level test that stubs or triggers a transform error, runs the `imports` command, and asserts a non-zero exit code plus no 'Changes applied successfully' message.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` error summary handling and add a focused CLI exit-status test.

items.title: DiagnosticLocation omits documented null line and column values
items.recommendation: Change the nullable location fields to include null, for example line?: number | null, column?: number | null, end_line?: number | null, and end_column?: number | null, or update the contract text if null is no longer valid on the wire.
items.reproduction: const loc: DiagnosticLocation = { file: 'README.md', line: null }; // TypeScript rejects null under strictNullChecks
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostics test only covers the omitted-field case and asserts line/column are undefined after JSON round-trip. It never constructs or type-checks an explicit null location value.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostics type parity test that constructs a Diagnostic with location: { file: 'README.md', line: null, column: null } and round-trips it through JSON, if null is valid per the wire contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/diagnostics/types.ts plus the diagnostics parity test

items.title: Package bin can no-op when invoked through a symlinked binary
items.recommendation: Use a more robust main-module check for Node ESM, for example compare realpath-normalised file paths for import.meta.url and process.argv[1], or remove the guard from the actual bin entrypoint and keep import-safe behaviour in a separate module.
items.reproduction: Install/link the package so node_modules/.bin/anvil-admin points at apps/admin-cli/dist/index.js, then execute node_modules/.bin/anvil-admin --help. If process.argv[1] is the bin link while import.meta.url is the resolved dist file URL, the guard is false and run() is never called.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing run() test calls run() directly with argv values; it does not execute the packaged bin path or exercise the invokedAsBin guard.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that imports or executes the built entrypoint through a symlinked bin path and asserts --help exits 0 with help output, or factor the main detection into a helper and cover symlink-normalised paths.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/src/index.ts main-entry guard plus a focused test in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/index.test.ts

items.title: Kindling parity fixture is not typechecked against the public Diagnostic contract
items.recommendation: Update the kindling test fixture to use `schema_version` and `summary`, and add a spec/test typecheck path or include tests in package typechecking so invalid public-contract fixtures fail before runtime tests run.
items.reproduction: Run the existing package typecheck and tests: both pass because test files are excluded from `tsc` and Vitest does not perform semantic typechecking; then include `src/kindling/types.test.ts` in a TypeScript check and the `Diagnostic` return object is missing required fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The runtime helper only reads `severity` and `source.rule_id`, so the malformed fields do not affect assertions. The TypeScript configuration explicitly excludes tests from `tsc --noEmit`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `typecheck:test` script or `tsconfig.spec.json` that typechecks `src/**/*.test.ts`, then keep `makeDiag()` typed as `Diagnostic` with the canonical snake_case fields.
items.minimumFixScope: Fix `src/kindling/types.test.ts` fixture fields and add test-file typechecking to the package validation scripts.

items.title: Rejected DriverClientError does not expose the documented error discriminator
items.recommendation: Add a public readonly `error: DriverErrorCode` property to `DriverClientError` initialised from `payload.error`, keep `code` as a compatibility alias, and update direct request/connect tests to assert both the documented `error` discriminator and the legacy `code` alias.
items.reproduction: Catch a rejected `DriverClient.request()` timeout or transport-drop error and inspect `(err as any).error`; it is undefined while `(err as any).code` contains the discriminator.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The direct request/connect tests assert `.code`, which locks in the alias rather than the exported `DriverError.error` contract. The tests that assert `.error` go through `validateMidEdit`, which converts with `toJSON()` and therefore bypasses the rejected Error instance shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: In `src/client/driver-client.test.ts`, for timeout, transport drop, wrong-owner, and pre-connect rejection cases, assert `(err as DriverClientError).error` equals the same discriminator currently asserted via `.code`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `src/errors.ts` `DriverClientError` only, then adjust direct client/framing tests to cover the documented property.

items.title: Shell integration tests source the wrapper path without shell quoting
items.recommendation: Add a small shell-quoting helper for paths embedded in `bash -c` scripts, or avoid string interpolation by passing the script path as an argument/environment variable and sourcing `"$ANVIL_RUN_SCRIPT"`. Apply it consistently at all three call sites.
items.reproduction: Run the crate tests from a checkout path containing a space, or adjust the test to source a copied `anvil-run.sh` from a temp directory named with a space; the generated `. /path/with space/anvil-run.sh` command will not source the intended file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests use the current `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which usually has no whitespace or shell metacharacters, so the unquoted path bug is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Copy `shell/anvil-run.sh` into a temp directory whose name contains a space, source that copied path through the same test helper, and assert the dispatcher still invokes the stub.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `crates/anvil-run/tests/shell_integration.rs` to quote or otherwise safely pass `script_path()` in all generated bash snippets.

items.title: Parser accepts inherited fields as valid wire data
items.recommendation: Read required fields only as own properties, or normalise parsed records into null-prototype/plain own-property dictionaries before validation. For example, use Object.hasOwn(obj, 'schema_version') before reading each required field, and apply the same rule to SurfaceClaim fields and the validate_write response envelope's protection_claim field.
items.reproduction: const proto = { schema_version: 'anvil.protection-claim.v1', worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] }; parseProtectionClaim(Object.create(proto)); // currently returns a valid full claim instead of rejecting missing own fields
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hostile-input suite covers a JSON.parse('__proto__') payload where schema_version is not an own field, but it does not cover inherited claim fields or Object.prototype pollution. The missing-required-field tests use ordinary object literals with clean prototypes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add hostile-input tests asserting parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({ schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] })) rejects on schema_version, and parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({ identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating' })) rejects on identifier.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden protection_claim/types.ts field extraction for parseProtectionClaim, parseSurfaceClaim, and parseOptionalProtectionClaimFromValidateWrite; add targeted hostile-input regression tests.

items.title: Package build script points at a missing TypeScript config
items.recommendation: Change the build script to use the actual package config, or add a tsconfig.lib.json that extends tsconfig.json and is committed alongside the package. Keep the emitted declaration settings aligned with the package exports.
items.reproduction: From .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/packages/anvil-driver-client, run pnpm build or tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json; TypeScript will fail to find tsconfig.lib.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise runtime helpers via Vitest. They do not run the package build script or assert that the published export files can be emitted.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level build validation in CI, such as pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-driver-client build, and assert dist/index.js and dist/index.d.ts are produced.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json build script and, if declarations are not already inherited from the base config, the package TypeScript config needed to emit dist declarations.

items.title: Protection claim parsers accept inherited wire fields
items.recommendation: Read only own properties at the wire boundary. For required fields, require Object.hasOwn(obj, key) before validating the value. For optional protection_claim, return undefined unless Object.hasOwn(obj, 'protection_claim') is true. Consider rejecting non-plain objects or normalising via own enumerable entries if this API is intended to accept only parsed JSON objects.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hostile-input tests assert that a JSON.parse-created __proto__ own data property does not satisfy schema_version, but they do not construct an object with inherited schema_version/worktree_state/surfaces or an inherited protection_claim field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parseProtectionClaim(Object.create(validClaimFields)) throws /schema_version/ or a JSON-object/prototype error, and parseOptionalProtectionClaimFromValidateWrite(Object.create({ protection_claim: validClaim })) returns undefined or rejects the non-wire envelope.
items.minimumFixScope: Update protection_claim/types.ts property access for schema_version, worktree_state, surfaces, identifier, state, and protection_claim to require own wire fields, then add hostile-input tests for inherited required and optional fields.

items.title: Reliability records are never evicted for expired or recovered identities
items.recommendation: Evict records once they no longer carry useful state, for example delete the identity on recordSuccess after clearing quarantine, and delete expired quarantine records in isQuarantined instead of retaining an empty record. If telemetry needs historical identities, add an explicit bounded retention policy.
items.reproduction: Create a single ReliabilityBudget and call recordFailure with many unique identities. Then either call recordSuccess for each identity or advance the injected clock beyond cooldown and call isQuarantined. snapshot() will still return one record per identity with empty failures and quarantinedUntil 0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing tests verify clone safety and behaviour for one or two fixed identities, but they do not assert that recovered or expired identities are removed from the ledger or that snapshot excludes inert records.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with an injected clock that records failures for several unique identities, lets cooldown expire or records success, and asserts snapshot() is empty or bounded according to the intended retention contract.
items.minimumFixScope: Update ReliabilityBudget eviction behaviour in budget.ts and add focused unit coverage in budget.test.ts.

items.title: In-flight connects can resurrect or duplicate live transports
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise/generation and make connect() return that promise while state is connecting or reconnecting. In openTransport(), after await transport.connect(), check that the attempt generation is still current and state is not closed before assigning this.transport; otherwise close the just-opened transport and return or throw an anvil-driver-closed error. close() should invalidate pending connection attempts so late completions cannot publish a transport.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() returns a manually resolved promise. Call const p = client.connect(); then await client.close(); then resolve the transport connect promise and await p. The current implementation ends with state effectively connected and a live transport installed after close. Similarly, Promise.all([client.connect(), client.connect()]) before either connect resolves constructs two transports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: driver-client.test.ts covers sequential connect idempotence after connection is already established and close() after a completed connect, but it has no delayed transport test for concurrent connect() calls or close() while connect() is in flight.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fake transport recipe with a deferred connect promise. Assert that two concurrent connect() calls create only one transport, and assert that close() before resolving the deferred connect leaves the client closed, closes the late transport, and makes subsequent request() reject with anvil-driver-closed.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient connection lifecycle state in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.ts plus targeted unit tests in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: Rejected DriverClientError instances do not expose the documented error discriminator
items.recommendation: Add a readonly `error: DriverErrorCode` property to `DriverClientError` set from `payload.error`, keep `code` as a compatibility alias if needed, and update direct rejection tests to assert both the documented `error` discriminator and `toJSON()` shape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The request and integration tests assert `err.code`, while `validateMidEdit` tests exercise the `toJSON()` path. None assert that the rejected `DriverClientError` itself has the documented `error` field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a driver error unit or request rejection test that catches a timeout/drop error and expects `(err as DriverClientError & DriverError).error` to equal the stable discriminator, with `retriable` and `message` still present.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `DriverClientError` in `src/errors.ts` and the direct rejection assertions in the driver-client/integration tests.

items.title: Kindling parity test fixture is not a valid Diagnostic shape
items.recommendation: Change the Kindling fixture to use the canonical diagnostic shape (`schema_version`, `summary`, and the other exported `Diagnostic` fields), or deliberately type it as `DiagnosticLike` if the test is only meant to cover the narrowed input contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostic shape is tested separately, but the Kindling parity tests do not reuse that canonical shape, so they do not prove that real driver diagnostics flow through the observation builder unchanged.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Keep `makeDiag` typed as `Diagnostic` with `schema_version` and `summary`, then add one assertion that a full canonical Diagnostic can be passed to `fromMidEditResponse` without casts.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/kindling/types.test.ts` fixture construction and, if the intended contract is narrower, its return type.

items.title: Spoof-block scan results are dropped as clean diagnostics
items.recommendation: Use the canonical AnvilScanBufferResult type for the RPC response and extend ValidateMidEditResult to surface spoof_block explicitly, either as a dedicated degraded/spoof-block kind or a field that consumers must handle. Do not cache spoof-block responses as ordinary diagnostics unless the cached result preserves the same degraded signal.
items.reproduction: Have the fake transport respond to validateMidEdit with a JSON-RPC result containing version: 1, diagnostics: [], truncated: false, and spoof_block: { reason: 'degraded:spoofed-attribution', fenced_worktree: '/repo' }. The current API returns kind: 'diagnostics' with an empty diagnostic list and no spoof-block data.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: validate-mid-edit.test.ts covers forwarding ANVIL_AGENT_TAG and truncated diagnostics, while protocol/types.test.ts only constructs a scan_buffer result without spoof_block. No test exercises a successful scan_buffer result containing spoof_block.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateMidEdit test where the daemon returns a result with spoof_block and no diagnostics; assert the public result carries a non-pass spoof-block/degraded outcome and does not collapse to kind: 'diagnostics' with an empty list.
items.minimumFixScope: midedit result typing and mapping plus one fake-transport regression test; likely also update README/API docs if the public result union changes.

items.title: close() can be undone by an in-flight connect()
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise and a connection generation/abort flag. close() should mark the generation closed and close any transport that resolves after shutdown before openTransport publishes it. connect() should return the existing in-flight promise while state is connecting rather than starting another transport attempt.
items.reproduction: Use a test transport whose connect() promise is manually controlled. Call const pending = client.connect(); await client.close(); then resolve the transport connect promise and await pending. The client transitions to connected after close(), and request()/notify() can use the newly installed transport.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing idempotency test only calls connect() sequentially after the first call has reached connected, and close() idempotency is tested only after a completed connect. There is no delayed-connect or concurrent-connect lifecycle test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fake transport with deferred connect resolution. Assert close() during connect leaves the client closed after the deferred connect resolves, closes the transport, emits no connected event after close, and rejects subsequent request() with anvil-driver-closed. Add a second test that two concurrent connect() calls share one transport attempt.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient lifecycle state only, plus fake transport support for deferred connect in tests.

items.title: Associated Kindling test still builds an obsolete Diagnostic fixture
items.recommendation: Update the Kindling test fixture to use `schema_version` and `summary`, preferably with a `satisfies Diagnostic` or another type-checked fixture pattern, so the test exercises the current public diagnostic contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test's runtime assertions only depend on `severity` and `source.rule_id`; they do not assert that the diagnostic fixture itself matches the canonical diagnostic shape exported by the owned diagnostics module.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change `makeDiag` to construct a canonical `Diagnostic` and add a type-checked fixture assertion so stale `schema`/`message` keys cannot remain in associated tests.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts

items.title: Diagnostic location type omits nullable wire values
items.recommendation: Model nullable optional location fields as `number | null` where the wire contract permits null, and update the parity tests to cover explicit null as well as omitted fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostic parity test only asserts that path-only locations can omit `line` and `column`; it never constructs or round-trips a payload where those fields are explicitly null.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostic parity test that parses or declares a `Diagnostic` with `location: { file: 'README.md', line: null, column: null }` and confirms JSON round-trip behaviour matches the Rust/spec contract.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/diagnostics/types.ts and .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/diagnostics/types.test.ts

items.title: DiagnosticLocation cannot represent null line anchors allowed by the documented wire contract
items.recommendation: Change the nullable anchor fields to `number | null` while keeping them optional, for example `line?: number | null`, and apply the same policy consistently to column and span end fields if the Rust/spec contract permits null there.
items.reproduction: In strict TypeScript, `const loc: DiagnosticLocation = { file: 'README.md', line: null }` is rejected even though the documented envelope contract allows that wire shape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostic parity test only covers omitted `line` and `column`; it never constructs or round-trips a diagnostic with explicit null location anchors.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostic parity test that constructs `{ location: { file: 'README.md', line: null, column: null } }` as a `Diagnostic`, JSON round-trips it, and asserts the null fields are preserved when present.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `DiagnosticLocation` nullability and add the null-anchor parity test in the diagnostics test file.

items.title: Associated Kindling test fixture uses stale diagnostic field names while pretending to be a Diagnostic
items.recommendation: Either make the fixture a real `Diagnostic` by using `schema_version` and `summary`, or type it as the narrower `DiagnosticLike` if the test intentionally exercises only the Kindling builder's minimal input contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions do not inspect the diagnostic wire fields, and the package test script runs Vitest rather than a spec typecheck that would reject the annotated object literal.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: After correcting the fixture, add a compile-time or runtime assertion that Kindling tests use the canonical diagnostic field names when they import `Diagnostic`.
items.minimumFixScope: Fix `makeDiag` in the Kindling test to match `Diagnostic`, or change the helper return type to the builder's narrower accepted input type.

items.title: Standalone daemon command is not covered by process-level tests
items.recommendation: Add a small process-level integration test for the binary contract, at minimum covering help/usage and invalid invocation. If feasible on Unix, also spawn `anvil-intercept start` under an isolated temporary HOME/state directory, send SIGTERM, and assert it exits successfully.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Both included test files construct `IpcListener` or service harnesses in-process, bypassing `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs` entirely.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Use `CARGO_BIN_EXE_anvil-intercept` or an `assert_cmd` equivalent to verify `anvil-intercept --help`, `anvil-intercept` without a subcommand, and a Unix-only `anvil-intercept start` smoke test that terminates via SIGTERM in a temporary environment.
items.minimumFixScope: Add binary-level integration coverage for `crates/anvil-intercept/src/main.rs`; no daemon library changes are required.

items.title: Non-finite budget options can disable or corrupt quarantine behavior
items.recommendation: Validate numeric options with Number.isFinite, keep threshold/window strictly positive, keep cooldown non-negative, and consider requiring failureThreshold to be an integer.
items.reproduction: new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: Number.NaN }).recordFailure('driver-A') never crosses the threshold; new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: 1, cooldownMs: Number.NaN }) makes isQuarantined('driver-A') stay true after the first failure.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included validation test only asserts zero and negative rejection, so NaN and Infinity remain untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add constructor tests asserting RangeError for NaN and Infinity across failureThreshold, windowMs, and cooldownMs, plus a behavioral test showing finite options still quarantine normally.
items.minimumFixScope: ReliabilityBudget constructor validation and budget option tests.

items.title: Test-only clearForTests method is exported as part of the public class API
items.recommendation: Remove clearForTests if unused, make tests create fresh ReliabilityBudget instances, or mark it internal and ensure declaration generation strips internal members.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not use clearForTests and do not assert the generated public API shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API surface test or declaration snapshot that ensures ReliabilityBudget does not expose test-only mutators.
items.minimumFixScope: ReliabilityBudget public method surface and API declaration tests.

items.title: Reliability records are never evicted for expired or successful identities
items.recommendation: Prune records whose failures are empty and quarantinedUntil is 0, and delete records after trimming leaves no in-window failures. Consider running a small prune pass on recordFailure, isQuarantined, and snapshot.
items.reproduction: Call recordFailure with many unique identities, advance now beyond windowMs, and call isQuarantined or recordSuccess; snapshot still contains a record for every identity unless clearForTests is called.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests verify per-identity behavior and cloned snapshots, but they never assert that expired or successful identities are removed from the ledger.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that records failures for multiple identities, advances beyond the window or records success, then asserts snapshot omits inactive identities.
items.minimumFixScope: ReliabilityBudget record lifecycle management and corresponding unit tests.

items.title: DiagnosticLocation excludes documented null wire anchors
items.recommendation: Either widen nullable wire fields to `number | null` (`line`, `column`, `end_line`, `end_column` if they share the Rust Option contract), or add a parser that accepts null and normalises it before exposing the typed object. Keep the comments, types, and tests aligned.
items.reproduction: Create a Diagnostic with location: { file: 'README.md', line: null }; TypeScript rejects it even though the documented wire contract allows null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The diagnostics parity test asserts omitted line/column for path-only locations but never exercises JSON with explicit null anchors.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a diagnostic JSON round-trip fixture with `location: { file: 'README.md', line: null, column: null }` and assert the TS API accepts or normalises it according to the chosen contract.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/diagnostics/types.ts` and `src/diagnostics/types.test.ts`.

items.title: Documented known-mode branch does not type-check for Mode
items.recommendation: Export a small `isKnownMode(mode: Mode): mode is KnownMode` helper, or type the catalogue/search surface so the documented predicate works without casts while preserving the literal `KnownMode` union.
items.reproduction: In a strict TS consumer, `function f(mode: Mode) { return KNOWN_MODES.includes(mode); }` is rejected because `Mode` is not assignable to `KnownMode`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test only checks the catalogue values; it does not compile or exercise the documented `includes(mode)` usage against a `Mode` value.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an exported `isKnownMode` helper with Vitest coverage for a known value and an unknown future string; keep the helper in compiled source so package typecheck covers the signature.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/diagnostics/types.ts`, `src/diagnostics/index.ts`, and the diagnostics type tests if a helper is added.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC responses are classified as valid responses
items.recommendation: Validate the full response shape before returning kind: 'response': id must be string, number, or null; success responses must have result and no error; error responses must have error as a non-null object with numeric code and string message; responses with both result and error should be rejected as unknown or surfaced as a protocol error.
items.reproduction: Call classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: 'boom' }); it returns kind: 'response'. If the caller then handles it as JsonRpcErrorResponse, errorFromResponse receives a string error value and reads response.error.message/code as undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current classifyIncoming tests cover valid success/error responses and a few non-response shapes, but they do not include malformed error objects, invalid ids, or result/error mutual-exclusion cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming tests asserting kind === 'unknown' for { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: 'boom' }, { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, result: true }, and { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', result: true, error: { code: -32603, message: 'x' } }.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts plus jsonrpc.test.ts

items.title: Concurrent connect calls can open and orphan multiple transports
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise and return it while state is connecting or reconnecting, or otherwise serialize openTransport() so only one transport can be active. Clear the shared promise on success or failure and ensure superseded transports are closed.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() promise is externally controlled, call Promise.all([client.connect(), client.connect()]) before resolving either connect, then resolve both. The factory will have created two transports, while close() can only close the final this.transport reference.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included idempotency test only calls connect() after the first connect() has fully resolved, so it exercises state === 'connected' but not the state === 'connecting' race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a manually resolved fake transport connect() that starts two connect() calls concurrently and asserts only one transport instance is created and closed.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient.connect/openTransport connection lifecycle plus one focused unit test in driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: parseAgentTag accepts inherited prototype properties as wire fields
items.recommendation: Require AgentTag fields to be own properties before validating their primitive types, preferably via the same asObject/Object.hasOwn style used by the protection-claim parser. Reject arrays explicitly if the contract is JSON object envelopes only.
items.reproduction: const inherited = Object.create({ driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'agent-1', pid_starttime: 1 }); parseAgentTag(inherited) currently returns a tag even though Object.hasOwn(inherited, 'driver_id') is false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: src/session/types.test.ts asserts missing direct fields and array rejection, but it never constructs an object whose required fields are inherited from its prototype.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a hostile-input test asserting parseAgentTag(Object.create({ driver_id: 'anvil-run', claimed_agent_id: 'agent-1', pid_starttime: 1 })) throws on driver_id or AgentTag shape.
items.minimumFixScope: Update parseAgentTag field extraction and add one hostile-input test in src/session/types.test.ts.

items.title: Expired dedup entries persist for keys that are never touched again
items.recommendation: Prune expired dedup entries independently of same-key lookups, for example by scanning the cache on submit before/after writing, keeping an expiry timestamp and bounded LRU, or scheduling cleanup with the injected scheduler. Keep the cache size bounded if this API can receive arbitrary URI keys.
items.reproduction: Create a MidEditDebouncer with a fake scheduler and dedupWindowMs: 1000; submit and resolve many unique keys; advance the scheduler past the window; submit a new different key. The old keys remain in the private dedupCache because the only expiry delete path checks the currently submitted key.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expiry test reuses the same key after advancing past the window, so it exercises the per-key lazy delete path. It does not cover many unique keys expiring without being submitted again, nor does it assert cache size or retention after the window.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a debouncer test that submits several unique keys, advances past dedupWindowMs, submits another unique key, and asserts stale entries are pruned via an exposed test-only cache size, telemetry snapshot, or observable pruning hook.
items.minimumFixScope: MidEditDebouncer dedup cache eviction logic and a focused unit test in debouncer.test.ts.

items.title: Same-key requests stop coalescing once the debounce timer fires
items.recommendation: Track active in-flight dispatch state per key in addition to timer-pending state. When a later submit supersedes the same key, mark the earlier active generation stale and settle its public promise as `coalesced` or ignore its eventual dispatcher result so it cannot seed the cache or return stale diagnostics.
items.reproduction: Use an injected scheduler with debounceMs=0 and a dispatcher whose promise is manually deferred. Submit key `file:///x` with content A, advance the scheduler so dispatch A starts but does not resolve, then submit the same key with content B and advance again. Both dispatch functions are invoked and both returned promises can resolve as `fresh` instead of the earlier one being coalesced or suppressed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing coalescing tests only submit replacements before the debounce timer fires and assert `dispatchCount` is still zero before the final advance. They never hold a dispatcher unresolved after the timer has fired and then submit a same-key replacement.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `MidEditDebouncer` test where the first same-key dispatch starts and remains unresolved, a second same-key submit occurs, and the assertions prove only the current generation can produce a `fresh` result or seed the dedup cache.
items.minimumFixScope: `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.ts` plus focused tests in `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.test.ts`; add a `validateMidEdit` regression only if the public envelope semantics change.

items.title: Expired dedup entries for inactive keys are retained indefinitely

evidence.symbol: cache expires after the dedup window

items.recommendation: Prune expired cache entries opportunistically on submit, add a bounded cache size, or schedule expiry cleanup using the injected scheduler. Keep cleanup deterministic under fake schedulers so tests can verify it.
items.reproduction: Submit successful requests for many distinct keys, advance the scheduler past `dedupWindowMs`, and do not submit those keys again. The entries remain in `dedupCache` until `clearDedupCache()` or process teardown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current expiry test advances past the window and re-submits the same key, which exercises the only implemented delete path. It does not create multiple inactive keys or assert that stale entries for untouched keys are removed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test-only cache size accessor or observable pruning hook, submit several unique keys, advance beyond the dedup window, trigger cleanup with a different key, and assert expired inactive keys no longer remain cached.
items.minimumFixScope: `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.ts` and `packages/anvil-driver-client/src/midedit/debouncer.test.ts`.

items.title: Protocol method catalogue is stale against the authoritative Rust contract
items.recommendation: Add TS constants, exported parameter/result types where applicable, and include the three missing methods in `ALL_ANVIL_METHODS`; update protocol and barrel exports plus tests to count-pin and assert parity with the full Rust set.
items.reproduction: Compare `.claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts` with `crates/anvil-intercept-proto/src/protocol.rs`: Rust's `ALL_ANVIL_METHODS` includes nine entries, while this TS catalogue includes six.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The protocol test asserts the six existing entries are unique and present, but it has no count pin or fixture for the authoritative Rust method set, so omitted Rust methods are invisible.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `types.test.ts` to assert the full nine-entry method list, including `ANVIL_VALIDATE_PATHS`, `ANVIL_WORKSPACE_STATUS`, and `ANVIL_REQUEST_FULL_SCAN`, with a count assertion matching Rust's authoritative list.
items.minimumFixScope: `src/protocol/types.ts`, `src/protocol/index.ts`, package-level protocol exports if present, and `src/protocol/types.test.ts`.

items.title: scan_buffer spoof-block wire contract is not enforced by the TS API
items.recommendation: Model `AnvilScanBufferResult` as a union separating the normal diagnostics result from the spoof-block result, make `AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock.reason` the literal type `'degraded:spoofed-attribution'`, and re-export `AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock` from the protocol barrel.
items.reproduction: A TS consumer can currently type-check an invalid value like `{ version: 1, diagnostics: [diag], truncated: false, spoof_block: { reason: 'typo', fenced_worktree: '/tmp/wt' } } satisfies AnvilScanBufferResult`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `types.test.ts` only constructs a normal scan result with `truncated`; it never covers `spoof_block`, the fixed reason string, exportability of the spoof-block type, or the diagnostics/spoof-block exclusivity invariant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add typecheck-backed tests for a valid spoof-block response and `// @ts-expect-error` cases for a non-literal reason and for combining non-empty diagnostics with `spoof_block`; add an import test for `type AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock` from `./index.js`.
items.minimumFixScope: `src/protocol/types.ts`, `src/protocol/index.ts`, package-level public exports if they re-export protocol types, and `src/protocol/types.test.ts`.

items.title: In-flight connect can resurrect a closed client and leak duplicate transports
items.recommendation: Track a connection generation or in-flight promise. connect() should return the existing in-flight promise while connecting/reconnecting, and openTransport() should verify that its generation is still current and state is not closed before installing the transport. If the generation is stale or the client closed, close the newly connected transport immediately and leave state closed.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() returns a deferred promise. Call const p = client.connect(); then await client.close(); then resolve the deferred connect. The awaited connect path will run lines 484-488 and the supposedly closed client becomes connected again. Similarly, call connect() twice before resolving either deferred connect and observe two factory instances with only the last assigned to this.transport.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing connect idempotency test awaits the first connect before calling connect() again, and close idempotency only closes after a completed connect. There is no test for close() racing an unresolved connect() or two concurrent connect() calls.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add deferred fake-transport tests that start connect() without resolving it, call close(), resolve connect(), then assert request() rejects with anvil-driver-closed and the transport was closed; add a second test that two concurrent connect() calls create only one transport instance.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient lifecycle state handling in connect(), openTransport(), and close(), plus focused concurrency tests in driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: Malformed response-like frames are promoted to typed JSON-RPC responses
items.recommendation: Make classifyIncoming validate the JSON-RPC response contract before returning kind:'response': id must be string, finite number, or null; exactly one of result/error should be present; error must be an object with finite numeric code and string message. Return unknown or a framing/protocol error for malformed response-like frames.
items.reproduction: classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: 'boom' }) returns kind:'response' even though it is not a valid JsonRpcErrorResponse.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The classifyIncoming tests cover valid success and error responses plus a few non-response shapes, but they do not include malformed response-like frames with bad error payloads, invalid ids, or both result and error.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming tests for error:'boom', id:{}, and frames containing both result and error, asserting they are not classified as valid responses.
items.minimumFixScope: jsonrpc.ts classifyIncoming validation plus malformed-response unit tests.

items.title: Partial-line accumulation copies the full pending buffer on every chunk
items.recommendation: Store pending data as a list of chunks with a running byte count, enforce the cap against the count, and concatenate/decode once when a newline arrives. Alternatively use a growable buffer strategy that does not recopy the full line for every small append.
items.reproduction: Construct an NdjsonFramer with the default cap and call push(Uint8Array.of(0x41)) repeatedly without a newline until the cap is reached; each call after the first copies all previously accumulated bytes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover a partial frame split across three chunks and oversize recovery, but they do not cover highly fragmented input or assert linear allocation/copy behaviour under adversarial chunking.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a small cap and many one-byte chunks that verifies only one oversize error and, if practical, exercises a chunk-list implementation without repeated full-buffer concatenation.
items.minimumFixScope: ndjson.ts pending-buffer representation and the partial/oversize tests around fragmented chunks.

items.title: Non-finite numeric request IDs serialize to null
items.recommendation: Validate request ids in buildRequest, accepting only strings or finite numbers, and consider requiring safe integers if daemon correlation assumes integer numeric ids. Throw a DriverClientError or RangeError before encoding invalid ids.
items.reproduction: encodeNdjsonLine(buildRequest(Number.NaN, 'session.list')) produces {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"method":"session.list"}\n.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The request tests cover a string id and a finite numeric id only; no test exercises NaN, Infinity, or other JSON-unsafe numeric ids.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a jsonrpc test asserting buildRequest(Number.NaN, 'session.list') and buildRequest(Infinity, 'session.list') throw, and that finite ids still encode unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: jsonrpc.ts buildRequest id validation plus targeted jsonrpc unit tests.

items.title: Protection-claim parsers accept inherited fields as valid wire data
items.recommendation: Require required wire fields to be own properties before reading them, for example via a small getOwnField(obj, key, owner) helper using Object.hasOwn. Apply the same rule to protection_claim on the validate_write envelope and to SurfaceClaim.identifier/state. Preserve the current allowance for unknown extra own fields.
items.reproduction: const proto = { schema_version: 'anvil.protection-claim.v1', worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] }; parseProtectionClaim(Object.create(proto)); // currently returns a valid claim instead of rejecting missing own fields
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The missing-field tests use plain object literals with unpolluted prototypes, so inherited fallback is absent. The hostile-input test checks JSON.parse('__proto__') as an own data property, but it never exercises an object whose prototype actually supplies schema_version or protection_claim.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({ schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] })) throws for schema_version, parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({ identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating' })) throws for identifier, and parseOptionalProtectionClaimFromValidateWrite(Object.create({ protection_claim: validClaim })) returns undefined or rejects rather than parsing inherited data.
items.minimumFixScope: Field-access helper and parser call sites in src/protection_claim/types.ts, plus hostile-input regression tests in src/protection_claim/types.test.ts.

items.title: close() can be undone by an in-flight connect()
items.recommendation: Make connection attempts generation-scoped or abortable. After transport.connect() resolves, verify the attempt is still current and the client is not closed; if it is stale or closed, close the just-opened transport and reject with anvil-driver-closed. Consider storing a connecting promise so concurrent connect()/close() transitions are serialized through the same lifecycle path.
items.reproduction: Use a test transport whose connect() returns a deferred promise. Call const p = client.connect(); await client.close(); resolve the deferred connect; await p; then client.request(...) no longer fails with anvil-driver-closed because state was reset to connected.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included close() guard test only closes after await client.connect() has completed, so it never exercises close() while openTransport() is suspended inside transport.connect().
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient guard test with a deferred fake transport connect: start connect(), call close() before resolving the deferred connect, resolve connect, assert the connect promise rejects or the new transport is closed, and assert a subsequent request rejects with anvil-driver-closed.
items.minimumFixScope: DriverClient connection lifecycle handling plus a focused delayed-connect regression test in driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: TypeScript protocol mirror has drifted from the Rust wire contract
items.recommendation: Refresh the TS protocol mirror against Rust `protocol.rs` and the current `scan_buffer` request contract: add/export the missing method constants and include them in `ALL_ANVIL_METHODS`, add `session_id?: string` to `AnvilScanBufferParams`, and update public barrel exports as needed.
items.reproduction: Use `ALL_ANVIL_METHODS` from the TS package and compare it to Rust `anvil_intercept_proto::protocol::ALL_ANVIL_METHODS`: the TS list is missing the later Rust constants. Also try to type `const p: AnvilScanBufferParams = { path: 'x.ts', text: '', version: 1, mode: 'midEdit', session_id: 'sess-a' }`; the daemon accepts that wire field, but the TS type rejects it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `protocol/types.test.ts` pins the stale six-method subset rather than checking parity with the current Rust catalogue, and it only tests the scan_buffer result truncation flag, not the request params shape or session_id binding field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add TS parity tests that assert the new method constants are exported and included in `ALL_ANVIL_METHODS`, plus a compile-time/runtime shape test constructing `AnvilScanBufferParams` with `session_id` and verifying JSON preserves `session_id`.
items.minimumFixScope: `.claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts`, `.claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/index.ts`, the package root export surface, and `src/protocol/types.test.ts`.

items.title: CLI build can fail because importHelpers is enabled without a tslib runtime dependency
items.recommendation: Either remove importHelpers from the admin-cli tsconfig, or add tslib as a production dependency for @eddacraft/admin-cli.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise source files through Vitest/tsx-style TypeScript execution, not the compiled dist package installed with only production dependencies.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test that runs the built dist/index.js from a production-install style environment, or a manifest check asserting tslib is present whenever importHelpers is enabled.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/admin-cli/tsconfig.json or apps/admin-cli/package.json

items.title: Kindling parity test uses a non-canonical Diagnostic fixture
items.recommendation: Either make the fixture a real canonical Diagnostic using schema_version and summary, preferably with a compile-checked satisfies Diagnostic assertion, or change the helper to return DiagnosticLike if the test intentionally only exercises the minimal shape.
items.reproduction: Run the linked Kindling tests; they pass because the builder only consumes severity and source.rule_id, despite the fixture not matching the canonical Diagnostic shape shown in diagnostics/types.test.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Kindling tests assert only the generated observation fields, not that their diagnostic fixture serialises as the canonical Diagnostic wire shape. The separate diagnostics parity test covers Diagnostic itself but does not protect this Kindling fixture from drifting.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update makeDiag to construct a canonical Diagnostic and add an assertion that JSON.stringify/parse preserves schema_version and summary before passing it into fromMidEditResponse.
items.minimumFixScope: Change only .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-001/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts unless the intended contract is DiagnosticLike-only, in which case adjust the test helper type there.

items.title: scan_buffer spoof-block invariants are not encoded in the public type
items.recommendation: Model the result as a union that separates the diagnostic response from the spoof-block response, and make `AnvilScanBufferSpoofBlock.reason` the literal type `'degraded:spoofed-attribution'`. Export the spoof-block type through the same barrel if it is part of the public protocol surface.
items.reproduction: A TS consumer can currently type-check an invalid result such as `{ version: 1, diagnostics: [diag], truncated: false, spoof_block: { reason: 'typo', fenced_worktree: '/tmp/wt' } } satisfies AnvilScanBufferResult`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The protocol test only constructs the non-spoof diagnostic result and checks `truncated`; it never constructs a valid spoof-block result or asserts that invalid spoof-block combinations fail type-checking.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add typecheck-backed cases for a valid spoof-block response plus `// @ts-expect-error` cases for a non-literal reason and for combining spoof_block with diagnostics.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts and the protocol barrel/tests if the spoof-block type is public.

items.title: parseAgentTag accepts inherited fields as required wire keys
items.recommendation: Treat AgentTag envelopes as plain JSON records: reject arrays, and require Object.hasOwn(obj, 'driver_id'), Object.hasOwn(obj, 'claimed_agent_id'), and Object.hasOwn(obj, 'pid_starttime') before reading the values. Preserve dropping unknown own fields for forward compatibility.
items.reproduction: Object.assign(Object.prototype,{driver_id:'anvil-run',claimed_agent_id:'forged',pid_starttime:1}); try { parseAgentTag({}) } finally { delete Object.prototype.driver_id; delete Object.prototype.claimed_agent_id; delete Object.prototype.pid_starttime; } returns a tag instead of throwing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The session tests check null, primitive, missing-field, and numeric validation cases, but no test supplies inherited required properties or a prototype-polluted object. The array test only passes because Array.prototype is clean in that test process.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a hostile-input test where required fields exist only on the prototype and assert parseAgentTag throws for the first missing own field; optionally also assert arrays are rejected before field lookup.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/session/types.test.ts

items.title: Transport send can report success before the write succeeds
items.recommendation: Track both resolve and reject for pending writes. Resolve send() from the write callback only after a successful write, reject from the callback on errors, and reject all pending write promises from fireClose for peer/error drops instead of resolving them. If local close intentionally flushes, keep that case explicit and covered by tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix transport test sends a small happy-path message and waits for an echo; it does not force write() to return false, destroy the peer during a pending write, or assert that write callback errors reject the send promise. The Windows tests cover ownership-gate failures only and never exercise send/backpressure behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add transport tests that pause or destroy the peer while a large write is pending, assert the awaiting send() rejects with anvil-daemon-transport-drop, and assert no pending send resolves after onClose('peer') or onClose('error'). Mirror the write-settlement behaviour for the Windows transport with a mocked net.Socket or a platform-specific pipe test.
items.minimumFixScope: Update send/fireClose write-promise handling in both UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport, then add focused regression tests for write callback errors, backpressure, and peer/error close while a send is pending.

items.title: Pending backpressure sends resolve successfully when the connection closes
items.recommendation: Track both resolve and reject for pending writes. On drain, resolve pending writes; on close/error before drain, reject them with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop`. Consider resolving via the write callback on successful flush instead of a separate resolve-only drain queue.
items.reproduction: Use a slow or paused daemon connection so socket.write() returns false, call send(), then close the peer before drain. The pending send promise resolves from fireClose() rather than rejecting with a transport-drop error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing transport tests send a tiny message and wait for a normal echo, so socket.write() is expected to return true. They do not simulate backpressure, peer drop during a pending write, or assertion of send promise outcome under close.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with a paused server or mocked net.Socket where write() returns false and no drain fires before close/error; assert the pending send() rejects with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the writePromises storage and close/error handling in both UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport; add shared backpressure regression tests.

items.title: Windows named-pipe transport does not verify current-user ownership
items.recommendation: Implement a real Windows ownership gate before resolving connect(): derive the current user SID and require the canonical suffix to match it, and inspect the named pipe security descriptor/ACL via a native helper or other trusted boundary. If that cannot ship yet, make Windows named-pipe connection unsupported rather than accepting same-prefix pipes as owner-validated.
items.reproduction: Create or point DriverClientOptions.pipeName at a user-controlled pipe named \\.\pipe\anvil-intercept-S-1-5-21-anything. validateWindowsPipeName accepts it as long as the suffix has no whitespace or slashes, and connect() proceeds without proving ownership.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.test.ts only exercises string-shape validation and explicitly avoids opening or inspecting any pipe, so it cannot catch ACL or current-SID bypasses.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Windows-only test or native-helper-backed unit test that rejects a same-prefix pipe whose suffix is not the current user SID or whose ACL grants another user access, and accepts only the daemon's current-user-owned pipe.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.ts plus Windows transport tests; possibly add a small native/PowerShell ACL inspection helper if pure Node cannot read the pipe security descriptor.

items.title: Peer/error close does not put transports into the closed state before later sends
items.recommendation: In fireClose(), set `this.closed = true` and `this.socket = null` before invoking handlers and before draining any waiters. Ensure subsequent send() calls always reject with `anvil-daemon-transport-drop` after any close cause.
items.reproduction: Connect to a server that accepts and then closes the socket. After the transport's onClose('peer') fires, call transport.send('x'). The send path does not hit the closed guard because fireClose() left closed false and socket non-null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Unix happy-path test only calls send before close and asserts that some close event fired. There is no test that calls send after peer close or error close. The Windows tests do not exercise transport lifecycle at all.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add lifecycle tests for both concrete transports (or a shared fake socket harness) that trigger peer close/error, wait for onClose, then assert send() rejects with DriverClientError code `anvil-daemon-transport-drop` without waiting for drain.
items.minimumFixScope: Update fireClose() in packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/unix.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/transport/windows.ts, then add lifecycle regression coverage.

items.title: Successful responses can be treated as success when the body read fails
items.recommendation: Do not swallow response.text() failures. Catch them separately and throw an AdminError with an appropriate non-success exit code, status, and a message that preserves the read failure cause.
items.reproduction: Use a fetchImpl that returns a Response-like object with status 200 and text() rejecting. Calling client.get('/x') without a schema resolves to undefined instead of throwing an AdminError.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/client.test.ts covers network fetch rejection, 4xx/5xx bodies, invalid JSON, empty schema responses, and schema validation, but it does not cover response.text() rejection after fetch has resolved.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a client test with a fetchImpl returning an object whose status is 200 and whose text() rejects, then assert client.get('/x') rejects with AdminError instead of resolving undefined.
items.minimumFixScope: Update AdminClient.request body-read handling and add one focused regression test in apps/admin-cli/src/__tests__/client.test.ts.

items.title: Dedup cache ignores ANVIL_AGENT_TAG when skipping daemon validation
items.recommendation: Include the effective env_agent_tag in the dedup/debounce identity for validateMidEdit, or make the debouncer cache key include all wire parameters that can influence daemon validation.
items.reproduction: Call validateMidEdit once with ANVIL_AGENT_TAG='tag-a' and content 'A' so the response is cached. Within dedupWindowMs, set ANVIL_AGENT_TAG='tag-b' and call validateMidEdit with the same uri/content. The second call returns kind:'cached' and sends no frame containing env_agent_tag:'tag-b'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tag tests assert forwarding/omission only on fresh dispatches, and the dedup test asserts cached behaviour without changing ANVIL_AGENT_TAG between calls.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateMidEdit test that changes ANVIL_AGENT_TAG between identical-content calls and asserts the second call dispatches again with the new env_agent_tag, or otherwise proves the cache key distinguishes the tag.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust createMidEditValidator's debouncer key construction and add a focused test for tag-sensitive dedup.

items.title: Expired dedup entries are retained forever for keys that are not revisited
items.recommendation: Prune expired entries opportunistically across the map, add a bounded cache size, or schedule per-entry expiry cleanup when writing cache entries.
items.reproduction: Submit successful requests for many distinct keys, wait past dedupWindowMs, and never submit those keys again. The dedupCache entries remain until clearDedupCache or process teardown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cache expiry test advances time and then submits the same key, which exercises same-key deletion but not stale entries for keys that are never revisited.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test using a manual scheduler that dispatches many distinct keys, advances beyond dedupWindowMs, triggers a later submit for another key, and asserts expired unrelated entries are pruned or bounded via an observable test hook.
items.minimumFixScope: Update MidEditDebouncer cache eviction strategy and add a regression test for distinct-key stale-entry retention.

items.title: Mid-edit cache and coalescing ignore workspaceRoot, so multi-root clients can reuse diagnostics across workspaces
items.recommendation: Include workspaceRoot in the debounce/dedup key, for example `${workspaceRoot}\0${uri}`, or explicitly constrain DriverClient.validateMidEdit to a single workspace root and enforce that at construction. If the daemon needs workspace context to produce correct results, include workspaceRoot in the request shape once the protocol allows it.
items.reproduction: Call validateMidEdit({ workspaceRoot: '/repo-a', uri: 'src/index.ts', content: 'same', debounceMs: 0 }) and let the fake daemon return diagnostic id 'repo-a'. Then call validateMidEdit({ workspaceRoot: '/repo-b', uri: 'src/index.ts', content: 'same', debounceMs: 0 }) within dedupWindowMs. The second call will hit the uri-only dedup key and return the first diagnostic as cached instead of dispatching for /repo-b.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing validateMidEdit cache test repeats the same uri/content within the same workspaceRoot, so it proves same-document dedup but does not cover two workspace roots with the same relative uri.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateMidEdit test with two calls using the same uri/content but different workspaceRoot values and a fake daemon that returns root-specific diagnostics; assert the second call dispatches fresh and returns the second root's result.
items.minimumFixScope: createMidEditValidator key construction and its dedup/coalescing tests.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC error responses can escape the structured error path and leave requests unsettled
items.recommendation: Validate JSON-RPC response shape before returning kind='response', or harden handleResponse/errorFromResponse so malformed error responses are converted into a non-retriable structured DriverClientError or emitted as a framing_error without throwing. Do not delete and clear the pending request before the code path can guarantee it will settle the promise.
items.reproduction: Use the fake transport to respond to a request with JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: env.id, error: null }) + '\n'. The request path enters handleResponse, clears the pending timeout, then errorFromResponse throws a TypeError instead of settling the request with a structured error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The JSON-RPC tests cover a valid error response and a few unknown non-response shapes, but they do not cover malformed error members such as null, missing message, or non-numeric code, and the DriverClient tests do not drive malformed daemon responses through the pending-request path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient test where the fake daemon sends a malformed error response for a live request; assert the request rejects with a structured DriverClientError or that the malformed frame is surfaced via framing_error, and assert no uncaught exception or hanging promise occurs.
items.minimumFixScope: framing/jsonrpc.ts response validation plus the DriverClient.handleResponse settlement ordering for malformed responses.

items.title: Parsers accept inherited fields as trusted wire data
items.recommendation: Read required fields through an own-property helper, for example check Object.hasOwn(obj, key) before accessing obj[key], and apply it consistently for ProtectionClaim and SurfaceClaim fields. Keep unknown extra own fields ignored for forward compatibility.
items.reproduction: const polluted = Object.create({ schema_version: 'anvil.protection-claim.v1', worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] }); parseProtectionClaim(polluted) returns a valid claim instead of rejecting the envelope as missing required own fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The hostile-input test only covers JSON.parse('{"__proto__": ...}'), where __proto__ is an own data property and required fields are not inherited. It does not cover objects whose prototype actually contains the required fields, nor global prototype pollution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that parseProtectionClaim(Object.create({ schema_version: PROTECTION_CLAIM_SCHEMA_VERSION, worktree_state: 'full', surfaces: [] })) and parseSurfaceClaim(Object.create({ identifier: 'mcp', state: 'participating' })) both throw missing-field TypeErrors.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protection_claim/types.ts plus protection_claim parser hostile-input tests

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC responses are classified as valid responses
items.recommendation: Validate the response envelope before returning kind=response: allow only string/number/null ids, reject frames with both result and error, require error to be an object with finite numeric code and string message, and treat malformed response-shaped frames as unknown or a framing/protocol error.
items.reproduction: classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, error: 'boom' }) returns kind=response even though the payload is not a JsonRpcErrorResponse.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: jsonrpc.test.ts covers happy-path success and error responses plus non-object and missing-jsonrpc cases, but it never supplies malformed response-shaped payloads with invalid id, invalid error shape, or both result and error.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming tests for invalid ids, error as a primitive, missing error.message/code, and frames containing both result and error; assert they are not classified as valid responses.
items.minimumFixScope: Update classifyIncoming validation and add malformed-response tests in jsonrpc.test.ts.

items.title: Incremental NDJSON buffering can become quadratic under fragmented input
items.recommendation: Store pending chunks in an array with a tracked total byte count and concatenate once on flush, or maintain a growable buffer that expands geometrically. Keep the existing maxLineBytes check against the tracked total.
items.reproduction: Create NdjsonFramer with the default cap and call push(Buffer.from('A')) repeatedly without a newline until the cap is reached; each call after the first copies the full accumulated pending buffer.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: ndjson.test.ts checks oversize recovery and no-newline cap behaviour with large chunks, but it does not exercise highly fragmented input near the cap or assert copy/allocation behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fragmented-input test that feeds many small chunks up to a valid newline and verifies the frame is emitted; if practical, instrument or benchmark to guard against per-byte concatenation regressions.
items.minimumFixScope: Refactor NdjsonFramer pending storage in ndjson.ts and preserve existing rejection semantics in ndjson.test.ts.

items.title: JSON auth-required success envelope is written to stderr
items.recommendation: When the coerced exit code is EXIT_OK and a JSON auth envelope is produced, write the envelope to stdout. Keep stderr for non-zero error envelopes if that is the established error-stream contract, or consistently document and test any exception.
items.reproduction: Run the CLI with an isolated HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME and no credentials, for example `anvil --json start` or `anvil check --all --format json`, in a non-interactive environment. The process exits 0 for action commands, stdout is empty, and the JSON authRequired envelope is on stderr.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The unit test checks the pure auth_required_response return value but never spawns the CLI to assert stdout vs stderr. The included JSON integration tests parse stdout for successful JSON payloads and do not exercise unauthenticated gated JSON commands.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated action command with `--json` or `--format json` under an empty credential home, without ANVIL_DEV, and asserts exit 0, stdout parses as `{state:"authRequired"...}`, and stderr does not contain the sole JSON envelope.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the pre-dispatch auth branch in crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs to emit informational JSON success envelopes on stdout and add a subprocess regression test.

items.title: Air-gapped status verification can still attempt network refresh before running the local probe
items.recommendation: Special-case local/offline status verification before silent refresh, or add an auth-check mode that refuses/returns auth-required without refresh for commands documented as air-gapped. Then run the air-gapped harness without `ANVIL_DEV` against an isolated expired credential fixture with a refresh token.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included air-gapped test bypasses auth with `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so it verifies the status command body but not the global auth layer that runs first in production.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `air_gapped.rs` with a test that seeds isolated expired credentials containing a refresh token, runs `anvil --no-tui --json status --verify` through the network-blocked harness without `ANVIL_DEV`, and asserts the process does not attempt or hang on network refresh.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth pre-dispatch policy for documented local/offline commands plus the air-gapped credential fixture test.

items.title: `start --verify` is not included in the local-probe auth bypass
items.recommendation: Extend skips_auth_for_local_probe to include `Commands::Start(args) if args.verify` and, if `start --json` also implies read-only verify, include that mode as well. Keep full `anvil start` auth-gated if that is still intended.
items.reproduction: Create an isolated credential home containing expired credentials with a refreshToken, block network, and run `anvil --no-tui --json start --verify` without ANVIL_DEV. The pre-dispatch auth path is eligible to attempt silent refresh before the local verify command can run.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied air-gapped expired-credential test covers only `status --verify --json`. Other tests use ANVIL_DEV or command paths that bypass the local auth pre-check, so they do not catch a refresh attempt before `start --verify` dispatch.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an air-gapped test mirroring `anvil_status_verify_json_skips_auth_refresh_with_expired_credentials` for `start --verify --json`, asserting stdout is the local activation diagnostic and neither stream contains auth/network/update markers.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the local-probe skip predicate in crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs and add a focused air-gapped subprocess regression for start verify.

items.title: Pre-dispatch JSON auth responses are written to stderr despite successful exit
items.recommendation: When `auth_required_response` returns an informational EXIT_OK JSON envelope, print it to stdout. Keep true error envelopes on stderr if that is the project convention, but do not put successful JSON-mode output solely on stderr.
items.reproduction: Run a gated action command with no credentials, for example with an empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) anvil --json status`. The process exits 0, stdout is empty, and the JSON authRequired envelope is on stderr.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The main.rs unit tests assert the returned envelope shape and exit code but never exercise process stdout/stderr routing. The included JSON integration tests cover stdout parsing for doctor, edda, gate, and status --verify; none covers a gated action command stopped by pre-dispatch auth.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs `anvil --json status` or another gated action command with isolated empty credentials, asserts exit code 0, asserts stdout parses as `{ "state": "authRequired", ... }`, and asserts stderr does not contain the only JSON payload.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the pre-dispatch auth-required print path in crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs and add one CLI integration test for the JSON stdout contract.

items.title: JSON-mode auth failures emit human text before the JSON error envelope
items.recommendation: Thread JSON/machine-output mode into auth evaluation, or make `check_auth` return a structured auth error without printing when `global.json` is set, leaving `main` as the single JSON error renderer.
items.reproduction: env -u ANVIL_DEV -u ANVIL_LICENSE ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) cargo run -p eddacraft-anvil -- --json status 2>err; cat err
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included JSON-mode tests either use unauthenticated commands or set `ANVIL_DEV=1`, so they never exercise the gated auth-failure path in JSON mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs a gated command such as `anvil --json status` with isolated empty credentials and `ANVIL_NO_PROMPT=1`, then asserts stderr is exactly one parseable JSON object and contains no human auth guidance.
items.minimumFixScope: `crates/anvil-cli/src/main.rs` auth error rendering plus one auth-failure JSON integration test.

items.title: Kindling test fixture no longer matches the Diagnostic contract
items.recommendation: Update makeDiag to use the current Diagnostic wire fields, replacing schema with schema_version and message with summary, or change the helper return type to DiagnosticLike if the test intentionally exercises only the minimal Kindling input shape.
items.reproduction: pnpm --dir .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/packages/anvil-driver-client exec tsc --noEmit --ignoreConfig --moduleResolution NodeNext --module NodeNext --target ES2022 --strict --skipLibCheck src/kindling/types.test.ts
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The package Vitest command transpiles tests without TypeScript semantic checking, and the package tsconfig excludes **/*.test.ts from the normal typecheck path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test-typecheck target, or include a minimal tsc/vitest typecheck invocation for src/**/*.test.ts in CI so typed test fixtures cannot drift from exported contracts.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the makeDiag fixture in src/kindling/types.test.ts to match Diagnostic or narrow its declared return type to DiagnosticLike.

items.title: AgentTag parser accepts unsafe integer pid_starttime values
items.recommendation: Reject unsafe integers in parseAgentTag with Number.isSafeInteger(pidStarttime), and apply the same guard in makeAgentTag or document that makeAgentTag requires a safe integer and enforce it at call sites.
items.reproduction: parseAgentTag({ driver_id: 'd', claimed_agent_id: 'a', pid_starttime: 9007199254740992 }) returns an AgentTag even though that value is outside JS safe-integer precision; adjacent wire values around this range cannot be represented reliably after JSON parsing.
