items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing pid_starttime validation tests cover fractional, negative, Infinity, and NaN values, but do not exercise integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a session/types.test.ts case asserting parseAgentTag rejects pid_starttime: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1 and, if makeAgentTag is guarded, that makeAgentTag rejects the same value.
items.minimumFixScope: Update session/types.ts validation for pid_starttime and extend session/types.test.ts with an unsafe-integer case.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC error responses can throw through the transport callback
items.recommendation: Validate response envelopes before classifying them as JsonRpcResponse, or harden handleResponse/errorFromResponse to reject malformed response payloads with an `anvil-daemon-invalid-request`/framing error event without throwing. Require error.code to be a number and error.message to be a string before treating it as a JSON-RPC error response.
items.reproduction: Connect a DriverClient with a fake transport, issue request('session.list'), then push an inbound line `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"req-1","error":null}\n`. The pending request is deleted and errorFromResponse throws while handling the inbound frame.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The JSON-RPC tests cover valid success/error responses and a few unknown frames, but they do not include malformed response-shaped frames where `error` is null, a primitive, or missing required fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a jsonrpc/client test that sends `{ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 'req-1', error: null }` for an in-flight request and asserts the client does not throw synchronously; it should settle the request with a structured error or emit a non-fatal error event.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/framing/jsonrpc.ts and the corresponding jsonrpc/driver-client tests.

items.title: Concurrent connect calls can open and leak multiple transports
items.recommendation: Track an in-flight connect promise and return it when state is 'connecting' or 'reconnecting', or otherwise serialise connect attempts. Ensure a failed in-flight connect clears the stored promise and a successful one leaves exactly one owned transport.
items.reproduction: Use a transportFactory whose connect() promise is externally controlled. Call `const a = client.connect(); const b = client.connect();` before resolving either connect promise. The factory is invoked twice and two transports can become connected, but only the last assignment is closed by client.close().
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current connect idempotency test awaits the first connect before calling the second, so it never exercises the 'connecting' state race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a DriverClient test with a deferred fake transport connect; invoke connect() twice concurrently, resolve the deferred connect, assert the factory was called once and both promises resolve, then close and assert the one transport closed.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.ts and packages/anvil-driver-client/src/client/driver-client.test.ts.

items.title: Benchmark reports can be overwritten by runs started in the same second
items.recommendation: Make report paths collision-resistant and non-clobbering, for example by including subsecond time plus process id or a UUID, and create the file with exclusive-create semantics so collisions fail instead of overwriting.
items.reproduction: Start two `cargo run -p anvil-bench --release -- graph_memory` processes from the same directory within the same Unix second; both compute the same `bench-results/stress-<timestamp>.json` output path and one report is lost.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the CLI entrypoint or concurrent/same-second output path generation; existing report serialization tests do not validate collision behaviour for main.rs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test around output path generation or a refactored `run` helper that forces the same timestamp for two runs and asserts the second run does not overwrite the first report.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the output filename/open mode in `crates/anvil-bench/src/main.rs`; factor path generation into a small testable helper if needed.

items.title: Kindling test fixture uses the wrong Diagnostic wire shape
items.recommendation: Update `makeDiag` in `src/kindling/types.test.ts` to use the canonical Diagnostic fixture shape: `schema_version`, `summary`, and the same required fields used by the diagnostics/protocol tests. Prefer importing and using `DIAGNOSTIC_SCHEMA_VERSION` to avoid another hard-coded spelling.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --dir .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client typecheck` with the Kindling test included by tsconfig; TypeScript should reject the excess `schema`/`message` properties and missing canonical fields on the `Diagnostic` return value.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Kindling tests assert only the observation fields derived from `severity` and `source.rule_id`; they never assert that the diagnostic fixture itself matches the canonical Diagnostic wire contract. Vitest transpilation can also let this survive unless the package typecheck includes test files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an assertion in the Kindling test fixture path that JSON.stringify(makeDiag(...)) contains `schema_version` and `summary` and does not contain `schema` or `message`, or share the canonical diagnostic fixture helper from diagnostics tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only fixture correction in `.claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/kindling/types.test.ts`.

items.title: NDJSON encoder silently emits non-JSON for unsupported top-level values
items.recommendation: Store the JSON.stringify result, check for undefined, and throw a typed/range error for values that cannot be represented as a top-level JSON value. Keep existing exceptions for BigInt or circular structures, or wrap them consistently if the package has an established error type for encoding failures.
items.reproduction: encodeNdjsonLine(undefined) returns 'undefined\n' instead of throwing or returning a valid JSON line.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current encoder test only covers a plain object and checks newline/single-line shape; it does not cover unsupported top-level values.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an encodeNdjsonLine test asserting undefined, function, and symbol inputs throw instead of producing 'undefined\n'.
items.minimumFixScope: Update encodeNdjsonLine in jsonrpc.ts and add negative encoder tests in jsonrpc.test.ts.

items.title: Malformed JSON-RPC responses are accepted as typed responses
items.recommendation: Validate response shape before returning kind: 'response': id must be string, number, or null; exactly one of result or error should be present; error must be an object with numeric code and string message. Return unknown for malformed response-like payloads, or add a distinct invalid-response classification if callers need telemetry.
items.reproduction: classifyIncoming({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, error: 'boom' }) returns kind: 'response' even though the id and error members are not valid JSON-RPC response fields.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover well-formed success and error responses plus malformed notification-like frames, but they do not exercise malformed response-like frames with invalid id/error/result combinations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add classifyIncoming cases for { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: {}, result: true }, { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, result: true, error: {...} }, and { jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, error: 'boom' } and assert they do not return kind: 'response'.
items.minimumFixScope: Update classifyIncoming response validation in jsonrpc.ts and extend jsonrpc.test.ts for malformed response-like payloads.

items.title: Backpressured sends resolve successfully when the transport drops before drain
items.recommendation: Track pending writes as resolve/reject pairs, reject them on peer/error close, and only resolve the specific write when its write callback or a correctly associated flush signal succeeds. Apply the same fix to UnixSocketTransport and WindowsNamedPipeTransport.
items.reproduction: Use a server that accepts a connection but stops reading, send a large chunk until socket.write returns false, then destroy the server-side socket before drain. The pending send promise resolves via fireClose instead of rejecting with anvil-daemon-transport-drop.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included transport tests cover ownership checks, a small happy-path send, and connection rejection, but they never force write backpressure or close/error before drain.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add Unix and Windows/fake-socket transport tests where write() returns false and the socket emits error/close before drain; assert the pending send rejects with anvil-daemon-transport-drop and no request is treated as sent.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the shared write/backpressure handling pattern in src/transport/unix.ts and src/transport/windows.ts, plus focused transport tests for pending-write rejection.

items.title: Windows SID resolver can be redirected through mutable SystemRoot
items.recommendation: Do not derive the identity helper path from process.env.SystemRoot. Use a non-environment trusted system-directory lookup, a fixed trusted system path with appropriate validation, or preferably a native/current-token SID API. Keep failures closed.
items.reproduction: Launch the client with SystemRoot set to an attacker-controlled absolute directory containing System32\whoami.exe that prints a chosen CSV SID, then call resolveCurrentUserSid or connect to a matching explicit pipeName. The gate accepts the spoofed SID output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The Windows tests validate SID parsing and injected SID providers, but they do not exercise resolveCurrentUserSid with a hostile SystemRoot or assert that the default provider cannot be redirected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Windows-only or mocked execFileSync test that sets SystemRoot to an arbitrary absolute temp path and asserts resolveCurrentUserSid does not execute that path and fails closed or uses the trusted system directory.
items.minimumFixScope: Change resolveCurrentUserSid path selection in src/transport/windows.ts and add a focused regression around hostile SystemRoot handling.

items.title: `spoof_block` result shape cannot express the documented mutually exclusive error case

evidence.symbol: DRVR-002 method parameter shapes / scan_buffer result carries the truncation flag

items.recommendation: Model `AnvilScanBufferResult` as a discriminated or union type, for example a normal result with `diagnostics` and no `spoof_block`, plus a spoof-block result with `spoof_block` and no `diagnostics`; alternatively update the comment and Rust parity evidence if the actual wire contract is `diagnostics: []` plus `spoof_block`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The protocol test only constructs the normal non-spoof result and asserts `truncated`; it never constructs or serialises a spoof-block result, and it does not assert the diagnostics/spoof-block exclusivity invariant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add protocol tests that compile and round-trip the canonical spoof-block response shape, asserting either that `diagnostics` is absent when `spoof_block` is present or, if the intended wire shape is an empty array, that both Rust and TS explicitly pin that representation.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-001/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.ts and .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-001/packages/anvil-driver-client/src/protocol/types.test.ts

items.title: Same-key requests can run concurrently once the first debounce timer fires
items.recommendation: Keep per-key in-flight state until the dispatcher settles, or introduce an explicit in-flight supersession policy. If true cancellation is not possible, at minimum prevent overlapping dispatches for the same key and resolve/mark stale outcomes consistently with the public contract.
items.reproduction: Use an injected scheduler with debounceMs 0 and a dispatcher whose promise is externally controlled. Submit key 'a' and advance time so dispatch starts but does not resolve. Submit key 'a' again with different content and advance time. Both dispatchers will run concurrently instead of the first being coalesced or otherwise superseded.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only cover replacement before the debounce timer fires and distinct-key parallelism. They do not hold a same-key dispatcher unresolved while submitting a later request.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MidEditDebouncer test that starts a same-key dispatch, blocks it on a deferred promise, submits newer content for the same key, and asserts the older request is coalesced or otherwise cannot race as an active same-key dispatch.
items.minimumFixScope: MidEditDebouncer per-key pending/in-flight lifecycle plus a focused unit test.

items.title: Non-finite numeric options can silently disable or corrupt quarantine decisions
items.recommendation: Validate all numeric options with Number.isFinite, and require failureThreshold to be a positive safe integer. Consider also validating now() output before using it for window and cooldown arithmetic.
items.reproduction: new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: Number.NaN }).recordFailure('driver-A') never returns true; new ReliabilityBudget({ failureThreshold: 1, cooldownMs: Number.NaN }).recordFailure('driver-A') followed by isQuarantined('driver-A') remains true with a NaN deadline.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing bad-options test only covers 0 and negative values, not NaN, Infinity, fractional thresholds, or invalid clock output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add constructor tests for NaN and Infinity across failureThreshold, windowMs, and cooldownMs; add a behaviour test showing invalid options cannot disable quarantine or create a NaN quarantinedUntil.
items.minimumFixScope: ReliabilityBudget constructor validation plus focused tests in budget.test.ts.

items.title: Root tsconfig lists files that TypeScript does not actually check
items.recommendation: Either remove the inert entries and keep this as a narrow TypeScript-only config check, or add a dedicated config-check tsconfig that enables `allowJs`/`checkJs` for eslint.config.mjs and uses the current E2E path, likely `apps/e2e/**/*` if root-level E2E files are still intended.
items.reproduction: `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --explainFiles | rg 'eslint\.config|jest\.config|e2e|vitest\.config|playwright\.config'` only reports vitest.config.ts and playwright.config.ts as matched by tsconfig.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this config. The existing root TypeScript invocation succeeds because TypeScript silently ignores the unmatched or unsupported include entries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small validation script or test that runs `tsc --explainFiles` for the root config and asserts every intentional include entry is either matched or explicitly documented as inert.
items.minimumFixScope: Update tsconfig.json include entries and, if JS config checking is intended, the compilerOptions needed to make eslint.config.mjs part of the checked program.

items.title: Root Vitest discovery can miss package __tests__ directories outside src
items.recommendation: Add an include pattern for package __tests__ directories that are not necessarily under src, or align the documented convention and config so there is a single discoverable test location. Consider disabling passWithNoTests at the root config if CI expects the root suite to find tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or config smoke tests are included that assert the Vitest include globs discover expected repository test locations.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a small config-level test or CI smoke check that uses Vitest's resolved config/glob matching to assert packages/example/__tests__/sample.test.ts and packages/example/src/sample.test.ts are both discoverable.
items.minimumFixScope: vitest.config.ts include globs and, if retained intentionally, an explicit documented rationale for passWithNoTests.

items.title: Node type definitions exceed the supported runtime contract
items.recommendation: Either align @types/node to the minimum supported Node major, or raise the engines.node minimum if Node 25 APIs are intentionally allowed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise adapter parsing and serialization behavior; they do not verify package metadata consistency or run the suite against the minimum supported Node runtime.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata validation test that checks the @types/node major does not exceed the minimum engines.node major, or add CI coverage on Node 22 that catches runtime use of newer Node APIs.
items.minimumFixScope: package.json devDependency or engines.node

items.title: Release package root and manifest entrypoints disagree
items.recommendation: Choose one package shape and make the release config match it: either publish from the project root with files pointing at dist, or generate/copy a dist/package.json whose main/types/exports point at ./index.js and other dist-relative files.
items.reproduction: Build the package and publish or pack from packages/adapters/dist as configured by nx-release-publish; the package root will not contain files at ./dist/index.js relative to that root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites exercise source imports and adapter behaviour, but there is no packaging smoke test that builds and resolves the package from the configured release packageRoot.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging test that runs the adapters build, verifies packages/adapters/dist/package.json exists with dist-relative entrypoints, then imports the packed package entrypoint with Node.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/package.json and packages/adapters/project.json, plus the build/release step that creates the published manifest.

items.title: Documented subpath imports are blocked by package exports
items.recommendation: Add explicit subpath exports with both import and types targets for the supported public barrels, or change the README to require root imports only. Also correct the SpecKit example to use an actually exported symbol, such as SpecKitFormatAdapter or createSpecKitAdapter.
items.reproduction: Install or link the package with its current exports map, then run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad')"`; Node will reject the subpath because it is not present in package.json exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests import implementation files with relative paths under src, so they never exercise Node package exports or the README's public import examples.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-resolution test that builds the library and dynamically imports the documented root, speckit, bmad, generic, and utility entrypoints through the package name.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/package.json exports and README examples; possibly add top-level utility barrels if @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/utils is intended to be public.

items.title: BMAD conversion errors are collected then discarded
items.recommendation: Propagate conversion diagnostics into ParseResult. Either make bmadToAPS return a structured object containing plan, errors, and warnings, or throw when conversion errors are present so BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns createParseError. Non-fatal omissions should at least be returned as warnings.
items.reproduction: Parse an otherwise valid agent YAML whose agent.metadata.id is '../outside.md'. safePath throws, bmadToAPS records INVALID_PATH, but parse still returns success with the invalid agent change omitted.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The BMAD tests cover valid v6 YAML fixtures and generic parse success, but they do not assert that invalid paths or failed item conversions are reported through ParseResult.errors or ParseResult.warnings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parse test with an invalid agent metadata id or invalid module directory path and assert parse fails with INVALID_PATH, or succeeds only with an explicit warning and no silent omission.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/bmad/format-adapter.ts, plus BMAD parse tests for invalid conversion diagnostics.

items.title: Website build can pass with TypeScript errors and no local typecheck target
items.recommendation: Add a website-scoped typecheck script/target, for example `tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`, wire it into the project target graph and CI/build pipeline, and remove `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` unless there is a documented temporary migration gate.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, and the declared package/project commands do not include a typecheck step that would fail independently of `next build`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI validation target for `website:typecheck` and a small fixture or pipeline assertion proving type errors fail the website validation even when Next build is configured separately.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the website package manifest and Nx project targets, then adjust `next.config.mjs` or CI so type errors cannot be released.

items.title: Security page publishes a placeholder PGP fingerprint as if it were usable
items.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with the real PGP fingerprint and ensure the referenced `.well-known/pgp-key.txt` content is published and matches it, or remove the PGP section until the key is available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No content tests were supplied, and there is no assertion that public security copy is free of placeholder values or that referenced security resources exist.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a content smoke test for `/security` that rejects placeholder fingerprint text and, if the key endpoint is part of this app, verifies the displayed fingerprint matches the served public key metadata.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the security page content and, if applicable, add the matching public key asset or route.

items.title: Vercel ignore command path arguments are shell-parsed without validation
items.recommendation: Validate `rootDirectory` and every `extraWatchPaths` entry with a conservative path allowlist, or centralise shell argument rendering with correct POSIX single-quote escaping and use it for all dynamic arguments.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover shell metacharacter rejection for `productionBranch` and assert generated command fragments only for safe literal paths such as `apps/web`; they do not instantiate `VercelApp` with paths containing spaces, quotes, or metacharacters.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that reject or safely quote `rootDirectory: 'apps/web; touch /tmp/pwned'` and an `extraWatchPaths` entry containing a single quote or whitespace.
items.minimumFixScope: `infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts` command construction plus focused tests in `infra/src/__tests__/vercel-app.test.ts`.

items.title: Beta-tier token without a subject can pass the docs gate
items.recommendation: Fail closed before calling resolveFlag when sessionSubject is null, undefined, or empty. Either make sessionSubject required in DocsEvaluationInput or return the disabled/default resolution unless both a non-empty subject and an allowed tier are present.
items.reproduction: Call evaluateDocsAccess({ accountTier: 'beta', sessionSubject: null }); the context uses targetingKey 'anon-visitor' and still includes the canonical beta account tier, allowing the flag targeting to match enabled.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the included file has no regression coverage for missing or empty sessionSubject with a privileged accountTier.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add docs-site tests for evaluateDocsAccess({ accountTier: 'beta', sessionSubject: null }) and evaluateDocsAccess({ accountTier: 'beta', sessionSubject: '' }) asserting variant 'disabled' and reason 'default'.
items.minimumFixScope: Update evaluateDocsAccess in apps/docs-site/lib/feature-flags.ts to require a non-empty sessionSubject before adding audience/accountTier to the context or before resolving the entitlement flag.

items.title: License verification accepts tokens without an expiry
items.recommendation: After jwtVerify, require payload.exp to be a finite number, or pass requiredClaims: ['exp'] if supported by the jose version in use. Consider also requiring issuer/audience if BAuth has a stable token contract.
items.reproduction: Sign an ES256 JWT with the configured LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY's corresponding private key, omit setExpirationTime/exp, and pass it to verifyLicense; jwtVerify succeeds and verifyLicense returns { valid: true }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing jwt tests cover valid tokens with exp, expired tokens, garbled tokens, and wrong-key tokens, but no token that is correctly signed and missing exp.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that signs a token with the test private key without setExpirationTime and expects verifyLicense(token).valid to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-shell/lib/jwt.ts and apps/docs-shell/lib/jwt.test.ts

items.title: Array undefined values make object hashing throw instead of producing a stable JSON-equivalent hash
items.recommendation: Handle undefined array elements explicitly, most likely by serializing them as null to match JSON.stringify array semantics, or document and validate that undefined is forbidden anywhere inside arrays.
items.reproduction: canonicalizeJSON([1, undefined, 3]) throws TypeError; JSON.stringify([1, undefined, 3]) returns "[1,null,3]".
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover top-level undefined and undefined object properties, but no test covers undefined values or sparse holes inside arrays.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a canonicalizeJSON test asserting canonicalizeJSON([1, undefined, 3]) is '[1,null,3]' and, if sparse arrays are supported, canonicalizeJSON([, 2]) is '[null,2]'.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the Array.isArray branch in packages/anvil/core/src/crypto/hash.ts and add focused tests in packages/anvil/core/src/crypto/hash.test.ts.

items.title: Index templates emit a non-APS module status
items.recommendation: Replace Draft with a valid initial APS status, most likely Proposed, or show the allowed status set as a placeholder that cannot be mistaken for a real status value.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The index tests only assert that a Status field exists; they do not assert that the generated value is one of the allowed APS lifecycle statuses.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add assertions for standard and full index templates that module status values match the allowed APS status set and do not contain `**Status:** Draft`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the standard and full index template status lines plus the generator tests to validate APS-compatible status values.

items.title: Package metadata requires Node 20.0 despite Docusaurus 3.10 requiring newer Node
items.recommendation: Raise `engines.node` to match the Docusaurus 3.10.1 minimum supported Node version used by this workspace, and align CI/runtime documentation with that floor.
items.reproduction: Use Node 20.0.x and run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-site build`; the package manifest permits the runtime even though the Docusaurus dependency line may reject or fail on it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or CI matrix evidence are included that exercise the package on the lower bound declared by `engines.node`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package metadata check or CI engine assertion that verifies `engines.node` is at least the strictest minimum required by direct runtime/build dependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/docs-site/package.json` `engines.node` to the correct Docusaurus-compatible lower bound.

items.title: Typecheck script uses a tsconfig documented as editor-only
items.recommendation: Either make the comment truthful by describing the file as the package typecheck configuration, or change the script to point at the actual intended build/typecheck config. Keep the script and tsconfig header aligned.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-site typecheck`; TypeScript will use `apps/docs-site/tsconfig.json` despite the file claiming it is not used in compilation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the mismatch is between package metadata and configuration documentation rather than runtime behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a workspace validation check that runs the docs-site `typecheck` script and fails if the referenced tsconfig is missing or intentionally marked editor-only.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/docs-site/tsconfig.json` comment or `apps/docs-site/package.json` `typecheck` script so they describe the same contract.

items.title: SpecKit format serialize/reparse loses change paths
items.recommendation: Make serialization and parsing agree on the path contract. For example, emit backticked paths in headings or a `Path: \`...\`` line, and add parser support for the serialized heading format.
items.reproduction: Create an APS plan with a file_create change at src/auth/controller.ts, call SpecKitFormatAdapter.serialize, then parse the returned content. The parsed change description is 'Create src/auth/controller.ts', but its path becomes src/generated-file.ts instead of src/auth/controller.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test is for the generic parser and does not exercise SpecKit serialize/parse round trips or path preservation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitFormatAdapter round-trip test that serializes a plan containing file_create, file_update, and file_delete paths, reparses it, and asserts the paths are unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: Update SpecKitFormatAdapter.serialize or SpecKitParser path extraction, plus a focused round-trip test.

items.title: SpecKit input limit counts UTF-16 code units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for the SpecKit size guard, matching the generic parser behaviour.
items.reproduction: Call new SpecKitParser().parseSpecMarkdown('😀'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)); the UTF-8 byte length is over 2 MiB while string.length is below MAX_INPUT_SIZE, so the size guard does not throw.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test covers parseGeneric only; no included SpecKitParser test asserts byte-length enforcement for multibyte content.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitParser parseSpecMarkdown test mirroring the generic multibyte case and expecting /maximum size/ when UTF-8 bytes exceed MAX_INPUT_SIZE.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the guard in packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts and add a focused parser test.

items.title: Empty-change exports produce NaN task progress
items.recommendation: Handle the zero-task case explicitly, for example by reporting 0% progress when tasks.length is 0 or omitting the progress percentage for empty task lists.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with a valid APS plan whose proposed_changes is []. The conversion succeeds and the returned tasksContent contains `Progress: NaN%`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included linked test is unrelated to SpecKit export, and no included export test covers an APS plan with zero proposed changes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitExportAdapter test for an empty proposed_changes plan asserting conversion succeeds without NaN in tasksContent.
items.minimumFixScope: Update generateTasksMarkdown's progress calculation and add a focused export test.

items.title: Create stdout does not match the documented JSON contract
items.recommendation: Either change stdout to JSON.stringify({ id, hashed_key: hashedKey }) or update the documented contract and any consumers to use hashedKey consistently. Given the database column and comment use hashed_key, preserving snake_case is the lower-surprise fix.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests that execute create and assert the stdout JSON shape.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a create-path test with a stubbed pg client that asserts stdout includes id and hashed_key, not an undocumented field name.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key-manage.mjs stdout shape or its documented contract, plus a focused regression test.

items.title: Remote database URLs can accidentally disable TLS
items.recommendation: Parse DATABASE_URL with the URL API and disable SSL only when the parsed hostname is exactly localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1. Treat malformed URLs as configuration errors rather than falling back silently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the context package manifest does not define a focused test target for URL classification or pg client options.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add unit coverage around the connection option builder with localhost, 127.0.0.1, localhost.example.com, and URLs where localhost appears outside the hostname.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key-manage.mjs connection option construction, preferably factored into a small testable helper.

items.title: Concurrent creates can leave multiple active keys for one actor
items.recommendation: Make the invariant database-enforced or lock-backed. For example, add a partial unique index on active actor rows, use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT against that constraint, or take a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by actor_email before the SELECT/INSERT sequence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the inspected package manifest has no test script for exercising this database mutation path or concurrent create behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that runs two create operations concurrently for the same ACTOR_EMAIL with different BEARER_HEX values and asserts only one active admin_keys row remains while the loser fails cleanly.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key-manage.mjs create transaction logic plus the admin_keys schema or migration that owns the active actor uniqueness invariant.

items.title: File discovery drops default roadmap files and under-ranks exact basenames
items.recommendation: Score against basename for exact filename checks and add confidence handling for every default pattern, including roadmap. Keep the prefilter and confidence scorer in one shared pattern table if possible so defaults cannot drift.
items.reproduction: Create a searched directory containing roadmap.md. discoverPlanningFiles({ rootPath }) prefilters it because roadmap is in DEFAULT_PATTERNS, but calculateFileConfidence returns below 40 and the file is omitted. Create plan.md and proposal-design.md in the same directory and plan.md will not get the intended exact-match boost because the full path is compared with 'plan.md'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file only exercises AdapterRegistry behavior; there are no file-discovery tests for default patterns, exact filename ranking, or findBestPlanningFile ordering.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add file-discovery tests with a temp directory proving roadmap.md is returned by default and plan.md outranks a less canonical planning document when confidence ties or recency would otherwise obscure the issue.
items.minimumFixScope: Update calculateFileConfidence in file-discovery.ts and add focused tests for default pattern coverage and basename exact matching.

items.title: Exported registry singleton becomes stale after resetInstance
items.recommendation: Avoid exporting a mutable singleton object that can be invalidated. Export a getRegistry() accessor, remove resetInstance from production API, or make resetInstance clear the current instance instead of replacing it when the exported constant is part of the public API.
items.reproduction: Import { registry, AdapterRegistry }, register an adapter on registry, call AdapterRegistry.resetInstance(), then compare registry with AdapterRegistry.getInstance(); registry still contains the old object and any old registrations, while getInstance() returns a new instance.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The reset test only compares two values returned from AdapterRegistry.getInstance(); it never imports or asserts behavior for the exported registry constant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that imports the exported registry, registers an adapter, calls resetInstance, and asserts the documented reset semantics for both registry access paths, or removes one access path from the contract.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust registry.ts singleton export/reset semantics and add one regression test covering the exported registry binding.

items.title: Pattern utilities treat literal strings and reusable regexes incorrectly
items.recommendation: For string patterns, count literal occurrences without constructing a RegExp, or escape the string before building one. For RegExp patterns, preserve caller flags while ensuring global counting, and reset lastIndex before or after test operations in matchesPatterns.
items.reproduction: countOccurrences('a.b.c', '.') returns 5 instead of 2; countOccurrences('ABC', /abc/i) returns 0 because the i flag is dropped; calling matchesPatterns('foo', [/foo/g]) twice with the same regex can return 1 and then 0 because lastIndex was advanced.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included registry tests import createDetection from utils but do not cover matchesPatterns or countOccurrences with literal metacharacters, regex flags, or global regex reuse.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add utils tests for literal string counting with '.', invalid regex characters as strings, case-insensitive RegExp counting, and repeated matchesPatterns calls with a global RegExp.
items.minimumFixScope: Update matchesPatterns and countOccurrences in utils.ts and add focused utility tests.

items.title: canExport advertises APS markdown export even though serialize always fails
items.recommendation: Either implement APSPlan-to-APS-markdown serialization, or override canExport to return false for APS markdown until serialize is implemented.
items.reproduction: Instantiate APSMarkdownAdapter, observe canExport('aps') returns true, then call serialize(plan) and receive success: false with NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests assert canExport returns true, but they never call serialize to verify that advertised export capability works.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that, for every format where canExport returns true, serialize(samplePlan) succeeds or the adapter explicitly reports canExport false until export is supported.
items.minimumFixScope: APSMarkdownAdapter export capability and serialize implementation.

items.title: Detected APS index files are not parsed into any module representation
items.recommendation: Define the import contract for APS index files: either parse module entries into an explicit APSPlan representation, return a clear unsupported-index parse error, or stop detecting index files as importable APS markdown.
items.reproduction: Use the index fixture shape from the detection test and call parse after detect returns true; there is no owned code that maps the Modules entries into APSPlan output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only assert that index files are detected; they do not parse a Modules-only index or assert preservation of module paths and metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parse test for a Modules-section index file that asserts either preserved module metadata in the result or a deliberate unsupported-index parse error after detection.
items.minimumFixScope: APSMarkdownAdapter detection/parse contract for Modules-section index files.

items.title: Public crate docs still describe shipped validation as deferred
items.recommendation: Update the `lib.rs` scope/out-of-scope section to reflect that hard-pinned validation is now part of the crate, and explicitly state that `parse_str`/`parse_file` parse only while callers that load operator config should call `validate_hard_pinned_classes` after parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover parse and validation behavior, but they do not verify that the public crate documentation matches the shipped API surface.
items.minimumFixScope: Documentation-only change in `crates/anvil-config/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: Testing entrypoint is not exported from the package
items.recommendation: Add ./testing, and likely ./testing/* if direct subpath imports are intended, to package.json exports with dist type and import targets.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked provenance-chain test imports files relatively from src and never performs a package subpath import against package.json exports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level export smoke test or publint/API test that imports @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/testing from the built package.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json

items.title: require-mock-cleanup can be bypassed by comments or strings
items.recommendation: Inspect the AST inside the afterEach callback and set hasRestoreInAfterEach only for an actual CallExpression whose callee is vi.restoreAllMocks.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: require-mock-cleanup.test.ts includes an invalid afterEach using vi.clearAllMocks with a descriptive comment, but it does not include a comment or string containing the exact vi.restoreAllMocks() call text.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add invalid cases where afterEach contains only // vi.restoreAllMocks() and where it contains the string 'vi.restoreAllMocks()'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-mock-cleanup.ts plus its rule test file

items.title: require-cwd-restoration accepts a restore before the cwd-changing call
items.recommendation: Track the sequence of chdir calls and only count a saved-cwd chdir as restoration for a preceding non-restoration chdir, or require the saved-cwd chdir to occur after a cwd-changing call in the same relevant scope.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: require-cwd-restoration.test.ts has valid cases where restoration follows the cwd change and invalid cases with no saved-cwd restoration, but no invalid case where saved-cwd chdir happens before the dirty chdir.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an invalid RuleTester case with const originalCwd = process.cwd(); process.chdir(originalCwd); process.chdir('/tmp/test'); expecting missingRestoration.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/require-cwd-restoration.ts plus its rule test file

items.title: recommended config enables no-any-in-tests for every file
items.recommendation: Either scope the recommended config to test file globs using an appropriate flat-config export, or make the rule detect test filenames and no-op outside tests. If the intended contract is global, update the rule name/docs/tests to reflect that broader behaviour.
items.reproduction: Enable plugin.configs.recommended on a normal source file containing const x = value as any; and it will warn.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: no-any-in-tests.test.ts exercises AST patterns only; it does not pass filenames for test versus non-test files or validate the recommended config scope.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add RuleTester cases with filename values for a test file and a non-test source file, or add config-level tests verifying the recommended config only applies this rule to test globs.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts and/or packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/rules/no-any-in-tests.ts plus config or filename-aware tests

items.title: Public template mutations can desynchronise the explain service
items.recommendation: Keep the service state tied to the registry. Options include not exporting clearTemplates from the public explain index, making clearTemplates reset the service flag through a single owner, or having ensureTemplatesInitialised verify required built-in templates before returning.
items.reproduction: Call initExplainService(); clearTemplates(); then isExplainable('ARCH-001') or explainByRule('ARCH-001'). The service does not re-register built-in templates because templatesInitialised is still true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests reset through resetExplainService() or test template-loader in isolation; none compose public clearTemplates/registerTemplate with the high-level explain-service APIs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a public-API test that initialises the service, calls clearTemplates(), and verifies the next explainByRule('ARCH-001') either reinitialises built-ins or that clearTemplates is no longer exported for consumers.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/index.ts and/or packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts, with one explain-service integration test.

items.title: similarWarnings can become negative when the current warning is not in allWarnings
items.recommendation: Clamp the value at zero or only subtract when the current warning is actually present in the same-rule/same-file set.
items.reproduction: Call explainWarning with an ARCH-001 warning and allWarnings set to [] or to warnings from other files only. The returned boundary explanation has related.similarWarnings === -1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing similar-count test only covers the happy path where allWarnings includes the current warning and another same-file warning; it does not cover an empty or partial allWarnings list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that calls explainWarning(archWarning, []) and asserts related.similarWarnings is 0 or undefined, never negative.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/explain/explain-service.ts buildContext plus a focused explain-service regression test.

items.title: Exported API composition has only CORS preflight coverage
items.recommendation: Add a small index-level integration test that imports ../index.js and asserts representative mounted routes under /api/v1, including /health and at least one route behind the global middleware stack.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests mount route modules such as auth and admin on fresh Hono instances, so they prove route-local behaviour but not the exported app's base path, route registration, or middleware ordering. cors.test imports index.ts but only covers one waitlist preflight.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: In apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/index.test.ts, mock db/licence dependencies as needed, import ../index.js, and assert /api/v1/health responds with the expected shape plus representative /api/v1/auth/verify and /api/v1/admin/invite requests reach the mounted route/middleware rather than returning 404.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change under apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__ for exported app composition.

items.title: Queued waiters can be bypassed by new direct acquisitions
items.recommendation: Before direct acquisition, check the queue for existing entries from other agents. If the queue is non-empty, join it and only acquire when this agent is first. Alternatively make direct acquisition conditional on an empty queue under the same queue-file lock.
items.reproduction: Have A hold a lock, have B call `waitForLock` and enter the queue, release A's lock, then have C call `waitForLock` before B's next poll. C can acquire directly without joining behind B.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests cover position ordering after explicit `join` calls, but they do not cover `waitForLock` with an existing waiter and a later contender.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `waitForLock` fairness test where an existing queued agent must acquire before a newcomer when the lock becomes available.
items.minimumFixScope: QueueManager.waitForLock acquisition ordering and corresponding fairness tests.

items.title: Concurrency subpath is advertised but not exported
items.recommendation: Add a `./concurrency` export with `types` and `import` entries pointing at `./dist/concurrency/index.d.ts` and `./dist/concurrency/index.js`, and verify the build emits that directory.
items.reproduction: Install or build the package as an ESM dependency, then run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency')"`; Node will reject the unexported subpath.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The listed tests import concurrency files by relative source paths and do not exercise package-level exports or the generated hook import path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds the runtime package and dynamically imports `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency` through the package exports map.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json plus any build/package export smoke test needed to verify the subpath.

items.title: Agent registry updates can lose concurrent registrations and heartbeats
items.recommendation: Protect all registry mutations with a registry file lock or switch to per-agent registry records so independent agents do not overwrite a shared JSON object.
items.reproduction: Start two AgentManager instances with different agent IDs and call `register()` concurrently against an empty registry. Both can read an empty registry and save a single-agent registry; the final file may contain only one agent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No listed AgentManager tests exercise concurrent registration, heartbeat, unregister, or stale cleanup against the same registry file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent registration test that launches multiple AgentManager.register calls and asserts the final registry contains every agent with correct heartbeat metadata.
items.minimumFixScope: AgentManager registry mutation methods and concurrent registry tests.

items.title: Queue mutations are only partially serialised
items.recommendation: Use the same per-queue file lock for every queue mutation, including leave, getStatus cleanup, cleanupAllTimedOut, and waitForLock's leave-on-acquire/timeout paths.
items.reproduction: Run one agent leaving a queue while another joins the same resource. If both read the old queue before either final write, whichever writes last determines the file and can drop the other update.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The queue tests are sequential and do not create concurrent join/leave or cleanup interleavings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add concurrent join/leave tests that assert no joined entry is dropped and no leaving entry is resurrected after both operations complete.
items.minimumFixScope: QueueManager mutation methods and queue concurrency tests.

items.title: Expired or stale lock takeover is not mutually exclusive
items.recommendation: Serialize all lock state transitions, including renewals and force-acquire, behind the same per-lock sentinel or implement a compare-and-swap check that only succeeds when the existing lock still matches the lock that was read.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock, then start two LockManager instances with different agent IDs and call `acquire({ type, resource })` concurrently. Both can observe the expired file before either write completes and both can receive `acquired: true`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test performs a single sequential takeover; it does not race two contenders against the same expired or stale lock.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a concurrent expired-lock takeover test that releases a barrier after both contenders have observed the expired lock and asserts exactly one acquisition succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: LockManager takeover and renewal paths, plus concurrency tests for expired/stale takeover.

items.title: SpecKit input size limits are bypassable or missing
items.recommendation: Centralize a UTF-8 byte-length guard and apply it before all SpecKit parsing entrypoints, including spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md in v2.
items.reproduction: Pass a string of repeated multi-byte characters whose `content.length` is below 2 MiB but whose `Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8')` exceeds it to SpecKitParser.parseSpecMarkdown, or pass a very large spec/plan/tasks document to SpecKitImportAdapterV2.convertToAPS.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The associated test covers parseGeneric only; there is no equivalent SpecKit parser or SpecKitImportAdapterV2 size-limit test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mirror the generic parser byte-limit tests for SpecKitParser.parseSpecMarkdown and add a convertToAPS v2 test that rejects oversized spec, plan, and tasks contents before parsing.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitParser.parseSpecMarkdown plus SpecParser.parseSpec, PlanParser.parsePlan, TasksParser.parseTasks, or a shared guard in SpecKitImportAdapterV2 before dispatch.

items.title: Successful SpecKit imports return placeholder APS hashes
items.recommendation: After createPlan, compute and assign generateHash(plan) consistently across all SpecKit import and generateSpec paths instead of returning the placeholder.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitImportAdapter.convertToAPS or SpecKitImportAdapterV2.convertToAPS with valid input and inspect `result.data.hash`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise SpecKit import output contracts or assert hash validity.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add SpecKit import tests that assert successful conversion returns a non-zero 64-character hash matching the same generateHash pattern used by SpecKitFormatAdapter.parse.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitImportAdapter.generateSpec, SpecKitImportAdapter.convertToAPS, SpecKitImportAdapterV2.generateSpec, and SpecKitImportAdapterV2.buildAPSFromDocs.

items.title: SpecKit v2 import can emit traversal paths from scenario titles
items.recommendation: Slugify scenario titles to a constrained character set and run validateRelativePath on every generated path; reject or warn on invalid titles instead of emitting traversal paths.
items.reproduction: Import a SpecKit v2 spec with a user scenario heading like `### P1: ../../outside` and inspect the first proposed change path.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file only exercises generic parser input-size handling and has no SpecKit v2 import case for unsafe user scenario titles.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitImportAdapterV2 convertToAPS test with `### P1: ../../outside` and assert the conversion fails or the emitted path is a validated safe relative path without `..` segments.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitImportAdapterV2.inferPathFromScenario and any caller that synthesizes Change.path from parsed external content.

items.title: Official SpecKit v2 adapter is omitted from the package surface
items.recommendation: Export SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from src/speckit/index.ts and ensure the package root exports it through the published `.` surface.
items.reproduction: Attempt to import SpecKitImportAdapterV2 through the package's SpecKit barrel exports.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not perform public API import checks for the adapters package.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package API test or typecheck fixture importing SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from @eddacraft/anvil-adapters and constructing it.
items.minimumFixScope: src/speckit/index.ts, plus any generated/package root export expectations if required.

items.title: Empty APS exports produce NaN task progress
items.recommendation: Handle the zero-task case explicitly, for example by emitting 0% progress or omitting the progress percentage when there are no tasks.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with an APSPlan whose proposed_changes array is empty and inspect content.tasksContent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not cover SpecKit export or empty-change APS plans.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitExportAdapter convertFromAPS test for an APS plan with no proposed_changes and assert tasksContent does not contain NaN.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitExportAdapter.generateTasksMarkdown.

items.title: Requirements sections are parsed twice because both header patterns match the same heading
items.recommendation: Make the patterns mutually exclusive, remove the duplicate generic Requirements pattern, or collect sections/items into a Set before returning them.
items.reproduction:
parseGeneric('# Plan

## Requirements
- Add login
- Add logout
') will produce four requirement-derived changes instead of two because extractRequirements reads the same section once per matching pattern.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: parser.test.ts only checks input size limits and does not assert parsed requirements or proposed_changes counts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseGeneric test with a single '## Requirements' section containing two list items and assert exactly two proposed_changes are produced.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts extractRequirements

items.title: Numbered requirements parse successfully but fail generic detection and validation scoring
items.recommendation: Count numbered markdown list items in analyzeContent using the same list grammar supported by the parser, and include them in listItemCount/hasLists.
items.reproduction:
A document such as '# Plan

## Requirements
1. Add login
2. Add logout
3. Add reset password
' has parseable requirements, but analyzeContent reports hasLists=false and listItemCount=0, leaving confidence below the 30% validation threshold for typical short documents.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise detect(), validate(), or numbered-list parsing behavior.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add adapter detect/validate tests for a numbered-only Requirements section and assert detection succeeds and validation has no LOW_CONFIDENCE error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/utils.ts analyzeContent list detection

items.title: Parsed generic plans receive a hash computed over the placeholder hash field
items.recommendation: Build a planWithoutHash object in genericToAPS or parse(), compute generateHash(planWithoutHash), and return { ...planWithoutHash, hash }. Avoid including any placeholder hash in the hashed payload.
items.reproduction: Parse any generic markdown document through GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse, then validate the returned APS plan with hash validation enabled. The calculated hash over the plan content without the hash field will differ from the stored hash generated at packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts:88.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests only exercise the byte-size guard, and serializer tests do not call GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse or validate generated hashes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GenericMarkdownAdapter.parse test that parses a representative markdown document and asserts the returned hash equals generateHash({ ...plan, hash omitted }).
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/generic/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/generic/format-adapter.ts hash construction path

items.title: Private Anvil docs are not auth-gated in the reviewed Next surface
items.recommendation: Add a Next middleware or explicit /anvil route/proxy gate that reads the anvil-docs-session cookie, calls verifyLicense, redirects unauthenticated users to /auth/login?next=<validated path>, and only then serves or proxies the private docs. Keep the X-Robots-Tag header as defence in depth, not as the gate.
items.reproduction: Request /anvil/overview directly in this app surface. In the reviewed files, the only /anvil-specific handling is the next.config.ts header rule, so no session cookie or JWT validation is enforced before the request proceeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover individual helpers only. There is no route or middleware test that requests /anvil/overview with and without an anvil-docs-session cookie and asserts redirect versus access.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add integration tests for /anvil/overview: no cookie redirects to /auth/login with a validated next parameter, invalid JWT redirects, and a docs-entitled JWT reaches the protected docs/proxy path.
items.minimumFixScope: Wire authentication enforcement into the /anvil request path and add route-level tests for authenticated and unauthenticated access.

items.title: Expired-token test does not prove expiry enforcement for entitled tokens
items.recommendation: Change the expired-token test to include an entitled tier, for example { sub: 'user@example.com', tier: 'beta' }, with a past expiration. Consider adding a separate test for a beta token with no exp claim if license JWTs are required to be time-bound.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current expired-token case also fails the entitlement requirement, so it does not isolate expiration handling.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Sign { sub: 'user@example.com', tier: 'beta' } with a negative expiration and assert verifyLicense returns { valid: false }. If appropriate, sign the same claims with no exp and assert rejection.
items.minimumFixScope: Update lib/jwt.test.ts so expiry behaviour is tested independently from tier entitlement checks.

items.title: docs-site typecheck depends on prebuilt workspace declaration output
items.recommendation: Make the typecheck target build-mode/topology aware, for example by using tsc -b with valid references and Nx target dependencies, or by mapping editor/typecheck paths to source declarations that are available in a clean checkout.
items.reproduction: From a clean workspace where ../../packages/anvil/*/dist has not been generated, run pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-site typecheck. The docs-site compiler resolution is configured to look for those dist .d.ts files.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the package metadata only exposes the typecheck script without a test or build target proving referenced package outputs exist first.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an Nx or CI check that runs docs-site typecheck from a clean workspace before package dist artifacts are generated, or assert the target depends on the referenced package build/typecheck outputs.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-site/package.json and/or tsconfig/Nx target configuration so docs-site typechecking is deterministic from a clean checkout.

items.title: docs-site README uses yarn commands in a pnpm workspace
items.recommendation: Replace the yarn examples with pnpm or Nx commands that match the workspace, such as pnpm install, pnpm start, pnpm build, and the documented nx start/build docs-site forms where appropriate.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked docs validation or README command test was provided, and package metadata tests do not exercise documentation command accuracy.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs command check that validates README command snippets for package-manager consistency, or include this README in the existing docs lint/check workflow.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-site/README.md command snippets to match the workspace package manager and package scripts.

items.title: SpecKit v2 adapter is tested but not reachable through the package API
items.recommendation: Export SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from src/speckit/index.ts and ensure the package root re-exports it. If subpath imports are part of the public API, add explicit ./speckit export entries in package.json as well.
items.reproduction: Build or pack the adapters package, then attempt to import SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from @eddacraft/anvil-adapters or @eddacraft/anvil-adapters/speckit in an ESM consumer.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: speckit-import-v2.test.ts imports ../speckit/import-v2.js directly, bypassing src/index.ts and the package.json exports map, so the adapter can pass tests while remaining unavailable to package consumers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-boundary test that imports the built @eddacraft/anvil-adapters package and asserts SpecKitImportAdapterV2 is exported and can convert the existing spec.md + plan.md + tasks.md fixture.
items.minimumFixScope: src/speckit/index.ts, src/index.ts if needed, package.json exports if subpath imports are intended, and one package-boundary regression test.

items.title: Licence verification accepts malformed claim shapes after signature verification
items.recommendation: Validate the full verified payload with a runtime schema before returning claims: require scopes to be string[], identity to be an object with provider string and id string|null when present, org to be string|null, seats to be a finite integer, and email to be a valid email if that is part of the licence contract.
items.reproduction: Using the test private key setup, sign a JWT with issuer https://api.eddacraft.ai, audience anvil-cli, a subject, email 'a@b.com', and payload { scopes: [123], identity: 'not-an-object', org: 7 }. verifyLicence returns a non-null claims object instead of null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The licence tests cover missing scopes, malformed JWTs, wrong issuer/audience, expired tokens, and bad signatures, but they do not cover malformed claim element types inside an otherwise validly signed token.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add verifyLicence cases for signed tokens with scopes: [123], malformed identity, non-string org, and invalid seats; each should return null rather than a LicenceClaims object.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/licence.ts claim parsing plus focused verifyLicence regression tests.

items.title: Debug logger emits object payloads without redaction
items.recommendation: Before logging non-string data, serialize through a safe redactor that recursively redacts strings in arrays and plain objects, or narrow debug data to the same scalar field-bag model as infoLog and sanitize every string value before emission.
items.reproduction: Set DEBUG=anvil:* and call createDebugger('auth-github-device')('poll result', { authorization: 'Bearer ghu_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz', access_token: 'ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' }); the object payload is logged without redaction.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise debug.ts. Existing email and auth-adjacent tests assert other redaction/validation paths, but none spy on console.debug with object payloads containing token-like strings.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a debug logger test that enables DEBUG=anvil:*, spies on console.debug, logs an object containing Bearer/ghp_/ghu_ token-shaped values, and asserts the emitted payload contains [REDACTED] and not the original secrets.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts plus a focused debug logger test.

items.title: Docs-site typecheck depends on generated workspace dist declarations without a build prerequisite
items.recommendation: Either make the docs-site build/typecheck targets depend on the workspace package build outputs, or resolve workspace imports to source declarations via a supported source condition/path mapping that does not require pre-existing dist artifacts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and package-level build orchestration is not exercised by the included source snippets.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run docs-site typecheck and build from a clean checkout after deleting referenced workspace dist directories, or add an Nx/package-manager validation that proves docs-site builds its workspace dependencies first.
items.minimumFixScope: Update docs-site package/project TypeScript and build orchestration; referenced package exports may need source/build-target support if the current dist-only contract is intentional.

items.title: Docs-site package documentation is stale against the manifest and agent instructions
items.recommendation: Refresh README.md and AGENTS.md to match the current package metadata and pnpm workflow, including the current Docusaurus version and commands.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included files contain no documentation validation or command-snippet tests that would catch stale setup instructions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs/package metadata check that verifies README and AGENTS command snippets use the repo-supported package manager and that documented Docusaurus major/minor versions match package.json.
items.minimumFixScope: Documentation-only update in docs-site README.md and AGENTS.md.

items.title: README says every traversal attempt throws, but exists intentionally returns false
items.recommendation: Adjust the README API contract to state that exists() returns false for blocked or inaccessible paths, while mutating and reading operations throw on traversal or symlink escape.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover the intended exists() behavior; they do not validate README/API text against that exception.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/shared/storage/README.md to document the exists() exception.

items.title: Dangling final symlink can escape the storage sandbox on write
items.recommendation: In the ENOENT path, lstat the requested final path before treating it as a new file and reject if it is a symlink, or use no-follow/openat-style file creation where available. Keep the existing parent realpath walk for missing intermediate paths, but also validate the final path object when it exists as a dangling symlink.
items.reproduction: Create base and outside directories. Inside base, create a symlink named link pointing to outside/new.txt, where new.txt does not exist but outside exists. Then call await storage.write('link', 'escaped'). The current resolvePath path returns base/link and fs.writeFile follows the symlink, creating outside/new.txt.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The symlink write test covers a symlink to an existing outside file, where realpathSync succeeds and the current code rejects. There is no test for a final-component symlink whose outside target is missing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a non-Windows test that creates symlinkSync(join(outsideDir, 'new.txt'), join(tempDir, 'dangling-write-link')), calls storage.write('dangling-write-link', 'data'), expects a path escape error, and asserts outsideDir/new.txt was not created.
items.minimumFixScope: Update FileStorage.resolvePath's ENOENT handling for final-component symlinks and add the focused regression test in file-storage.test.ts.

items.title: drift-check can compare against a prose N/M instead of the index count cell
items.recommendation: Move the index row/count-cell lookup into the shared lib and have drift-check use the same name-cell link plus dedicated count-cell logic as index-counts.
items.reproduction: Use a module with header progress 4/4 and an index row for that module that contains prose like "infrastructure (6/38 complete)" before the dedicated progress cell "4/4". drift-check will capture 6/38 and warn, while index-counts would leave the row unchanged.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature payload lists no linked tests, and the owned drift-check code still has an independent regex instead of sharing index-counts' protected lookup path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a drift-check fixture where an index row has an unrelated N/M in a prose cell before the real progress cell; assert no aps-index-progress-mismatch when the dedicated cell matches the module header.
items.minimumFixScope: Extract findIndexRow or equivalent logic to scripts/aps/lib/modules.mjs and replace drift-check's indexText.match regex with that shared helper.

items.title: advance-released can mark APS items shipped from a non-published release record
items.recommendation: Require lifecycleState === "published" before allowing writes. For non-published records, exit non-zero with wrote=false, or add an explicit override flag if historical/manual operation is truly required.
items.reproduction: Create a release record whose fenced JSON has {"lifecycleState":"candidate","aps":{"items":[{"id":"WID-001"}]}} and a module item WID-001 with Status: Merged. Run advance-released without --dry-run. The script prints only a note about candidate state, rewrites WID-001 to Released/Shipped, and exits 0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature payload lists no linked tests, and the owned code has no lifecycle guard. Existing behaviour around non-published lifecycle states is not asserted by the included evidence.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an advance-released fixture with lifecycleState: candidate and a Merged item; assert exit is non-zero, no module file is rewritten, and JSON output reports wrote:false.
items.minimumFixScope: Change advance-released.mjs to validate lifecycleState before computing wrote or before mutating dirtyFiles, and add the candidate-record regression fixture.

items.title: Empty task export emits NaN progress
items.recommendation: Handle the zero-task case explicitly, for example by emitting `Progress: 0%` when tasks.length is 0.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with an APSPlan whose proposed_changes is an empty array; the returned tasksContent contains `Progress: NaN%`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file exercises the generic parser size guard only and does not cover SpecKit export output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKit export test that converts a plan with no proposed_changes and asserts tasksContent contains a finite progress percentage.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/adapters/src/speckit/export.ts plus one export regression test.

items.title: SpecKit size guard counts UTF-16 code units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') or an equivalent byte counter for the SpecKit guard, matching the generic parser behaviour.
items.reproduction: Pass parseSpecMarkdown a string of 524289 U+1F600 characters. Its UTF-8 byte length is greater than 2 MiB while content.length is about 1048578, so the guard does not throw.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests cover parseGeneric only; there is no equivalent SpecKitParser multi-byte boundary test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add SpecKitParser tests for ASCII over-limit, exact byte-limit, and multi-byte over-limit input mirroring parser.test.ts.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/adapters/src/speckit/parser.ts and a focused SpecKit parser test.

items.title: Nested markdown headings truncate section bodies
items.recommendation: Parse headings by level, or at minimum search for the next true level-2 heading with a pattern such as /^##[ \t]+/m from the section start instead of a raw substring that also matches deeper headings.
items.reproduction:
parseGeneric('# Plan

## Requirements

### API

- Accept config') returns no requirement change because the Requirements body is truncated at the nested ### heading before list extraction.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests do not cover section extraction, nested headings, or conversion of parsed requirements/tasks/features into APS proposed_changes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser test with Requirements and Tasks sections containing level-3 subsections and list items, asserting all nested items are present in proposed_changes.
items.minimumFixScope: Change extractSectionBody in generic/utils.ts and add parser coverage for nested heading sections.

items.title: Numbered-list planning items are dropped or fail detection
items.recommendation: Use one shared list-item extractor that supports bullets, numbered items, and task checkboxes where relevant, then use it consistently in extractGoals, extractRequirements, extractTasks, extractFeatures, and analyzeContent.
items.reproduction:
parseGeneric('# Plan

## Tasks

1. Build API
2. Add tests') produces no task changes because extractTasks only matches bullet list items. A short numbered-only requirements document can parse numbered requirements but still validate as LOW_CONFIDENCE because analyzeContent ignores numbered lists.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests only exercise the byte-size guard, and the serializer tests only exercise metadata type handling; none parse or validate numbered-list sections.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parser and validate/detect tests for numbered Goals, Requirements, Tasks, and Features sections, asserting extracted APS changes and confidence/list counts match equivalent bullet-list documents.
items.minimumFixScope: Update generic/utils.ts list matching and add focused parser/detection tests under generic/__tests__.

items.title: Root leaf plans with "Modules ..." headings are misclassified as indexes
items.recommendation: Use the same parseIndex probe at the root before selecting loadMultiModulePlan, or make detectIndexFile strict enough to recognise only actual index module sections.
items.reproduction: Create a single-file leaf APS document with normal tasks plus a level-2 heading named "Modules impacted", then call loadPlan(path). It will enter loadMultiModulePlan instead of loadSingleFilePlan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included false-positive test loads an index whose child leaf has the ambiguous heading. It never calls loadPlan directly on an ambiguous root leaf file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a loader test that calls loadPlan on examples/false-positive-modules/leaf.aps.md, or an equivalent root leaf fixture with "## Modules impacted", and asserts isMultiModule is false and tasks are loaded.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust root index detection in loadPlan and add one root false-positive regression test.

items.title: Bundle downloads can follow redirects to non-HTTPS hosts with credentials
items.recommendation: Resolve redirects against the original URL, reject non-HTTPS redirects except explicit localhost test cases, cap redirect depth, and strip Authorization and other sensitive headers when the redirect changes origin.
items.reproduction: Configure an https bundle URL with bearer auth that responds 302 Location: http://attacker.example/bundle.tar.gz. The recursive download sends the Authorization header to the redirected HTTP URL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The redirect test intentionally exercises an HTTP localhost redirect and only asserts success; it does not cover HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade, cross-origin redirects, or credential preservation across redirects.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for an HTTPS-origin redirect to HTTP non-localhost expecting failure, and for cross-origin HTTPS redirects expecting Authorization not to be forwarded.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts redirect handling and BundleManager redirect/auth tests.

items.title: Ed25519 is advertised as supported but cannot verify with Node crypto
