items.recommendation: Implement Ed25519 using crypto.verify(null, Buffer.from(data), publicKey, signature), or remove Ed25519 from the supported/default algorithms until it is implemented and tested.
items.reproduction: Generate an Ed25519 key pair, sign the canonical files array with crypto.sign(null, data, privateKey), configure BundleVerifier with algorithm Ed25519, and verifyBundle(); the Ed25519 case throws during createVerify and the result is unverified.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The crypto verification tests cover RS256 and ES256 only; there is no Ed25519 positive-path test despite Ed25519 being in DEFAULT_ALLOWED_ALGORITHMS.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a valid Ed25519 signed bundle test that expects verifyBundle() to return verified=true and keyId for the Ed25519 key.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-verifier.ts Ed25519 branch and BundleVerifier Ed25519 tests.

items.title: Bundle signature verification accepts unsigned files in the bundle
items.recommendation: During verification, enumerate all policy/data files that are allowed to be part of the signed bundle, require every relevant file to appear exactly once in the verified manifest, and reject empty file lists or unexpected extra files.
items.reproduction: Create policy.rego, sign a manifest listing only policy.rego, then add evil.rego beside it. verifyBundle() still returns verified=true because evil.rego is never compared against the manifest.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover valid manifests with one or more listed files and tampering of a listed file, but they never add an extra unlisted bundle file or use an empty signed file list.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BundleVerifier test that signs only policy.rego, writes an additional unsigned extra.rego, and expects verifyBundle() to fail with an unsigned/uncovered file error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-verifier.ts plus focused BundleVerifier tests.

items.title: Failed bundle updates delete the last valid cached bundle
items.recommendation: Extract updates into a separate temporary directory, fully validate extraction and signatures/checksums there, then atomically replace the old bundle directory only after the new bundle is ready. On failure, leave the existing cache entry and files untouched.
items.reproduction: Download a valid bundle with a short refresh interval, wait for expiry, then have the server return a corrupt gzip/tar. The second download fails and the original bundle directory has been removed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover cache reuse, checksum failure before deletion, invalidation, and cache clearing, but not an expired cached bundle where extraction of the replacement fails after the old directory is removed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that seeds a cached bundle, forces it expired, serves an invalid tarball, asserts downloadBundle() fails, and asserts getBundle() still returns the original path with policy.rego present.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts extraction/replace flow and one cache-preservation regression test.

items.title: BundleManager signature_key contract is unusable for signed bundle downloads
items.recommendation: Define the signature source explicitly. Either integrate BundleVerifier/.signatures.json after extraction, or add config for a signature URL/path, download/read it deliberately, and resolve signature_key file paths before calling crypto.verify.
items.reproduction: Configure a bundle with signature_key set to a valid public key file path. downloadBundle() looks for <cache>/<name>.tar.gz.tmp.sig, then passes the path string as the key material, so verification fails.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: BundleManager tests disable signature verification in the shared setup and only cover checksum validation, so no test exercises signature_key, key-file paths, or sidecar signature retrieval.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add BundleManager tests for inline PEM and key-file signature verification using a generated signed tarball/signature pair, including a missing signature case with a clear error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/policy/src/bundle-manager.ts signature handling and BundleManager signature tests.

items.title: Freshness guard misses Rust dependency source changes
items.recommendation: Include Rust workspace/path dependency sources in the freshness baseline, preferably by deriving package dependencies with cargo metadata and walking the relevant source roots, or by otherwise tracking the native crates that feed this binding.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata declares no linked tests for check-binding-fresh.mjs, and the package test script only runs binding tests after pretest; it does not exercise stale-input detection cases for dependency-source changes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a node:test or fixture-driven script test that creates a fake binding older than a workspace dependency source file but newer than this crate's src, Cargo.toml, build.rs, and Cargo.lock, then asserts check-binding-fresh.mjs exits non-zero.
items.minimumFixScope: Update check-binding-fresh.mjs input discovery and add focused coverage for dependency-source freshness.

items.title: Human input IDs are returned but never emitted
items.recommendation: Add the generated identifier to the human_input observation contract and emitted payload, or stop generating/returning a link ID if human_input observations are intentionally unaddressable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this source group, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test that calls emitHumanInput with a fake KindlingService and asserts the emitted human_input observation contains the same generated/linking identifier returned by emitHumanInput.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/emitters/human-input-emitter.ts plus the HumanInputObservation contract/types and any schema validation for human_input observations.

items.title: Worksheet build fails when the output directory is absent
items.recommendation: Call OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) before writing the worksheet, preferably immediately before dest.write_text or during startup.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and none cover running build with a fresh output directory.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run build against a temporary EXT_FP_WORK/EXT_FP_OUT where the output directory does not exist and assert the worksheet file is created.
items.minimumFixScope: Create the output directory before worksheet writes and add one focused build test for a fresh output path.

items.title: Warning file paths can escape the checked repository
items.recommendation: Parse relfile as a relative path, reject absolute paths, resolve the candidate path, and require it to remain under (WORK / repo).resolve() before reading. Return a placeholder such as <source unavailable> for rejected paths.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and none exercise absolute or parent-directory file paths in warning dumps.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a temporary WORK directory with a repo subdirectory and a separate secret file outside that repo, feed a warning whose file is ../secret.txt or an absolute path, then assert the worksheet does not contain the secret line.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden source_line path validation and add a focused test for path traversal and absolute warning paths.

items.title: docs-public is registered as an Nx application without explicit build/typecheck targets
items.recommendation: Add explicit project.json targets for build, typecheck, start/serve as needed, or otherwise wire docs-public into the workspace's package-script inference and CI gates. The fix should make the standard repository build/typecheck path exercise this Docusaurus app.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the included project.json has no test, build, or typecheck target for Nx-based validation to execute.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a workspace validation test or CI assertion that nx show project docs-public exposes build and typecheck targets, then run those targets in the standard docs validation path.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/docs-public/project.json target metadata and any CI/workspace target selection needed to include docs-public.

items.title: queryMemories does not apply pagination defaults for raw query objects
items.recommendation: Parse or normalise incoming queries at the MemoryStore boundary before filtering, including defaulting include_superseded, limit, offset, sort_by, and sort_order consistently.
items.reproduction: After saving at least one memory, call store.queryMemories({} as MemoryQuery). The result page is empty because the computed end index is NaN instead of defaulting to offset 0 and limit 100.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The MemoryStore tests use the local queryDefaults helper, so they never call queryMemories with omitted pagination fields even though the public query schema supports defaulted pagination.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that saves a memory and asserts queryMemories({} as MemoryQuery) returns it with limit 100, offset 0, and has_more computed from those defaults.
items.minimumFixScope: Normalise query defaults in MemoryStore.queryMemories and add a focused test for an empty query object.

items.title: Promotion validation can throw TypeError instead of returning schema errors
items.recommendation: Use the safeParse result as the source for field-level checks, or guard with typeof input.reason === 'string' and typeof input.promoted_by === 'string' before trimming.
items.reproduction: Call validatePromotionInput with a payload that is missing reason or promoted_by, cast as PromoteProposalInput. Instead of returning validation errors, it throws when accessing .trim() on undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Zod schema violation test removes proposal_id, leaving the fields used by the extra trim checks intact.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend the promotion validation tests with malformed inputs missing reason and promoted_by and assert validatePromotionInput returns valid: false without throwing.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden PromotionService.validatePromotionInput and add the missing malformed-input cases.

items.title: Search misses matches beyond the index preview
items.recommendation: Either store a separate full searchable statement in the index, or when query.search is present, load candidate memories and apply the search predicate to memory.statement rather than the truncated index preview.
items.reproduction: Save a memory whose statement is 120+ characters and contains a unique token only after the first 100 characters, then call searchMemories with that token. The memory will not be returned because queryMemories filters against the truncated index statement.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The search test uses 'Use deterministic plan checks in CI.', where the searched token appears inside the first 100 characters, so the index preview and full statement behave the same.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MemoryStore test that saves a memory with a long statement containing a unique token after character 100 and asserts searchMemories(token) returns that memory.
items.minimumFixScope: Update MemoryStore search filtering and add a regression test in packages/edda-stack/src/edda/memory-store.test.ts.

items.title: Typecheck target combines `--noEmit` with `emitDeclarationOnly`
items.recommendation: Remove `emitDeclarationOnly` from the docs-shell tsconfig used for application typechecking, or split declaration-emitting settings into a separate build tsconfig that is not used by the `tsc --noEmit` target.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-shell typecheck` or the Nx `docs-shell:typecheck` target with this tsconfig.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites exercise runtime helpers only; they do not invoke the package or Nx typecheck target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI/package validation check that runs the docs-shell typecheck target, or ensure the existing workspace typecheck includes this project.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/docs-shell/tsconfig.json` or the docs-shell typecheck/build target configuration so no target passes `--noEmit` while loading a config with `emitDeclarationOnly`.

items.title: Refresh rotation consumes the old token before new credentials are durably issued
items.recommendation: Make refresh rotation atomic at the database boundary where possible: consume the old token and insert the replacement in one transaction, and avoid exposing the client to a consumed-old/no-new-token state. At minimum, add explicit recovery semantics for post-consume failures so retries do not trigger family theft detection for server-side issuance failures.
items.reproduction: Simulate consumeRefreshToken resolving true and insertRefreshToken or signLicence throwing during POST /auth/session/refresh. The old token is already consumed, no new raw refresh token reaches the client, and a retry with the old token will be treated as token reuse.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The auth-session tests cover happy path, invalid tokens, consumed-token reuse, and concurrent consume failure. They do not cover downstream failures after consumeRefreshToken succeeds, such as insertRefreshToken or signLicence throwing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where consumeRefreshToken succeeds but insertRefreshToken rejects, asserting the implementation does not leave the old token consumed without a retry-safe outcome; add a similar test for licence signing failure after replacement creation.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-session.ts and the refresh-token query/transaction helper used by that route.

items.title: Default invite flow advertises requested scopes but never persists them for activation
items.recommendation: Persist the granted scopes in the default invite transaction, matching /admin/approve's access_tokens insert pattern, or change the API to reject scoped default invites if only tokenOnly/approve can establish scoped grants.
items.reproduction: POST /admin/invite with {"email":"alice@example.com","scopes":["preview","beta"]} and tokenOnly omitted/false, then complete the device activation flow. The invite response reports preview+beta, but no access_tokens row was created for those scopes, so /auth/device/poll cannot issue a licence with the preview grant.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included default invite test only uses the implicit ['beta'] default and asserts the response shape. It does not send non-default scopes or assert that the transaction includes an INSERT INTO access_tokens for the default device-code invite path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an admin invite test for tokenOnly=false with scopes ['preview','beta'] that asserts the transaction includes an access_tokens insert containing those scopes, then add/extend a device activation test to assert the issued licence preserves the preview scope for that invite path.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts default /admin/invite transaction and the corresponding admin/device route tests.

items.title: OTP active-code limit is enforced with a check-then-insert race
items.recommendation: Move the cap enforcement into a single database operation, for example an INSERT ... SELECT guarded by a COUNT predicate in a transaction/serializable block, or a per-user partial constraint/lock that prevents more than the configured number of active unconsumed, unexpired codes.
items.reproduction: Send several POST /auth/otp/request calls concurrently for the same active user when they have fewer than three active codes. Each request can read the same pre-insert count and then insert its own OTP row, resulting in more than MAX_ACTIVE_CODES active rows.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test sets countActiveOtpCodes to 3 and verifies a single request does not insert. It does not exercise concurrent requests where the count is below the limit for every racing caller.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a query-level or integration test that fires concurrent OTP requests with the active count initially below MAX_ACTIVE_CODES and asserts the database ends with no more than three active codes for the user.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-otp.ts plus the OTP insert/count query helper so the limit is enforced atomically.

items.title: Packaged API omits the migration CLI and migration inputs it advertises
items.recommendation: Either include the migration CLI and SQL migration files in the package artefact, or change the migration command to use packaged dist assets and ensure the build copies migrations there. If migrations are source-checkout-only by design, do not advertise the command in a package manifest used for release artefacts.
items.reproduction: Run npm pack or pnpm pack for apps/anvil-api and inspect the tarball: package.json will contain the migrate scripts, but scripts/migrate.mjs and src/db/migrations are not included because package.json files only allows dist and README.md.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise the source implementation imported from ../db/migrate.js with temporary fixture directories. They do not exercise package packing, package.json files filtering, or the scripts/migrate.mjs wrapper's resolved paths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package/artefact smoke test that builds apps/anvil-api, creates the packed artefact or packlist, and asserts that the migration entrypoint plus the SQL migration directory used by that entrypoint are present and addressable.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/package.json files/build scripts plus apps/anvil-api/scripts/migrate.mjs pathing if migrations are copied to dist

items.title: Plan-based filters receive relative paths while planless filters receive absolute paths
items.recommendation: Compute the absolute fullPath before applying filter in the plan-based branch, and call filter(fullPath) there just as normaliseTargetFiles does.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this source group, and the owned file contains no co-located assertions covering filter parity between planless and plan-based contexts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a runtime test that passes the same workspace-relative file through context.targetFiles and context.plan.proposed_changes with a filter asserting path.isAbsolute(input), and verify both modes return the same absolute path.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/types/gate.types.ts plan-based branch in getFilesFromContext, plus a focused unit test for filter callback path shape parity.

items.title: Linked registry tests do not exercise the common registry
items.recommendation: Add tests under src/common or adjust the linked test to import the common registry explicitly, covering duplicate registration, unregister, getAdapterForFormat, listSupportedFormats, clear, detectFormat, and singleton state isolation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The associated registry.test.ts targets the base registry by relative path, so none of its assertions instantiate or call the owned common AdapterRegistry implementation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/adapters/src/common/__tests__/registry.test.ts importing { AdapterRegistry } from '../registry.js' and asserting common registry registration, lookup, duplicate rejection, unregister, supported format listing, clear, and detectFormat behaviour.
items.minimumFixScope: Add focused tests for src/common/registry.ts and include them in the existing adapters vitest run.

items.title: README package metadata is stale against the manifest and changelog
items.recommendation: Update the README release-status/current-baseline text and Node prerequisite/badge to match the manifest and changelog, or relax package.json engines back to the documented Node 22 floor if that is the intended support contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the included docs-check surfaces validate metadata, tags, links, indexes, APS, ADRs, and release-plan shape but do not assert README release/runtime claims against package.json and CHANGELOG.md.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs validation check that parses package.json version and engines.node plus the latest released CHANGELOG.md heading, then fails when README release status or Node prerequisite text contradicts them.
items.minimumFixScope: README.md plus any generated docs/index metadata affected by the README update; optionally package.json if Node 22 is still intended to be supported.

items.title: check-tags --json emits plain text for catalogue bootstrap failures
items.recommendation: Route early catalogue failures through the same JSON payload shape when values.json is true, including surface, findings, and summary, then exit non-zero.
items.reproduction: Run `node scripts/docs/check-tags.mjs --root <fixture-without-docs/governance/tags-catalogue.md> --json`; stdout starts with `[tags] ERROR:` rather than a JSON object.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included feature lists no linked tests, and the normal JSON branch is only reached after a valid non-empty catalogue, so early bootstrap failures can remain uncovered.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a check-tags fixture test for `--json` with a missing catalogue and an empty catalogue, asserting stdout parses as JSON and contains one ERROR finding.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/check-tags.mjs early error handling for catalogue read/parse and empty-catalogue paths.

items.title: E2E package imports undeclared direct dependencies
items.recommendation: Add all directly imported packages to apps/e2e/package.json, using workspace:* for workspace packages and the appropriate dependency/devDependency entry for jose.
items.reproduction: Run the e2e package in an isolated or strict pnpm install without root/transitive hoisting; the direct jose, @eddacraft/anvil-contracts, or @eddacraft/anvil-api imports are not guaranteed to resolve from apps/e2e.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests execute inside the current workspace layout, where aliases or hoisting can mask missing manifest edges. There is no manifest-dependency validation for direct imports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dependency hygiene check such as knip/depcheck or a package graph rule that fails when apps/e2e imports undeclared external or workspace packages.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/e2e/package.json and the lockfile if dependency metadata changes require it

items.title: Status filters are dropped from generated context bundles
items.recommendation: Add `statuses?: Array<'open' | 'locked' | 'completed' | 'cancelled'>` to `ContextBundleJSON.filter` and populate it from `criteria.statuses` in `buildContextBundleJSON`. Consider including it in the Markdown bundle's filtered-by line as well for parity.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests check that scopes and tags are preserved in the JSON bundle, but there is no test for `criteria.statuses` in either JSON or Markdown context bundle output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a context bundle test that filters with `{ statuses: ['locked'] }` and asserts `bundle.filter.statuses` equals `['locked']`.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/filter/context-bundle.ts plus the associated filter tests.

items.title: Malformed percent escapes in links crash the link checker
items.recommendation: Wrap percent-decoding in a helper that catches URIError and returns an ERROR finding message for the current link, file, and line.
items.reproduction: Add a Markdown link such as `[bad](./guide%zz.md)` or `[bad](#bad%zz)` to a checked docs/plans file and run the links surface; the process throws instead of returning a structured broken-link finding.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the included files do not contain a malformed-escape fixture for check-links.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a check-links fixture containing a malformed percent escape and assert the surface exits non-zero with a labelled ERROR rather than an uncaught exception.
items.minimumFixScope: Change resolveLink to safely decode raw paths and anchors, returning a validation error when decoding fails.

items.title: Baseline regeneration can overwrite the baseline after partial surface failures
items.recommendation: Read the existing baseline before regeneration and either preserve entries for failed surfaces or abort without writing. Also make --update-baseline exit non-zero when any baselineable surface fails to produce valid JSON.
items.reproduction: Trigger a baselineable surface to emit non-JSON output during `node scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs --update-baseline`, for example by making the tags catalogue unreadable. docs-check logs the parse failure, continues, and writes a baseline without that surface's previous entries.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the included files do not show coverage for partial --update-baseline failures or preservation of existing baseline entries after a failed surface run.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a fixture baseline with an existing surface entry, force one baselineable surface to produce invalid JSON, run --update-baseline, and assert the command fails without deleting that entry.
items.minimumFixScope: Update regenerateBaseline to collect failures, preserve or reload existing baseline data for failed surfaces, and skip the final write unless regeneration completed successfully.

items.title: --no-baseline is forwarded to the index checker, which rejects it
items.recommendation: Only pass baseline flags to baselineable surfaces, or have check-index-freshness strip orchestrator-only flags before invoking docs-index.mjs.
items.reproduction: Run `node scripts/docs/check-index-freshness.mjs --no-baseline`; docs-index.mjs receives an unsupported option and exits non-zero before checking freshness.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the included evidence does not show a clean --no-baseline scenario asserting that non-baselineable surfaces still pass.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check contract test that runs the orchestrator with --no-baseline against a fixture with no baselined findings and asserts index-freshness does not fail on an unknown option.
items.minimumFixScope: Change docs-check.mjs runSurface argument forwarding so --no-baseline is appended only when surface.baselineable is true.

items.title: Parser accepts governance tables that are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Change table discovery to validate the immediate top-level sequence after the H1: metadata table first, relationships table next, allowing only non-semantic whitespace because blank lines are not AST nodes. Reject any intervening non-table content before either required table.
items.reproduction:
Call parseDocGovernance on markdown shaped like `# Title

Intro prose before metadata.

| Type | Authority | Owner | Status | Freshness |
| ---- | --------- | ----- | ------ | --------- |
| Guide | Authoritative | x | Live | 2026-01-01 |

| Upstream | Downstream |
| -------- | ---------- |
| a | b |`. It returns parsed metadata instead of rejecting the misplaced tables.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover the happy path and cases where a required table is entirely absent, but they do not include valid-looking tables preceded by prose or another block after the H1.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting ParseError when a paragraph or heading appears between the H1 and the metadata table, and another asserting ParseError when prose appears between the metadata and relationships tables.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.ts and packages/docs-meta/src/parser/parse-metadata.test.ts

items.title: rule panic isolation is not valid in release builds with panic=abort
items.recommendation: Either build the daemon/rule-execution path with panic="unwind" if catch_unwind is the intended boundary, or move rule execution behind a process boundary so aborting rules cannot terminate the daemon. Add the documented multi-process release fixture before treating the contract as covered.
items.reproduction: Run the daemon in a release profile configured with panic="abort" and install a rule equivalent to panicking_rule_service; sending rule_panic_request aborts the daemon process instead of returning the unwind-mode empty diagnostics response.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current Rust fixture explicitly pins only panic="unwind" behaviour under cargo test and documents the panic="abort" release path as an unimplemented follow-up.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-process release-profile test that starts the daemon with a panicking rule and asserts the expected release contract, either no daemon abort or a controlled child-process failure with daemon survival.
items.minimumFixScope: Release profile or rule-execution isolation strategy, plus the midedit_contract release-mode regression fixture.

items.title: Windows PID directory is created without ownership or permission validation
items.recommendation: Add a Windows-specific secure runtime directory verifier before PID/lock creation. It should reject reparse/symlink directories, verify the owner SID matches the current user, and ensure the DACL does not grant write/delete rights to untrusted principals. Reuse the existing Windows trusted-read/security helper if available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The PID directory security tests in lib.rs are cfg(unix), and the context tests exercise Unix sockets or dependency/parity contracts rather than Windows run_foreground startup with insecure PID parents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: On Windows, create a PID parent directory whose security descriptor permits broad write access or is a reparse point, then assert run_foreground(ForegroundOpts::with_pid_file(...)) fails before creating the PID file or lock. Also assert a current-user-owned private directory still starts successfully.
items.minimumFixScope: Implement Windows secure-directory validation in ensure_secure_runtime_dir and add Windows-specific tests for insecure DACL/reparse rejection.

items.title: stale PID recovery can remove a newly-created live PID file
items.recommendation: Serialise PID-file recovery and daemon ownership with an actual lock, or make recovery remove only the exact file identity that was inspected. On Unix, hold a lock file or locked open PID file across recovery and daemon lifetime; do not rely on a read/status/remove/create sequence alone.
items.reproduction: Start two run_foreground instances concurrently against the same stale PID file, with recovery interleaved so both read the stale record before either remove_file call completes. The second remover can unlink the first starter's replacement PID file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stale recovery and that Drop preserves an already-replaced PID file, but they do not run two stale-recovery attempts concurrently or force the interleaving between stale read, first recreate, and second remove.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test that uses two coordinated tasks/processes and an injected recovery hook to pause both after stale-status detection, then lets one recreate the PID file before the other attempts removal. Assert the live replacement is not removed and only one daemon proceeds.
items.minimumFixScope: PidFileGuard acquisition and stale PID recovery logic in crates/anvil-intercept/src/lib.rs, plus a targeted concurrent stale-recovery regression test.

items.title: OAuth route handlers lack regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add focused Vitest coverage for the auth route handlers: login should validate next, emit a GitHub authorize redirect, and set the nonce cookie; callback should cover missing params, invalid state, nonce mismatch, pending/error exchange results, and successful session cookie issuance.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the included files only show the package test command, not route-handler tests that exercise these auth branches.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create app/auth route-handler tests with mocked state and bauth helpers, asserting redirect targets and Set-Cookie attributes for success and failure branches.
items.minimumFixScope: Add auth route tests without changing production behavior unless the tests expose an implementation defect.

items.title: Crawler directives miss the exact /anvil route
items.recommendation: Add explicit entries for /anvil as well as /anvil/ in both robots.txt and llms.txt responses.
items.reproduction: Fetch /robots.txt or /llms.txt and compare the directives against the exact /anvil path; only /anvil/ is listed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were supplied for these route handlers, and there is no included assertion that crawler policy covers both the exact private docs root and descendants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Vitest route-handler test that calls the robots.txt and llms.txt GET handlers and asserts the response includes directives for both /anvil and /anvil/.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the BODY constants in app/robots.txt/route.ts and app/llms.txt/route.ts and add a focused route-handler test.

items.title: Exported package version is stale relative to the manifest
items.recommendation: Derive PACKAGE_VERSION from the release source of truth during build, or update the constant whenever package.json is bumped. Add a metadata regression test so release bumps cannot drift silently.
items.reproduction: Build or import the package root and compare PACKAGE_VERSION with packages/edda-stack/package.json version; the exported value is 0.1.0 while the manifest is 0.6.2-beta.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise config and contract modules directly through ./config.js or ./contracts/*.js imports. None of the included tests imports packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts or asserts that PACKAGE_VERSION matches the package manifest.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a root index metadata test that imports PACKAGE_VERSION and reads packages/edda-stack/package.json, then expects PACKAGE_VERSION to equal the manifest version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts metadata handling and add a package-root metadata test.

items.title: Root entrypoint eagerly couples contract consumers to service-layer runtime dependencies
items.recommendation: Keep the root entrypoint limited to lightweight contracts/config/package metadata, or replace service-layer root exports with explicit subpath-only imports (`@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/ember` and `/edda`). If root-level service exports must remain for compatibility, add a compatibility wrapper that does not force native service dependencies to load for contract-only imports.
items.reproduction: In a consumer that only needs contracts, import from the root package, for example `import { UuidSchema } from '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack'`, in an environment without native better-sqlite3 support. The root entrypoint still links the Ember service export path instead of limiting loading to contracts/config.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise contracts and configuration through relative source imports such as `./contracts/index.js` and `./config.js`; none import the package root entrypoint or verify contract-only root imports in a minimal/runtime-constrained consumer.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-entry test that imports a contract symbol from `src/index.ts` while mocking or excluding service-layer runtime dependencies, and assert that contract-only import succeeds without loading Ember/Edda storage modules.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `packages/edda-stack/src/index.ts` root exports and add one package-entry regression test.

items.title: Docusaurus CLI is used without declaring @docusaurus/core
items.recommendation: Add @docusaurus/core at the same 3.10.1 version as the other Docusaurus packages, refresh the lockfile, and verify the package build script from a clean install.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the included project metadata does not show a build/test target that proves the package-level Docusaurus scripts resolve their CLI dependency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/docs-public build` in CI or add an Nx build target for docs-public that executes the package build script.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/apps/docs-public/package.json plus the corresponding lockfile update

items.title: Index templates emit legacy Draft module status
items.recommendation: Change the template status examples to a canonical value, most likely `Proposed`, or use an explicit canonical placeholder such as `[Proposed|Ready|In Progress|Done|Blocked]`. Update the tests to assert the canonical value and reject `Draft` in generated index templates.
items.reproduction: Call `generateIndexTemplate()` or `generateIndexTemplate({ variant: 'full' })` and inspect the module metadata block; each sample module contains `- **Status:** Draft`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests only assert that a `**Status:**` field exists; they do not assert that the emitted status value is canonical.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add assertions for standard and full index templates that `template` contains `**Status:** Proposed` and does not contain `**Status:** Draft`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the standard and full index template literals in `generator.ts` and strengthen `generator.test.ts` status-value assertions.

items.title: Package test script can pass with zero contract tests
items.recommendation: Add focused schema tests for accepted and rejected response shapes, and make the package test command fail when no tests are discovered, for example by adding an explicit local Vitest include for `src/**/*.test.ts` and disabling pass-with-no-tests behaviour.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/admin-contracts test`; it exits 0 and reports `No test files found, exiting with code 0`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the package's current `vitest run` invocation reports zero discovered test files while still succeeding.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.test.ts` covering representative valid and invalid parses for each exported response schema, especially `SendMigrationResponseSchema`, timestamp coercion, nullable timestamps, and ID coercion.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the admin-contracts package test setup and add schema tests under `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src`.

items.title: Common registry is not covered by the linked registry tests
items.recommendation: Add a focused test file for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts that imports from ../../common or ../common as appropriate and covers duplicate registration, unregister/clear behavior, getAdapterForFormat, listSupportedFormats, and detectFormat.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current linked tests target packages/adapters/src/base/registry.ts through a relative import from packages/adapters/src/base/__tests__, so they do not instantiate or assert the common AdapterRegistry implementation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create packages/adapters/src/common/__tests__/registry.test.ts with a mock SpecToolAdapter and assertions for register, duplicate register error, unregister, getAdapterForFormat, listSupportedFormats, clear, and detectFormat.
items.minimumFixScope: Add direct unit coverage for packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts and include it in the existing packages/adapters vitest run.

items.title: Published architecture template loader loses its YAML templates
items.recommendation: Make template assets part of the build output, for example by copying `src/architecture/templates/*.yaml` to `dist/architecture/templates` during build/pack, or embed the template data in TypeScript so no runtime file asset is required.
items.reproduction: Run the package build, then execute the built `dist/architecture/templates/index.js` API and call `getTemplate('layered')`; it attempts to read `dist/architecture/templates/layered.yaml`, which the `tsc` build does not emit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The template tests run against the source tree where the YAML files exist beside `src/architecture/templates/index.ts`; they do not exercise the built or packed package layout.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a post-build/package-layout test that imports the built architecture template module from `dist` and calls `getTemplate` for every built-in template.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the core package build/packaging path for architecture template YAML assets and add a built-output smoke test.

items.title: Architecture baseline inference follows symlinked directories out of the workspace
items.recommendation: Use `lstatSync` to skip symlinked entries by default, or resolve realpaths and enforce that descendants remain inside `workspaceRoot` while tracking visited directories to avoid cycles.
items.reproduction: Create a workspace containing a symlinked directory such as `src/outside -> /some/large/tree` or `src/loop -> ..`, then call `inferBaseline(workspaceRoot)`. The walker follows the symlink because `statSync` reports the target directory.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The analyzer tests cover normal filtering and missing/unreadable paths, but they do not create symlinked directories or cyclic directory structures for `inferBaseline`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an `inferBaseline` test with a symlinked directory pointing outside the temp workspace and assert the collected module count excludes files behind the symlink.
items.minimumFixScope: Harden `collectSourceFiles` in `packages/anvil/core/src/architecture/analyzer.ts` and add symlink traversal coverage.

items.title: Documented .anvil compiler API is not reachable from package consumers
items.recommendation: Either add an `./anvil-format` entry to `package.json` exports and keep its declarations in dist, or re-export the anvil-format barrel from `src/index.ts` if it is intended to be part of the root API. If it is intentionally internal, update the README so it does not describe the compiler as active package surface.
items.reproduction: Install or pack the package, then try `import { compilePatterns } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core/anvil-format'`; Node will reject the unexported subpath. Trying the root import also fails because `src/index.ts` does not re-export the symbol.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The compiler tests import `compilePatterns` via `./compile.js`, so they validate implementation behaviour but not package-level importability through `package.json` exports or the root barrel.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package API smoke test that imports `@eddacraft/anvil-core/anvil-format` from the built package output and asserts `compilePatterns` is exported.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/anvil/core/package.json` exports and/or `packages/anvil/core/src/index.ts`, plus one public API smoke test.

items.title: Generated dependency-cruiser config is CommonJS despite using a .js filename
items.recommendation: Emit a `.cjs` config filename for CommonJS output, or generate ESM syntax when the target workspace is ESM. Keep the consumer command/config path in sync with the chosen extension.
items.reproduction: Use `compileArchitecture` in a project with `package.json` containing `"type":"module"`, then load the generated `.anvil/dependency-cruiser.js` with Node/dependency-cruiser. The file is parsed as ESM but contains CommonJS assignment.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The dc-generator tests parse the returned string to inspect JSON rule content; they do not execute or load the generated config under an ESM package boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that creates a temp workspace with `package.json` set to `type: module`, runs `writeDCConfig`, and verifies the generated file can be loaded by the intended dependency-cruiser loading path.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `DC_CONFIG_FILENAME`/generated module syntax and update tests around generated config loadability.

items.title: Docs access can resolve enabled without an authenticated subject
items.recommendation: Fail closed before calling resolveFlag when sessionSubject is null, missing, or empty, or make sessionSubject required for enabled evaluations and only attach accountTier after a valid subject is present.
items.reproduction: Call evaluateDocsAccess({ accountTier: 'beta', sessionSubject: null }) in an environment where docs.access targets eligible account tiers; the helper builds an anon-visitor context with the beta audience and can return variant='enabled'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the available code in this feature does not include a docs-site regression test for missing sessionSubject paired with an eligible accountTier.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused evaluateDocsAccess test asserting that beta, pro, and enterprise tiers return disabled when sessionSubject is null, omitted, or empty, and enabled only when paired with a non-empty subject.
items.minimumFixScope: Update .claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/apps/docs-site/lib/feature-flags.ts to fail closed for missing or empty sessionSubject and add a focused docs-site unit test.

items.title: validateNext drops query strings and fragments from accepted redirects
items.recommendation: Validate against the normalised pathname, but return pathname plus search plus hash for accepted same-site /anvil targets. Keep rejecting protocol-relative and non-/anvil URLs.
items.reproduction: Call validateNext('/anvil/search?q=policy#results'); it returns '/anvil/search' rather than preserving the same-document search and fragment.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: next-url.test.ts only asserts accepted and rejected pathnames; it has no case for a valid /anvil redirect containing search params or a hash fragment.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add expectations for validateNext('/anvil/search?q=policy') === '/anvil/search?q=policy' and validateNext('/anvil/overview#install') === '/anvil/overview#install', plus a rejected non-/anvil query case if needed.
items.minimumFixScope: Update validateNext return construction and add targeted tests in next-url.test.ts.

items.title: Package build script points at a TypeScript config that is not part of the package metadata under review
items.recommendation: Either change the build script to `tsc -p tsconfig.json` if this package only has the shown config, or add and include a package-local tsconfig.lib.json that extends tsconfig.json and is covered by the project metadata.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-flags-catalogue build` in a checkout where packages/anvil/flags-catalogue/tsconfig.lib.json is absent; TypeScript will fail to find the referenced project file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked Vitest suites import from `../src/index.js` and validate runtime catalogue behaviour; none invokes the package `build` script or verifies that `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` are generated.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package/build validation target or CI check that runs `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-flags-catalogue build` and verifies the exported dist files exist.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/flags-catalogue/package.json plus either the existing TypeScript config reference or a new package-local build tsconfig.

items.title: Concurrent updates for different tasks can overwrite state.json entries
items.recommendation: Serialize all state.json read-modify-write operations with a project-level state lock, or store each task's mutable state independently and compose reads. Keep the per-task lock for first-lock-wins semantics, but make state persistence transactional for concurrent different-task updates.
items.reproduction: Start two TaskLocker.lock calls for different tasks from the same empty project state, with both calls reaching updateTaskState before either write is observed by the other. The final .anvil/state.json can contain only one of the two task entries while both .anvil/locks/*.lock files exist.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included TaskLocker concurrency test only races several lockers against TEST-001, where the per-task lock correctly allows one winner. It never races successful locks for TEST-001 and TEST-002, which is the path that exercises shared state.json lost updates.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TaskLocker test that concurrently locks TEST-001 and TEST-002, then asserts state.json contains locked records for both tasks and both tasks can be completed or unlocked successfully. Use a controllable state-write barrier or injected filesystem helper if needed to make the read-modify-write interleaving deterministic.
items.minimumFixScope: Change updateTaskState/writeStateFile call sites in the state module so state.json mutations are serialized across all task IDs, then add a different-task concurrency regression test.

items.title: Unlock deletes the execution plan before the cancellation state is durable
items.recommendation: Make unlock order failure-safe: first persist a recoverable transition or write a tombstone, then delete the execution plan only after the state transition is durable, or restore the execution plan/state on failure. At minimum, do not leave a locked state pointing at a deleted execution file.
items.reproduction: Lock a task, then make .anvil/state.json unwritable or otherwise force updateTaskState to throw during unlock after deleteExecutionPlan succeeds. unlock returns success:false, but the execution plan file has already been removed while the task remains locked in state.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The unlock tests only cover the successful path and assert the plan is gone after a completed unlock. They do not inject a writeStateFile or releaseLockFile failure between deleting the plan and finishing the state transition.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that locks a task, forces the state update in unlock to fail after deleteExecutionPlan would run, and asserts either the execution plan remains available or the state no longer points at a missing execution file.
items.minimumFixScope: Rework TaskLocker.unlock ordering and error handling, plus add a failure-path test around state-write failure during unlock.

items.title: Heading slug generation can reject valid rendered anchors
items.recommendation: Use the same slugger as the Markdown renderer or a tested GitHub-compatible slugger package instead of maintaining a partial local implementation. Add fixture coverage for punctuation, duplicate headings, inline code, and non-ASCII heading text.
items.reproduction: Create a Markdown heading such as `## A & B` and link to the renderer-generated anchor form that preserves the double separator; the local `slugify` collapses the generated slug to `a-b`, so the checker does not recognise the rendered anchor.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for `check-links.mjs`, and the bug only appears for headings whose rendered anchor differs from the simplified local slug algorithm.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add link-check fixtures with punctuation-heavy headings, including `A & B` and duplicate headings, and assert that anchors matching the project renderer are accepted.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace or harden `slugify` and its duplicate-heading handling in `check-links.mjs`.

items.title: Glob source references can bypass the repository-root escape check
items.recommendation: Resolve each glob pattern relative to root, reject absolute or parent-traversing glob patterns before calling globby, or validate every globby match with the same `relPath(root, targetAbs)` repository-root check used for non-glob references.
items.reproduction: Add a governed As-built or Runbook source reference containing an escaping glob such as `../*` on a machine where the parent directory has entries, then run `node scripts/docs/check-asbuilt-paths.mjs --no-baseline`; the glob branch treats the reference as valid instead of reporting that it escapes the repository root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the current code path has separate glob and non-glob handling, so tests that cover only literal path escapes would not exercise the early return.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture governed Runbook/As-built document with source references for `../*` and `/tmp/*` and assert that `check-asbuilt-paths.mjs --no-baseline` emits an ERROR for repository escape rather than accepting the glob when it matches.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `resolveSourcePath` in `check-asbuilt-paths.mjs` to apply repository-root validation to glob patterns before accepting matches.

items.title: Targeting rules can reference variants that do not exist
items.recommendation: In FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check, build the set of variant keys and validate every targeting rule's variant against it, emitting an issue at ['targeting', ruleIndex, 'variant'] when it is unknown.
items.reproduction: FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse(validFlag({ targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'missing' }] })) currently succeeds even though 'missing' is not in variants.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover defaultVariant reference validation and valid targeting rules, but there is no negative test for a targeting rule whose variant is absent from variants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema with targeting test that uses variant: 'nonexistent' and expects safeParse(...).success to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the feature flag schema tests.

items.title: Parser accepts governance tables that are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Make the table collection adjacency-aware: after locating the H1, skip only ignorable whitespace-equivalent nodes if any are represented, require the next top-level node to be the metadata table and the following top-level node to be the relationships table, and stop before any intervening paragraph, heading, list, code block, or other non-table content.
items.reproduction:
Parse a document shaped as `# Title

Intro prose before metadata.

| Type | Authority | Owner | Status | Freshness |
| ---- | --------- | ----- | ------ | --------- |
| Guide | Authoritative | x | Live | 2026-01-01 |

| Upstream | Downstream |
| -------- | ---------- |
| a | b |`; the current implementation will accept it even though the tables are not immediately after the H1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The happy-path fixtures place both tables immediately after the H1, and the missing-table tests only cover absence of tables, not intervening non-table content before otherwise valid tables.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that puts a paragraph or subheading between the H1 and an otherwise valid metadata table and asserts parseDocGovernance throws a ParseError about the missing governance metadata table after H1.
items.minimumFixScope: Update collectTablesAfterH1 or its caller to enforce immediate top-level table adjacency after the H1, then add focused parser tests for intervening prose and intervening headings.

items.title: domainImports validation accepts import IDs for the wrong domain
items.recommendation: Parse the import ID and require its final domain segment to exactly equal the domainImports key. Keep accepting both project-only and team-prefixed forms.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests cover malformed IDs and keys absent from domains, but they do not cover a syntactically valid import ID whose domain suffix disagrees with the map key.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a VercelApp domainImports test asserting {'example.com': 'prj_test123abc/other.com'} throws a clear mismatch error.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts and the domainImports test block.

items.title: Default Vercel ignore command interpolates path arguments into shell without robust quoting
items.recommendation: Validate rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths with the same conservative path character policy, or build the command using a shell-escaping helper for every dynamic argument.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only exercise safe literal paths and the productionBranch metacharacter rejection. They do not assert escaping or rejection for rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that reject or correctly escape rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths containing spaces, semicolons, double quotes, and single quotes.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts and focused VercelApp ignoreCommand tests.

items.title: Per-operator admin keys are not reprovisioned when the pepper rotates
items.recommendation: Include the pepper input in the replacement trigger set, or create a rotation-specific resource/action that revokes and recreates each per-operator key when the pepper changes. Keep the database row command and API env var rotation coupled.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only assert that ADMIN_KEY_PEPPER is wired into the Vercel app and remains sensitive; there is no test for PerOperatorAdminKey trigger inputs or pepper-rotation behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Pulumi mock test for PerOperatorAdminKey that inspects the command.local.Command inputs and asserts ADMIN_KEY_PEPPER participates in the replacement triggers or equivalent rotation mechanism.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/infra/src/components/per-operator-admin-key.ts plus a focused admin-key component test.

items.title: Security page publishes a placeholder PGP fingerprint
items.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with the real key fingerprint, or remove the encrypted-communications instruction until the key and fingerprint are published together and verified.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and static page content assertions would be needed to catch placeholder security contact material.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a page/content test that renders the security page and asserts the PGP fingerprint matches the expected non-placeholder fingerprint format/value.
items.minimumFixScope: Update .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-001/apps/website/app/security/page.tsx and, if necessary, the corresponding public key asset so the fingerprint and key agree.

items.title: Successful but malformed verify responses are reported as invalid access keys
items.recommendation: Treat JSON parse failures and missing required fields on an otherwise successful upstream response as access_service_unavailable, or another 5xx contract error, while reserving invalid_key for explicit valid:false/isEdict:false responses.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route; the edge case requires a mocked 200 response with invalid JSON or missing fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Mock fetch to return ok: true with invalid JSON, and separately ok: true with {}, then assert the route returns a 503-style service/contract error rather than invalid_key.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the response parsing branch in .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-001/apps/website/app/api/early-access/install/route.ts and add route-level tests for malformed 2xx verify responses.

items.title: Structured debug payloads bypass redaction
items.recommendation: Sanitise structured payloads before passing them to `console.debug`. A minimal fix is to serialize unknown objects through a safe redacting replacer or recursively clone primitives/arrays/plain objects while applying `sanitizeForLog` to string values and known secret-bearing keys.
items.reproduction: Set `ANVIL_DEBUG=1`, call `createDebugger('api')('request', { authorization: 'Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345' })`, and observe that `console.debug` receives the unredacted object as its second argument.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests do not include `debug.ts`, and no test spies on `console.debug` with object payloads while debug logging is enabled.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `debug.test.ts` case that enables `ANVIL_DEBUG`, logs an object containing a Bearer token and API-key-like value, and asserts the `console.debug` arguments contain `[REDACTED]` and not the original secret.
items.minimumFixScope: `apps/anvil-api/src/lib/debug.ts` plus focused unit coverage for string, Error, and object payload redaction.

items.title: Licence verification returns malformed claims as `LicenceClaims`
items.recommendation: Validate every claim that is returned through the `LicenceClaims` interface: `identity` must be an object with `provider: string` and `id: string | null`, `org` must be `string | null` when present, `tier` must be a string, `scopes` must be an array of strings, and `seats` should be a finite positive integer if present. Return `null` for malformed signed payloads.
items.reproduction: Sign a JWT with the configured test private key containing `email: 'a@b.com'`, `scopes: [123]`, and `identity: 'bad'`, plus the correct issuer/audience/expiry. `verifyLicence` will return a non-null object instead of rejecting the malformed claims.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The licence tests cover missing `scopes`, but they do not cover malformed claim types inside otherwise valid signed JWTs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `licence.test.ts` with signed JWTs that have `scopes: [123]`, `identity: 'github'`, and `seats: '1'`, and assert `verifyLicence` returns `null` for each malformed payload.
items.minimumFixScope: `apps/anvil-api/src/lib/licence.ts` claim validation and targeted `verifyLicence` regression tests.

items.title: Top-level rustdoc incorrectly says the 80-writer stress test is ignored
items.recommendation: Update the `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs` deferred follow-up text to match the current test state, or remove the deferred follow-up entirely if MLP2-015 completed it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests exercise writer concurrency behaviour, but they do not validate rustdoc accuracy or cross-document consistency.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the stale crate-level documentation in `crates/anvil-witness/src/lib.rs`.

items.title: Package build script points at a non-owned TypeScript config
items.recommendation: Align the build script with the owned configuration, for example `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, or add and own a package-local tsconfig.lib.json that extends tsconfig.json and is included in the package review surface.
items.reproduction: From packages/anvil/observability, run `pnpm build` or `tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json`; if tsconfig.lib.json is absent, TypeScript exits with a missing config error and no dist files are produced.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suite exercises runtime traceparent parsing and envelope helpers only. It does not invoke the package build script or assert that the configured TypeScript project can emit the exported dist files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level build validation in CI/Nx that runs the observability package build target and verifies `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` are emitted.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/observability/package.json build script or a package-local tsconfig.lib.json plus build validation.

items.title: BMAD serializer emits unknown metadata values as document text
items.recommendation: Read BMAD metadata through narrow helpers, e.g. use typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0 before interpolation, otherwise fall back to docs/PRD.md and Project.
items.reproduction: Serialize an APS plan with metadata: { outputFile: { path: 'docs/PRD.md' }, projectName: 123 }. The BMAD output contains output_file: "{project-root}/[object Object]" and '# 123 - Product Requirements Document'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked serializer type-safety tests cover serializeToGeneric only. There are no corresponding BMAD serializer tests for non-string outputFile or projectName metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add BMAD serializer tests that pass non-string outputFile and projectName metadata and assert the output falls back to docs/PRD.md and Project rather than stringifying the values.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/serializer.ts plus BMAD serializer metadata type-safety tests.

items.title: BMAD input size guard counts UTF-16 units instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for the BMAD size check, matching the generic parser guard.
items.reproduction: Call parseBMADDocument('\u{1F600}'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)). Buffer.byteLength exceeds 2 MiB, but content.length remains under the current limit, so the maximum-size error is not thrown.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked byte-length regression tests target parseGeneric only. There is no equivalent BMAD test for multi-byte input at the 2 MiB boundary.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parser test mirroring packages/adapters/src/generic/__tests__/parser.test.ts that asserts parseBMADDocument rejects multi-byte content whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds MAX_INPUT_SIZE while content.length does not.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts plus a BMAD-specific parser regression test.

items.title: Invalid structured BMAD YAML paths are silently dropped from successful parses
items.recommendation: Make bmadToAPS surface conversion diagnostics. At minimum, throw when errors.length > 0 so BMADFormatAdapter.parse returns createParseError; alternatively return a richer internal result and pass warnings/errors through the adapter result.
items.reproduction: Parse an agent YAML document with metadata.id set to '../escape.md' and required metadata/persona fields present. safePath throws, bmadToAPS catches it into errors, then returns an APS plan without the agent change; BMADFormatAdapter.parse reports success.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests are for generic parsing/serialization. Existing BMAD path tests only cover requirement-ID generated paths and do not exercise structured YAML path fields such as agent metadata.id, menu workflow paths, module code, or module directories.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD adapter test with valid agent YAML except metadata.id: '../escape.md' and assert parse returns success false with an INVALID_PATH error, or returns a warning/error if the chosen contract permits partial parses.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/bmad/parser.ts and packages/adapters/src/bmad/format-adapter.ts parse result plumbing, plus structured-YAML invalid-path tests.

items.title: Warning result consistency check ignores blocking, suppressed, and category totals
items.recommendation: Extend validateWarningResultConsistency to recompute and compare byCategory, suppressed, blocking, and all expected severity buckets. Prefer comparing against createWarningResult(result.warnings).summary so the helper and producer stay aligned.
items.reproduction: Create a WarningResult with one unsuppressed error warning and summary.blocking set to 0, or mutate createWarningResult([errorWarning]).summary.blocking = 0; validateWarningResultConsistency still returns true as long as total and supplied bySeverity entries match.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for the contracts warning helpers, and the discovered validation tests only exercise APS plan validation/createPlan hash handling, not WarningResult consistency.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a WarningResult helper test that mutates each derived summary field (byCategory, bySeverity omission, suppressed, blocking) and expects validateWarningResultConsistency to return false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/contracts/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus focused tests for warning result consistency

items.title: Exported registry can diverge from reset singleton state
items.recommendation: Avoid exporting a cached singleton object, or make reset semantics explicit. Prefer exporting a `getRegistry()` accessor, removing `resetInstance`, or changing reset/clear behaviour so all public singleton access paths continue to refer to the same registry state.
items.reproduction: Import `{ registry, AdapterRegistry }`, register an adapter on `registry`, call `AdapterRegistry.resetInstance()`, then compare `registry.size` with `AdapterRegistry.getInstance().size`; the exported registry still contains the old state while the singleton instance is empty.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included singleton test only compares two `AdapterRegistry.getInstance()` calls after reset. It never imports or asserts the exported `registry` object, so the split public state is untested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a registry test that imports the exported `registry`, calls `AdapterRegistry.resetInstance()`, then asserts the public singleton access path cannot diverge from `AdapterRegistry.getInstance()`.
items.minimumFixScope: Registry export/reset contract in `src/base/registry.ts`, plus the registry singleton tests.

items.title: Regex utility helpers miscount common pattern inputs
items.recommendation: Reset `lastIndex` before/after testing RegExp inputs or use a cloned non-stateful RegExp for matching. In `countOccurrences`, escape string patterns for literal counting, and clone RegExp inputs while preserving their flags and ensuring `g` is present.
items.reproduction: `const r = /foo/g; matchesPatterns('foo', [r]); matchesPatterns('foo', [r])` returns different counts. `countOccurrences('a.b axb', 'a.b')` counts both `a.b` and `axb`; `countOccurrences('Foo foo', /foo/i)` ignores the case-insensitive flag.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover registry behaviour only. There are no tests for `matchesPatterns` or `countOccurrences`, and no adapter test exercises global regex reuse, literal metacharacter strings, or regex flags.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add utility tests for repeated `matchesPatterns` calls with `/foo/g`, literal string counting with metacharacters, and `countOccurrences` preserving `/i` flag behaviour.
items.minimumFixScope: Regex handling in `src/base/utils.ts`, with focused utility tests.

items.title: Failed watcher startup leaves the multi-agent watch lock alive
items.recommendation: Wrap the post-initialize startup sequence in try/catch and cleanup concurrencyContext and the partially-started watcher on any failure before rethrowing. Alternatively set a separate lifecycle state so stop() always cleans up an initialized concurrency context even when start() did not complete.
items.reproduction: Mock createConcurrencyContext with cleanup and lock renewal spies, mock FileWatcher.start to reject, call new WatchOrchestrator(...default multiAgent...).start(), then assert cleanup was not called and stop() still does not call it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover FileWatcher startup behaviour and git/debouncer helpers, but there is no orchestrator test exercising start failure after multi-agent initialisation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an orchestrator test where multi-agent initialisation succeeds, FileWatcher.start rejects, and the test asserts concurrencyContext.cleanup() is called and a subsequent stop() is harmless.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/orchestrator.ts startup error handling plus an orchestrator regression test.

items.title: Git octal path decoding corrupts non-ASCII filenames
items.recommendation: Prefer `git status --porcelain -z` and parse NUL-delimited raw paths, including rename records, to avoid quote decoding entirely. If keeping quoted parsing, collect octal escapes as bytes and decode them with UTF-8 TextDecoder instead of String.fromCharCode per byte.
items.reproduction: Mock gitExec to return ` M "caf\303\251.md"\n`, then call filterUnstaged([resolve('/repo', 'café.md')]). The parser produces `/repo/cafÃ©.md`, so the input path is filtered out.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The git-status tests cover quoted ASCII paths with spaces and rename arrows, but they do not include octal-escaped multi-byte filenames.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for getFileStatus, filterUnstaged, and getChangedFiles using mocked porcelain output with UTF-8 octal escapes such as `caf\303\251.md`, asserting the returned path is `café.md` and that filterUnstaged matches the Unicode input path.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/watch/git-status.ts path parsing plus git-status regression tests for non-ASCII filenames.

items.title: Plugin metadata version is stale
items.recommendation: Keep plugin.meta.version in sync with package.json, preferably by generating or importing it from package metadata during build if the project supports that pattern.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included rule tests exercise only individual rules; there is no test for the exported plugin object or its metadata.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index test that imports the plugin and asserts plugin.meta.name and plugin.meta.version match package.json.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/eslint-plugin-anvil/src/index.ts and add focused coverage for the exported plugin metadata.

items.title: README examples reference public symbols that are not exported
items.recommendation: Either add compatibility aliases for the documented names or update the README examples to use the exported symbols, for example `SpecKitFormatAdapter` or `createSpecKitAdapter`, and `discoverPlanningFiles` or `findBestPlanningFile`.
items.reproduction: Type-check a consumer file containing the README examples; TypeScript reports that `SpecKitAdapter` and `findPlanningDocuments` are not exported by the referenced modules.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests verify concrete adapter classes directly and do not compile README snippets or assert that documented public symbol names exist.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a documentation snippet smoke test, or a small public API test, that imports every symbol shown in the README from the package entrypoints.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/adapters/README.md` and, if backwards-compatible aliases are desired, update the relevant module index exports.

items.title: Documented subpath imports are not exposed by the package export map
items.recommendation: Add explicit exports for the documented subpaths, including declaration mappings, for example `./speckit`, `./bmad`, `./generic`, `./aps-markdown`, and any utility entrypoints that are intended to be public. Alternatively, change the README to only document root imports.
items.reproduction: After building or installing the package, run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad')"`; with the current exports map, Node rejects the subpath because only `.` is exported.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included adapter tests import implementation files by relative source paths, such as `../speckit/format-adapter.js`, `../bmad/format-adapter.js`, and `../generic/format-adapter.js`; they never exercise the built package export map or documented package subpaths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level smoke test that builds the adapters package and dynamically imports each documented public entrypoint from the package name, including `@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/bmad`, `@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/generic`, and `@eddacraft/anvil-adapters/speckit`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `packages/adapters/package.json` exports and ensure the build emits matching JS and `.d.ts` files for each exported subpath.

items.title: SpecKit v2 imports build APS paths from unsanitised scenario titles
items.recommendation: Convert scenario titles with a strict slugifier that only permits safe path segment characters, reject empty or traversal-like slugs, and pass the final path through validateRelativePath before adding it to an APS Change.
items.reproduction: Import a v2 SpecKit ExternalSpec whose spec.md contains '### P1: ../../../outside' under '## User Scenarios & Testing'. The resulting APS plan includes a file_create change with an unsanitised traversal-bearing path derived from that title.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file only covers the generic parser input-size guard and does not exercise SpecKit v2 scenario-to-path conversion.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SpecKitImportAdapterV2 test that imports a P1 scenario titled '../../../outside' and asserts conversion fails or emits a safe validated slug path without '..' segments.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitImportAdapterV2.inferPathFromScenario and tests for v2 import path derivation.

items.title: Imported and generated SpecKit plans can reuse the same APS id for several seconds
items.recommendation: Use a deterministic content-based id for imports, as SpecKitFormatAdapter already does with generateDeterministicPlanId(content), or use a collision-resistant id generator that preserves enough entropy.
items.reproduction: Call either import adapter's convertToAPS twice in quick succession with different input specs; both calls can return an APSPlan with the same 'aps-...' id.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not instantiate either SpecKit import adapter or assert uniqueness/determinism of generated APS ids.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that convert two different SpecKit specs in the same mocked timestamp bucket and assert their APS ids differ, or assert the id is derived from content.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace Date.now().toString(16).substring(0, 8) in both SpecKit import adapters and add import id tests.

items.title: Exporting an APS plan with no changes produces NaN progress
items.recommendation: Guard the zero-task case and emit 0% progress, omit the progress percentage, or fail export if empty changes are not supported.
items.reproduction: Call SpecKitExportAdapter.convertFromAPS with an APSPlan whose proposed_changes array is empty; the returned tasksContent includes '- Progress: NaN%'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no included SpecKit export tests; the provided test file only exercises generic parser size limits.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an export test for an APSPlan with proposed_changes: [] and assert tasksContent contains a deterministic non-NaN progress value or that export returns a validation error.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitExportAdapter.generateTasksMarkdown zero-task handling and a focused export regression test.
