items.title: SpecKit parser enforces the 2 MiB limit by UTF-16 length instead of bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') or a shared byte-length guard helper for SpecKit parsing, matching the generic parser's tested semantics.
items.reproduction: Call new SpecKitParser().parseSpecMarkdown('\u{1F600}'.repeat(Math.floor((2 * 1024 * 1024) / 4) + 1)); its UTF-16 length is under the limit while its UTF-8 byte length exceeds it, so the guard does not reject it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided tests cover parseGeneric only; there is no SpecKitParser test for ASCII or multi-byte size limits.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add SpecKitParser tests mirroring the generic parser byte-limit cases, including multi-byte content whose string length is below the limit but byte length exceeds it.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitParser.parseSpecMarkdown size check and focused parser tests.

items.title: Format adapter silently drops non-file APS changes during serialization
items.recommendation: Serialize every APS Change type supported by the adapter, or reject unsupported types with a serialize error instead of producing lossy markdown.
items.reproduction: Serialize an APSPlan whose only proposed change is { type: 'dependency_add', path: 'package.json', description: 'Install x' }. The output contains an empty Changes section and no dependency change.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests are for the generic parser and do not cover SpecKitFormatAdapter serialization or round-tripping of non-file changes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a serialize or round-trip test with dependency_add, config_update, and script_execute changes and assert they appear in the SpecKit markdown or produce an explicit unsupported-type error.
items.minimumFixScope: SpecKitFormatAdapter.serialize change grouping plus serialization tests for all supported Change types.

items.title: Anvil docs path is exposed without an authentication gate in the reviewed shell
items.recommendation: Add a middleware/proxy guard for /anvil/:path* that reads anvil-docs-session, verifies it with verifyLicense, redirects unauthenticated users to /auth/login?next=<validated path>, and only forwards/serves the private docs after a valid token. Keep robots/noindex as indexing defence only, not as auth.
items.reproduction: Request /anvil/overview without an anvil-docs-session cookie. The reviewed package contains no middleware, route handler, rewrite, or proxy guard that would call getCookie/verifyLicense before serving or forwarding that path; next.config.ts only sets a noindex header for /anvil/:path*.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover helper-level behaviour for cookies, JWTs, OAuth state, and next URL validation, but there are no route or middleware tests asserting that unauthenticated /anvil requests are redirected or rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Next route/middleware test or integration test that requests /anvil/overview without an anvil-docs-session cookie and expects a redirect to /auth/login, then repeats with a valid signed beta/pro/enterprise token and expects the protected docs path to proceed.
items.minimumFixScope: Add and test the /anvil/:path* authentication enforcement path; update configuration only as needed to ensure the guard runs before any private docs content is served.

items.title: Real-send migration responses can silently include the dry-run discriminator
items.recommendation: Make the send branch reject discriminator drift, for example by adding `dryRun: z.never().optional()` with strict object handling, or by using a stricter object policy/refinement that fails when `dryRun` is present on real-send responses.
items.reproduction: Parse a payload like `{ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }` with `SendMigrationResponseSchema`; the dry-run branch fails because dry-run-specific fields are absent, then the send branch succeeds after stripping `dryRun`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and there is no evidence of a contract test asserting that real-send responses reject a `dryRun` property.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a schema test asserting `SendMigrationResponseSchema.safeParse({ dryRun: true, source: 'manual', total: 1, sent: 1, failed: 0, results: [] }).success` is false, and another asserting the normal real-send shape without `dryRun` still succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `SendResponseSchema` or `SendMigrationResponseSchema` in `packages/shared/admin-contracts/src/index.ts` and add focused contract coverage for the migration response discriminator.

items.title: Admin key create path is not atomic under concurrent provisioning
items.recommendation: Enforce uniqueness at the database boundary, preferably with a partial unique index on active actor_email rows, and make the script use an atomic insert/upsert or a per-actor transaction lock such as pg_advisory_xact_lock before checking/inserting. Keep the audit insert in the same transaction.
items.reproduction: Run two admin-key-manage.mjs create invocations concurrently against an empty admin_keys table for the same ACTOR_EMAIL with different BEARER_HEX values; both can pass the pre-insert SELECT before either INSERT commits.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included infra tests exercise DNS and Vercel resource generation only; none execute admin-key-manage.mjs against a database or simulate concurrent creates.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a database-backed test that launches two concurrent create operations for the same actor with different bearers and asserts exactly one succeeds or one active row remains.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/scripts/admin-key-manage.mjs plus the admin_keys schema/migration if the active-row uniqueness constraint is not already present.

items.title: domainImports accepts import IDs for a different domain
items.recommendation: Parse the import ID into optional team ID, project ID, and domain segments, then reject values whose domain segment does not exactly equal the domainImports key. Also reject import IDs with extra slash-delimited segments after the domain.
items.reproduction: Instantiate VercelApp with domains: ['www.example.com'] and domainImports: { 'www.example.com': 'prj_abc123/api.example.com' }; construction succeeds and passes the mismatched import ID through to ProjectDomain.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests cover keys absent from domains, malformed IDs, and a valid team-prefixed ID, but they do not assert that the domain embedded in the import ID matches the map key.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a VercelApp domainImports test that expects { 'www.example.com': 'prj_test123abc/api.example.com' } to throw a domain mismatch error.
items.minimumFixScope: infra/src/components/vercel-app.ts validation plus infra/src/__tests__/vercel-app.test.ts coverage.

items.title: scan_artifact_json does not catch registry-load panics
items.recommendation: Move the registry load into the same catch_unwind block as scan_artifact_rust, or wrap the whole scan_artifact_json implementation after JSON argument validation so registry panics are converted through panic_to_error.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The referenced registry-missing test covers ordinary load errors returned as Result values, but it does not exercise a panic from registry loading or mapping on scan_artifact_json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Node integration test or Rust-side injectable loader test that forces the scan entrypoint's registry-load path to panic and asserts scanArtifactJson throws a JS Error instead of aborting the process.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-checks-napi/src/lib.rs scan_artifact_json panic boundary

items.title: General rate limiter trusts caller-controlled X-Forwarded-For as the bucket key
items.recommendation: Derive the client address from a trusted runtime/proxy source, or normalise X-Forwarded-For only after confirming the request came through a trusted proxy that overwrites it. If no trusted client IP is available, prefer a conservative shared bucket or combine the key with another authenticated/connection-level signal.
items.reproduction: Send repeated requests with different X-Forwarded-For values, for example 1.1.1.1, then 1.1.1.2, etc. Each value creates a fresh bucket, so the configured max is never reached for a single chosen bucket.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover adminRateLimit and traceContext only; there is no test for rateLimiter's client identity selection or spoofed X-Forwarded-For behaviour.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a rateLimiter test that mounts max: 1, sends two requests with different untrusted X-Forwarded-For values, and asserts the second is still limited unless the request is marked as coming from a trusted proxy path.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts client-key derivation and add focused tests for spoofed forwarded headers.

items.title: Client-controlled X-Forwarded-For can bypass the generic rate limiter
items.recommendation: Derive the client identifier only from a trusted platform source or from a sanitised header installed by a trusted proxy. If X-Forwarded-For must be used, document the required proxy behaviour and parse the trusted hop rather than blindly trusting the leftmost client-provided value.
items.reproduction: Send more than max requests while varying the X-Forwarded-For header value on each request; each distinct value creates a distinct entry in the in-memory store and avoids the cap.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked admin-rate-limit tests exercise actor-based admin buckets only. They do not cover the generic IP limiter or spoofed/rotated X-Forwarded-For headers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a rateLimiter test that makes repeated requests with different client-supplied X-Forwarded-For values under a simulated untrusted-header path, then assert the limiter either ignores those values or uses a trusted request identity consistently.
items.minimumFixScope: Update apps/anvil-api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts to use a trusted client IP source or configurable extractor, and add focused tests for spoofed X-Forwarded-For handling.

items.title: Filtered initial-scan tests pass if matching files are all dropped
items.recommendation: Tighten the filtered initial-scan assertions to require exactly one tracked source file for these fixtures, or assert the retained file identity if the snapshot payload exposes it.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests accept 0 as success for the filtered cases, so complete over-filtering is indistinguishable from correctly dropping only the excluded/non-included file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change both filtered initial-scan tests to assert max_files == 1 for the current fixture, and keep the existing no-filter max_files == 2 control.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-kernel/tests/watch_pattern_filter.rs filtered initial-scan assertions.

items.title: Dual-run parity harness cannot validate the TS engine
items.recommendation: Wire run_dual to the real TS engine output or mark this as an ignored/pending harness until integration exists. Once wired, assert at least one fixture where both engines produce matching non-empty records and one fixture where a known discrepancy is reported from real TS output.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests assert that the placeholder stays empty, so they exercise serialization/comparison mechanics but not parity against the TS engine.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that invokes the real TS architecture checker for a fixture with a known cross-layer violation and asserts the Rust and TS ViolationRecord sets match.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-kernel/tests/dual_run.rs plus whatever adapter is needed to obtain real TS checker results.

items.title: TODO markdown documents can be rejected before the parser that supports them is used
items.recommendation: Include TODO in analyzeContent's task-section pattern, and add a detection/validation test proving a representative TODO markdown document is accepted and parsed consistently.
items.reproduction:
Use content like '# Backlog

## TODO

- Add parser tests
- Wire adapter registry
- Update docs'. GenericMarkdownAdapter.detect(content) scores 23 and returns detected=false, while parseGeneric(content) extracts those entries as tasks.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: parser.test.ts only covers the byte-length guard, and serializer.test.ts only covers metadata type handling; no test exercises GenericMarkdownAdapter.detect or validate for TODO documents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GenericMarkdownAdapter test that feeds a short ## TODO document with bullet or checkbox items, expects detect(...).detected to be true, validate(...).valid to be true or at least not LOW_CONFIDENCE, and parse(...).plan.proposed_changes to include file_update task changes.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the task-section regex in analyzeContent and add focused generic adapter detection/validation coverage.

items.title: Numbered lists are advertised as list content but are not detected or parsed for most sections
items.recommendation: Use a shared list-item matcher that recognises bullets, checkboxes, and numbered markdown items, then apply it consistently in analyzeContent, extractGoals, extractTasks, and extractFeatures.
items.reproduction:
Parse '# Plan

## Tasks

1. Add import support
2. Add export support'. analyzeContent reports hasLists=false/listItemCount=0, and parseGeneric(...).proposed_changes contains no task changes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included parser tests only assert input-size limits and do not assert extraction behaviour for numbered goals, tasks, or features; serializer tests do not exercise parsing or detection.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parser and detector tests for numbered ## Goals, ## Tasks, and ## Features sections, asserting that numbered items contribute to list indicators and become the expected metadata or proposed_changes.
items.minimumFixScope: Extend list matching in utils.ts and cover numbered-list parsing/detection in generic parser tests.

items.title: Generated package tests do not verify generated package behaviour
items.recommendation: Generate a minimal test that imports the package entrypoint and asserts the expected public surface for the selected package type, or remove tautological scaffold tests and cover the scaffold contract with generator-level tests.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions are independent of generated package code, so they cannot fail because of defects in the generated scaffold.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add generator-level tests that inspect the generated `src/index.test.ts` and run typecheck/test for representative generated package types.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the scaffolded `src/index.test.ts` templates in `tools/generators/src/generators/anvil-package/generator.ts` and `tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts`.

items.title: Unvalidated generator options are written into paths and TypeScript source
items.recommendation: Validate generator options before computing paths or source content. Enforce an explicit kebab-case/package-slug contract, reject `..`, path separators where unsupported, and invalid TypeScript identifier characters. Use `JSON.stringify` or an equivalent escaping helper when embedding user-provided strings in generated TypeScript.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked generator tests were provided, and the scaffolded tests only exercise generated happy-path code after generation has already succeeded.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add generator tests that reject invalid names, traversal-like directory/name values, and quote-containing descriptions, plus a valid-name case that typechecks the generated files.
items.minimumFixScope: Update option normalisation and validation in `tools/generators/src/generators/gate-check/generator.ts` and `tools/generators/src/generators/package/generator.ts`, then add focused generator tests.

items.title: template generation script drops the actions template
items.recommendation: Write templates.actions to an actions-template.md file and include it in the script output. Add a test or script-level smoke check for all TemplateBundle keys.
items.reproduction: Run packages/aps/scripts/generate-templates.js and inspect the output directory; actions-template.md is not created.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The generator tests verify generateAllTemplates returns an actions string, but no included test executes scripts/generate-templates.js or checks the generated files.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a script smoke test that runs generate-templates.js against a temp directory and asserts index-template.md, leaf-template.md, simple-template.md, and actions-template.md all exist and are non-empty.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/scripts/generate-templates.js and a focused script regression test.

items.title: root leaf plans with Modules-prefixed headings are loaded as empty indexes
items.recommendation: Apply the same real-index probe at the root detection point, or tighten detectIndexFile to match the headings parseIndex can actually parse. If variants like "Modules & Scopes" are intended, parseIndex must support them consistently before detection routes to the index loader.
items.reproduction: Create a single-file plan with an H1, a "## Modules impacted" section, and a valid "## Tasks" section, then call loadPlan(file). It will return isMultiModule true with an empty modules map and allTasks [], rather than the task list.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The loader tests include a false-positive "Modules impacted" case only for a leaf nested under an index. They do not exercise loadPlan directly on a root single-file leaf containing such a heading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a loader test that calls loadPlan on a standalone leaf fixture with "## Modules impacted" plus "## Tasks" and asserts isMultiModule is false and tasks are loaded.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts detection logic, with a focused loader regression fixture/test.

items.title: dist publish root conflicts with package entrypoints
items.recommendation: Align the release layout: either publish from {projectRoot} with dist included, or generate/copy a dist/package.json whose main/types/exports point to ./index.js, ./parser/index.js, etc. Include README and licence as needed for the dist package.
items.reproduction: Build the package, pack or publish from packages/aps/dist as configured, then try importing @eddacraft/anvil-aps and @eddacraft/anvil-aps/parser from the packed artifact; the entrypoints will be missing unless another unshown step rewrites the manifest.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Vitest suites import source modules and exercise runtime behavior; they do not run the package build, create the configured npm artifact, or import from the packed package.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a packaging smoke test that builds @eddacraft/anvil-aps, packs the configured packageRoot, extracts it in a temp project, and imports the root and each exported subpath.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps package metadata plus the release/build target that creates the published package root.

items.title: Ports package violates its stated dependency boundary by importing core types
items.recommendation: Move the shared public types used by ports into the intended contracts package, import them from that package here, and replace the @eddacraft/anvil-core dependency with the contracts dependency. If core is intentionally the source of truth, update the package description and module header to state that contract explicitly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and ordinary typechecking still passes because @eddacraft/anvil-core is declared as a dependency. A dependency-boundary regression needs to assert allowed imports, not just compilation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a dependency-boundary test or lint rule for packages/anvil/ports/src that fails on imports from @eddacraft/anvil-core and permits only the intended contracts dependency plus local relative imports.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/ports/src/interfaces/check.interface.ts, packages/anvil/ports/package.json, and the source package that owns APSPlan and WarningResult exports.

items.title: Website production build can pass with TypeScript errors
items.recommendation: Remove `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true`, or make the website build target run an explicit typecheck before `next build` so production builds cannot pass with TypeScript errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or build-contract tests are included for the website package. The provided scripts and Nx target definitions show the unsafe build path directly.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI/Nx target assertion or smoke check that `website:build` depends on typechecking, or add a fixture/type-error validation if the repo has project-configuration tests.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/website/next.config.mjs` and/or `apps/website/project.json`/`apps/website/package.json` so the website production build fails on TypeScript errors.

items.title: Published subpath exports do not expose declaration files
items.recommendation: Use conditional exports that include both types and default/import entries for each public subpath, for example mapping ./parser.types to ./dist/parser/index.d.ts and ./parser.default to ./dist/parser/index.js.
items.reproduction: After building and consuming the package from another TypeScript project using node16/nodenext or bundler resolution, import from @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta/parser and ask TypeScript to resolve declarations for that subpath.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests import the source file relatively, so they never exercise the built package exports map or downstream TypeScript declaration resolution.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package export smoke test that builds the package and typechecks a fixture importing @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta, @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta/parser, and @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta/types.
items.minimumFixScope: Package exports metadata and a build/typecheck smoke fixture for public subpath imports.

items.title: Build script references a missing TypeScript config
items.recommendation: Either change the build script to use tsconfig.json or add a real tsconfig.lib.json that extends tsconfig.json and is included in the package.
items.reproduction: Run pnpm -F @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta build in this package when tsconfig.lib.json is not present; tsc reports that the configured project file does not exist.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise parser behaviour through Vitest, but they do not run the package build target or assert that the build config file exists.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a workspace/Nx build validation for @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta, or at minimum a package-level smoke test/CI step that runs pnpm -F @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta build.
items.minimumFixScope: Package manifest build script and, if needed, the package TypeScript config file.

items.title: Package release configuration publishes dist without a package manifest
items.recommendation: Add an explicit build step that copies a publish-ready package.json into dist, or configure Nx/package tooling to generate the dist manifest before nx-release-publish runs.
items.reproduction: Run the package build, inspect packages/docs-meta/dist, then run the nx-release-publish target; unless another unshown step copies package.json into dist, the publish root lacks package.json.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only execute parser unit cases and do not validate the release output shape or publish root contents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a build-output assertion that packages/docs-meta/dist/package.json exists after the build and contains name, version, exports, dependencies, and type metadata needed for npm publication.
items.minimumFixScope: Build/release target configuration for @eddacraft/anvil-docs-meta.

items.title: Public export map and root barrel expose different runtime surfaces
items.recommendation: Make the public API consistent. Add `./concurrency` to package.json exports, and either export feature-flags from src/index.ts or document and test that feature flags are intentionally subpath-only.
items.reproduction: From packages/anvil/runtime after build, `node --input-type=module -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency')"` fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. A root import succeeds but does not contain `resolveFlag`, while it does contain concurrency symbols such as `LockManager`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests import implementation files with relative paths such as `./git-agent.js`, `./queue-manager.js`, and cache provider paths, so they bypass package.json exports and the root barrel.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package API smoke test that imports from `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime`, `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/cache`, `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/watch`, `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/feature-flags`, and `@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency` after build, asserting representative exports exist.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json, packages/anvil/runtime/src/index.ts if feature flags should be root-exported, and one package-level export smoke test.

items.title: Generated OpenAPI contract is omitted from package releases
items.recommendation: Include openapi.json in the package files allowlist, or generate/copy the spec into an included location such as dist as part of the build or publish flow.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and the package scripts do not include a packaging check that validates generated artifacts are present in the packed package.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a pack verification test or CI check that runs generate:openapi, creates a package tarball, and asserts openapi.json is included in the packed file list.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/package.json packaging metadata and, if necessary, the generator output/build flow so the generated OpenAPI artifact is shipped.

items.title: Freshness guard misses embedded scanner inputs, allowing stale native test binaries
items.recommendation: Extend the freshness baseline to include the local Rust scanner inputs that are compiled into this binding, at minimum crates/anvil-checks source files and patterns/compiled/registry.json. Prefer deriving local path dependencies from cargo metadata or centralising the list so future path dependencies are not silently missed.
items.reproduction: Touch or modify the embedded scanner registry or scanner crate source without changing crates/anvil-checks-napi/src, crates/anvil-checks-napi/Cargo.toml, crates/anvil-checks-napi/build.rs, or Cargo.lock; then run the package pretest with an older existing .node. The guard will not see the newer scanner input and will allow tests to run against the stale binary.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise the binding API and embedded-registry behaviour after import, but they rely on scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs to ensure the imported .node is current. There is no test that mutates or timestamps scanner-crate inputs and asserts the freshness guard rejects an older binding.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused test for the freshness guard that creates or touches a scanner-crate input such as patterns/compiled/registry.json after a dummy .node mtime and asserts the guard exits nonzero, ideally by extracting the mtime calculation into a testable helper.
items.minimumFixScope: Update scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs to include scanner crate and embedded registry inputs in inputMtime, then add a regression test for that freshness calculation.

items.title: Markdown link targets in metadata tables are discarded
items.recommendation: When extracting cell text or source references, preserve link destinations for link nodes. A minimal fix is to return `node.url` for path-like links, or include both label and URL in a form that splitRefs/extractPathLikeRefs can process. Add explicit handling for linkReference only if definitions are resolved or intentionally unsupported.
items.reproduction: Parse a governed document with `| [Guide](docs/guides/example.md) | |` in the relationships data row. The returned upstream entry is `Guide` and no `docs/guides/example.md` sourceReference is emitted.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover inline code and plain text cells, but none use markdown link syntax in metadata, relationship, or freshness cells.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser test with Upstream and Downstream cells containing markdown links to repo-relative docs paths and assert both `relations` and `sourceReferences` include the linked paths.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `phrasingText` or the table parsing path for `link` nodes, then add coverage in `parse-metadata.test.ts`.

items.title: Structured debug data bypasses log sanitisation
items.recommendation: Convert non-string data through a bounded serializer or util.inspect, then run sanitizeForLog on the resulting text before logging. Keep depth/length limits to avoid unexpectedly large debug output.
items.reproduction: Call debug('config', 'loaded', { token: 'Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' }) with ANVIL_DEBUG=1; the token value is printed because the object is not sanitised.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No debug utility tests are included, and the existing linked tests exercise only git operations and severity parsing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a debug test that enables ANVIL_DEBUG, logs an object containing a bearer token and newline, and asserts console.debug receives redacted single-line output.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/debug.ts plus focused debug utility tests

items.title: Explicit undefined default is ignored by parseSeverity
items.recommendation: Remove the default parameter initializer and distinguish omitted arguments from an explicit undefined default, for example by checking arguments.length before assigning the default fallback.
items.reproduction: Call parseSeverity('invalid', undefined) or parseSeverity(123, undefined); both return 'info' despite the documented example expecting undefined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: severity.test.ts only checks explicit undefined with valid values, where the default is not used. It does not assert invalid strings or non-string values with an explicit undefined default.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add expectations that parseSeverity('invalid', undefined) and parseSeverity(123, undefined) return undefined, while parseSeverity('invalid') still returns 'info'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/severity.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/utils/severity.test.ts

items.title: Backslash path segments are normalised after traversal validation
items.recommendation: Reject both '/' and '\\' traversal separators before platform-specific normalisation, or normalise backslashes to slashes before validating segments. Validate by splitting on '/' and rejecting empty, '.', '..', null-byte, and absolute-prefix cases as required by the intended contract.
items.reproduction: On a POSIX runtime, validateRelativePath('safe\\..\\..\\secret') returns 'safe/../../secret' instead of throwing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No path-safety tests are included with this feature; the linked tests cover git operations and severity parsing only.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add path-safety tests asserting that validateRelativePath('safe\\..\\..\\secret') and sanitizeIdentifier('a\\b') throw on POSIX as well as Windows-style separator inputs.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/utils/path-safety.ts plus new or extended path-safety unit tests

items.title: Complete statuses with trailing prose bypass validation-evidence checks
items.recommendation: Use the same leading-token style used for done statuses, for example filter on /^Complete\b/.test(item.status.trim()), while keeping the check scoped to Complete rather than all done-like lifecycle states if that is the intended policy.
items.reproduction: Create or edit an APS item with `- **Status:** Complete — merged 2026-04-29 via PR #1186` and no `- **Validation:**` line containing `validation passed`; scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs will not emit aps-complete-without-validation-evidence for that item.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no included test evidence exercises Complete statuses with appended dates or merge notes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an APS drift fixture with `Complete — ...` status and missing validation evidence, asserting aps-complete-without-validation-evidence is emitted.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs status predicate for the Complete validation-evidence advisory.

items.title: Malformed percent-encoded links crash the link checker
items.recommendation: Wrap path and anchor decoding in a small safeDecode helper that returns a structured invalid-URL finding on URIError, preserving the existing file and line reporting path.
items.reproduction: Add a Markdown link like [bad](./guide%ZZ.md) under docs/ or plans/ and run node scripts/docs/check-links.mjs; the script throws URIError rather than reporting a labelled broken-link finding.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no included test evidence covers malformed percent-encoding in Markdown hrefs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a check-links fixture containing malformed href and anchor escapes and assert the checker reports ERROR findings in both text and --json modes without crashing.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/check-links.mjs resolveLink decoding and result reporting.

items.title: Baseline regeneration overwrites with partial data after surface JSON failure
items.recommendation: Track regeneration failures and abort without writing the baseline unless every baselineable surface returns parseable JSON, or preserve the previous entries for failed surfaces and exit non-zero so the operator knows the baseline was not fully regenerated.
items.reproduction: Make a baselineable surface produce non-JSON output, for example by making scripts/docs/check-tags.mjs hit its catalogue fatal path, then run pnpm docs:check:update-baseline. The failed surface is skipped and the baseline file is still rewritten from the partial next object.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and no included test evidence covers --update-baseline child process failure or invalid JSON handling.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check baseline regeneration test with a mocked or temporary failing surface that emits invalid/no JSON, asserting the command exits non-zero and leaves the existing baseline file unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/docs/docs-check.mjs regenerateBaseline failure handling and baseline write gating.

items.title: Build script does not stage Nx generator metadata or schemas
items.recommendation: Extend the generator package build to copy or otherwise include generators.json and any generator schema files into the distributable layout, or point package metadata at files that are guaranteed to exist after build. Add a pack/build verification that runs the generator package from the built artefact.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are linked for this feature, and the package build script only type-compiles sources; it does not exercise package packing or Nx generator discovery from the built output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level test or CI step that builds tools/generators, packs or stages the package, then invokes Nx generator discovery against the resulting artefact and asserts all declared generators resolve with their schemas.
items.minimumFixScope: tools/generators/package.json build/package metadata and any generator asset staging configuration

items.title: Required native inputs are silently treated as optional
items.recommendation: Split required and optional mtime handling. Only build.rs should tolerate ENOENT; Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, and src/ should fail loudly when missing or unreadable.
items.reproduction: Remove or hide the workspace Cargo.lock or package Cargo.toml while leaving an older .node in place and native sources older than that binding; the pretest guard will skip the missing file rather than failing on an incomplete baseline.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this script, and the package manifest only wires it as a pretest hook.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Spawn the script against a fixture package with a .node file but a missing required Cargo.lock and assert that it exits non-zero with a baseline/configuration error.
items.minimumFixScope: Change fileMtime to accept an optional flag or add a requiredFileMtime helper, then update the Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock call sites to require presence.

items.title: Source deletions can leave stale bindings undetected
items.recommendation: Include directory mtimes in the recursive baseline, or use a manifest/hash-based build input stamp that records the source tree contents rather than relying only on surviving file mtimes.
items.reproduction: Build the binding, ensure existing source file mtimes are older than the .node, delete or rename a Rust source under src/, then run the package tests. The src directory mtime changes, but newestMtime ignores directory mtimes, so the stale .node can pass the freshness check.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and there is no fixture evidence exercising deletion or rename freshness cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a fixture src tree, set file and binding mtimes so the binding is newer, delete a source file after the binding timestamp, and assert the guard fails because the source tree changed.
items.minimumFixScope: Update newestMtime to stat each directory itself and include that mtime when computing the maximum, then cover deletion/rename cases with a focused script test.

items.title: docs-public has no registered test target or script
items.recommendation: Add a lightweight docs-public test target and at least one rendering/link contract test for the home page sections, or document why this docs app is intentionally covered only by a broader integration check.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, package.json has no test script, and project.json has no explicit test target.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that renders the home page section model or component and asserts the expected section titles and hrefs are present.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/docs-public test configuration plus a focused home page navigation test

items.title: Invalid BMAD-derived paths are collected as errors but parse still reports success
items.recommendation: Make bmadToAPS return both plan and collected diagnostics, or throw when errors is non-empty. BMADFormatAdapter.parse should pass warnings to createParseSuccess and use createParseError when conversion errors were collected.
items.reproduction: Parse structured agent YAML with metadata.id set to "../outside.md". The agent change is skipped after INVALID_PATH is pushed, but parse still returns success with no exposed errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise generic parser and serializer behaviour; none assert that BMAD safePath failures surface as ParseResult.errors.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD adapter test that parses agent/module YAML containing an invalid relative path and expects result.success to be false with an INVALID_PATH error.
items.minimumFixScope: Change BMAD conversion/adapter plumbing so collected AdapterError and AdapterWarning values are not discarded.

items.title: Serialized BMAD acceptance criteria are not recognised by the BMAD parser
items.recommendation: Make extractUserStories accept the serializer's bold header form, or change serializeToBMAD to emit the bare header format the parser already recognises. Prefer supporting both to preserve compatibility with common Markdown styling.
items.reproduction: Serialize an APS plan whose user story description contains '- Acceptance criteria: First; Second', then parse the generated BMAD. The emitted criteria section is not matched by extractUserStories, so the parsed story has no acceptanceCriteria.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included serializer tests cover the generic serializer only; they do not round-trip BMAD user stories with acceptance criteria through serializeToBMAD and parseBMAD.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD round-trip test for a user story with acceptance criteria and assert the criteria survive after serializeToBMAD followed by parseBMADDocument or parseBMAD.
items.minimumFixScope: Align BMAD acceptance-criteria heading parsing and serialisation formats.

items.title: BMAD input limit checks UTF-16 length instead of UTF-8 bytes
items.recommendation: Use Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8') for BMAD's size check, matching the generic parser contract.
items.reproduction: Call parseBMADDocument with '\u{1F600}'.repeat(Math.floor(MAX_INPUT_SIZE / 4) + 1); its UTF-8 byte length exceeds 2 MiB while content.length does not, so the guard passes.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The byte-length regression test is scoped to parseGeneric; there is no included BMAD equivalent for multi-byte input.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a BMAD parser test mirroring the generic multi-byte size guard case and expect parseBMADDocument to throw /maximum size/.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the BMAD parser's content.length guard with a UTF-8 byte-length guard.

items.title: Root package entrypoint is not covered by the included tests
items.recommendation: Add a root-entrypoint smoke test that imports representative runtime and type exports from ../index.js, or an integration compile test that imports from @eddacraft/anvil-aps after build.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests validate each submodule directly, so they do not exercise the aggregation contract provided by src/index.ts and package.json's root export.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create src/index.test.ts that imports parseDocument, loadPlan, filterPlan, validatePlanningDoc, TaskLocker, generateAllTemplates, and selected exported types from './index.js', then asserts the runtime exports are functions/classes.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a focused root barrel/export-map smoke test; no library implementation change is required unless that test exposes missing exports.

items.title: Plan-based and planless file filters receive different path shapes
items.recommendation: Construct fullPath before applying the filter in the plan-based branch, and pass the same path shape to the filter in both branches. If callers need relative-path filtering, add a distinct option rather than overloading this callback.
items.reproduction: Use a filter such as `(p) => p.startsWith(workspaceRoot)` with a CheckContext containing targetFiles and then with an equivalent plan proposed_changes entry. The targetFiles path passes after normalisation, while the plan path is rejected before it is joined to workspace_root.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked test covers getFilesFromContext filter behaviour across both planless and plan-based contexts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that call getFilesFromContext with equivalent targetFiles and proposed_changes inputs plus a filter expecting absolute paths, asserting both modes return the same file list.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/types/gate.types.ts and a focused test for getFilesFromContext

items.title: Expired or stale lock takeover can grant the same lock to multiple agents
items.recommendation: Serialize forceAcquire with the same lock-file sentinel used by createLock, then re-read the lock while holding the sentinel and only take over if it is still expired/stale and still represents the holder that was observed before waiting.
items.reproduction: Create an expired lock, then have two LockManager instances with different agent IDs call acquire({ type: 'action', resource: 'gate' }) concurrently. With the current forceAcquire path, both calls can return acquired: true under the read-before-write interleaving.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing expired-lock test exercises a single takeover after expiry; it does not race two takeover attempts against the same expired or stale lock.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that seeds an expired lock and runs two different agents' acquire calls concurrently, asserting exactly one result is acquired and the loser reports the winner as heldBy.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/lock-manager.ts plus a concurrent stale/expired takeover test in lock-manager.test.ts

items.title: Queue leave and timeout cleanup bypass the queue file lock
items.recommendation: Route every queue mutation through one locked helper that acquires `${queuePath}.lock`, reloads the current queue, applies the mutation, and writes or unlinks the file before releasing the lock.
items.reproduction: Have agent A and B queued, then run agent A leave while agent C joins the same queue. If leave reads before C's locked write and writes after it, C's entry can disappear from the queue file.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Queue tests cover sequential join, leave, status, and priority behaviour; they do not interleave join with leave or cleanup across QueueManager instances.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a multi-manager race test for join versus leave and another for join versus cleanupTimedOut, asserting no entries are lost and timed-out entries are the only removals.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/concurrency/queue-manager.ts and queue-manager.test.ts

items.title: File cache index updates lose entries across concurrent provider instances
items.recommendation: Protect index read-modify-write operations with a cache index lock, reload the index while holding the lock, apply the mutation, and then save. Avoid using a stale in-memory index across locked mutations unless it is refreshed or versioned.
items.reproduction: Instantiate two FileCacheProvider objects for the same workspace, make both load an empty index, then set different keys concurrently. The final index can contain only one key even though both entry files were written.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file cache tests cover sequential set/get, persistence, expiration, invalidation, and HMAC checks; they do not exercise concurrent writes from separate provider instances.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that runs Promise.all over two FileCacheProvider instances writing different keys to the same cache directory, then verifies a fresh provider can retrieve both keys and stats entries equals 2.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/src/cache/providers/file-cache.ts and file-cache.test.ts

items.title: Generated git hook imports an unexported package subpath
items.recommendation: Add a './concurrency' export with dist/concurrency/index.js and dist/concurrency/index.d.ts, and add a package-level import test for each documented subpath.
items.reproduction: After building or installing the package, run `node -e "import('@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency')"`; Node resolves through package.json exports and rejects the missing subpath.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The git-agent tests import the source module directly and validate the generated string, but they do not exercise Node package resolution against package.json exports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a build/package smoke test that imports '@eddacraft/anvil-runtime/concurrency' and verifies prepareCommitMsgHook is exported.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/runtime/package.json plus a package export smoke test

items.title: advance-released writes Released/Shipped for non-published release records
items.recommendation: Make non-published lifecycleState a blocking miss unless `--dry-run` is used, or require `lifecycleState === 'published'` before computing `wrote`. If legacy records may omit lifecycleState, decide explicitly whether omission is allowed and test that contract.
items.reproduction: Create a module item with `- **Status:** Merged ...`, pass a release record whose fenced JSON contains `{ "lifecycleState": "candidate", "aps": { "items": [{ "id": "MOD-001" }] } }`, and run `node scripts/aps/advance-released.mjs --root <tmp> --release-record plans/releases/r.md --tag v1.2.3 --sha abcdef123456 --date 2026-06-14`. The item is rewritten to Released/Shipped even though the record is not published.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests. The local advance-released fixture helper always writes `lifecycleState: "published"`, so it does not exercise candidate, draft, or other non-published records.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an advance-released fixture with `lifecycleState: "candidate"` and a Merged item, assert the command exits non-zero and leaves the module file unchanged.
items.minimumFixScope: `scripts/aps/advance-released.mjs` lifecycle validation plus one fixture case in `scripts/aps/_test/advance-released.test.sh`.

items.title: drift-check --root does not anchor relative input files
items.recommendation: Resolve relative `--changed-files`, `--release-record`, and `--pr-body-file` paths against `root` when they are intended to be project-local, or document and test that those arguments must be absolute/CWD-relative. Matching advance-released's root-relative release-record handling would make the APS scripts consistent.
items.reproduction: From a directory other than the project root, run `node scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs --root /path/to/repo --release-record plans/releases/release.json --json` where the release file exists only under `/path/to/repo`. The script attempts to read `plans/releases/release.json` relative to the current working directory and reports `release-record-unreadable`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the discovered drift-check fixtures pass absolute temporary paths for changed files and release records, so they do not exercise invocation from a different CWD with relative paths under `--root`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a drift-check fixture that runs from a subdirectory or unrelated directory with `--root <tmp>` and `--release-record plans/releases/r.json`, then asserts the record is read from `<tmp>` and the expected release finding appears.
items.minimumFixScope: Path resolution in `scripts/aps/drift-check.mjs` for file-valued options, plus one shell fixture covering `--root` with a relative release record.

items.title: SSL is disabled by substring matching the connection string
items.recommendation: Parse DATABASE_URL with `new URL(databaseUrl)` and disable SSL only when the hostname is exactly `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1`. Keep SSL enabled by default for all other hosts.
items.reproduction: Set DATABASE_URL to a remote PostgreSQL URL whose password or database name contains `localhost`; the script constructs the pg Client with `ssl: undefined` even though the host is not local.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and this edge case requires asserting the constructed pg Client options for non-local URLs containing the substring `localhost`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test around a small `sslForDatabaseUrl` helper covering localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, and remote URLs containing `localhost` outside the hostname.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the substring check in infra/scripts/admin-key-manage.mjs with hostname parsing and add focused tests for URL classification.

items.title: Create is not concurrency-safe for per-actor active key uniqueness
items.recommendation: Make the invariant atomic. Prefer a database partial unique index for active actor rows and handle the unique-violation path explicitly, or use a transaction-level advisory lock keyed by actor_email before the SELECT/INSERT. If revoke can affect multiple rows, write one audit row per returned id or enforce uniqueness so that multiple rows cannot be returned.
items.reproduction: Run two `create` invocations concurrently for the same ACTOR_EMAIL with different BEARER_HEX values against an `admin_keys` table without a partial unique constraint on active actor rows; both transactions can pass the pre-check and insert active keys.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this script, and a single-process happy path test would not exercise the concurrent SELECT/INSERT interleaving.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that starts two concurrent create operations for the same actor with different bearers and asserts that at most one active key exists and the loser exits with the expected database error.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key create transaction logic plus the admin_keys uniqueness constraint or locking strategy; update revoke audit handling if multiple active duplicates remain possible.

items.title: Documented create output uses hashed_key but script emits hashedKey
items.recommendation: Align the emitted JSON with the documented contract, or update the documented contract and every consumer to use `hashedKey`. For database-facing scripts, matching the snake_case column name in the output is likely the least surprising option.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided to assert the stdout JSON shape for the create action or to exercise the Pulumi consumer contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a script-level test for `create` that stubs pg, captures stdout, and asserts the exact JSON keys expected by the Pulumi component.
items.minimumFixScope: Update either the create stdout object or the documented contract and consumer expectations; add a focused stdout-shape regression test.

items.title: Line-number fields accept non-line-number values
items.recommendation: Constrain runtime-validated task line numbers with a shared positive-integer schema, for example `z.number().int().positive()`, and either enforce the same invariant in `ParseError` construction or document and guard callers that pass line numbers into errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the inspected manifest only exposes a package-level Vitest command; there is no included test asserting that invalid line-number values are rejected by these exported contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a types/schema test that `TaskSchema.safeParse` rejects `sourceLineNumber` values of 0, negative integers, and fractional numbers while accepting a positive integer.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `.claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/packages/aps/src/types/index.ts` to use a positive-integer line-number contract for task source locations and align `ParseError` handling with that contract.

items.title: Path validation can be bypassed by symlink swaps between check and filesystem operation
items.recommendation: Avoid treating a prevalidated string path as a security boundary when baseDir contents may be mutable by untrusted code. Implement operations using descriptor-relative traversal with no-follow semantics for path components where available, or narrow and document the contract so FileStorage is only used with a trusted, non-concurrently-mutated baseDir. For write/delete, do not perform the final operation through a path that can be reinterpreted after validation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests create symlinks before invoking FileStorage and assert that resolvePath rejects those stable paths. They do not simulate a path component changing between the resolvePath check and the subsequent fs.readFile/fs.writeFile/fs.unlink operation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that controls the gap between validation and fs.writeFile/fs.unlink, for example by mocking the fs operation to swap an already-validated internal directory or file path to a symlink pointing outside baseDir immediately before delegating to the real filesystem call, then assert the outside target is not read, written, or deleted.
items.minimumFixScope: FileStorage path resolution and filesystem operation implementation; at minimum the security contract for FileStorage must exclude attacker-writable or concurrently mutable base directories.

items.title: Ignored Rego violations are still emitted as warnings
items.recommendation: Have the generic new-violation rule preserve or respect `v.severity`, or exclude ignored/info-level violations from `warn`. If the intent is only summary accounting, keep it out of the `warn` rule path.
items.reproduction: Evaluate the generated policy with an `input.architecture.violations` entry that has `is_new: true` and `severity: "ignore"`; the generic `new-violation` rule still contributes a warning message.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests assert that a new-violation rule and warn rules are generated as text, but they do not evaluate the generated policy with `ignore` or `info` severities.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an OPA evaluation test for generated Rego where a new ignored violation produces no `deny` and no `warn` messages.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the `new-violation` Rego generation and add semantic policy tests for each supported severity.

items.title: Violation IDs can collide after lossy sanitisation
items.recommendation: Generate IDs from a lossless representation, for example `sha256(JSON.stringify([fromFile, toFile, line]))`, or encode each segment losslessly. Add migration/backwards-compatibility handling for existing baseline IDs if needed.
items.reproduction: Call `createViolationId('src/a-b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1)` and `createViolationId('src/a_b.ts', 'src/c.ts', 1)`; both return `src_a_b_ts:src_c_ts:1`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover stable IDs and different line/target values, but not two distinct paths that normalise to the same string after replacement.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting two edges that differ only by punctuation such as `a-b.ts` versus `a_b.ts` receive different violation IDs and are classified separately against a baseline.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `createViolationId` and the baseline comparison paths that depend on it; add focused tests for collision resistance.

items.title: Explicit Rego rule generation does not escape layer names
items.recommendation: Use a single helper based on `JSON.stringify` or equivalent Rego string literal escaping for every generated string value, including layer names, rule names used in comments, and severities. Alternatively, validate layer and rule identifiers to a strict safe subset before code generation.
items.reproduction: Use a definition with a layer key such as `bad"layer` and an explicit forbidden rule from that layer; the generated line becomes an invalid `v.from_layer == "bad"layer"` Rego expression.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests only use simple identifier-like layer and rule names and assert substrings; they do not parse the generated Rego or cover escaped characters in YAML layer names.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a generation test with quoted/backslash layer names and verify the resulting Rego parses, or add schema validation tests that reject unsupported identifiers.
items.minimumFixScope: Update explicit rule string interpolation in `rego-generator.ts` and cover generated Rego parsing for non-trivial layer names.

items.title: Template defaults leak mutable nested state across calls
items.recommendation: Deep-clone template defaults before returning them, for example with `structuredClone`, or clone each layer object and its arrays explicitly. Consider freezing the constants in tests to catch accidental mutation.
items.reproduction: Create a starter definition, push a value into `def.layers.lib.depends_on`, then call `createDefinitionFromTemplate('starter')` again. The later definition observes the earlier mutation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing coverage checks that the top-level return object is not the same reference, but it does not mutate nested layer objects or arrays and then request defaults again.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that mutates `getTemplateDefaults('layered').presentation.depends_on` and asserts a subsequent `getTemplateDefaults('layered')` call returns the original unmodified dependencies.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `getTemplateDefaults` to return fully independent layer definitions and cover `createDefinitionFromTemplate` because it exposes those defaults to callers.

items.title: command.invoked ignores capture opt-outs when Kindling is enabled
items.recommendation: Add an explicit capture flag for usage analytics or command invocations, map `command.invoked` to it in `shouldCapture`, and change the default branch to fail closed for unknown kinds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included command-invoked test covers schema shape only, and the redaction tests cover enabled/disabled service state only. There is no test for per-kind capture policy with all capture flags disabled.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a config test where `enabled: true` and every capture flag is false; assert `shouldCapture(config, 'command.invoked')` is false and that `KindlingService.emit` does not write the row.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/config.ts` and add capture-policy tests for `command.invoked` and unknown future kinds.

items.title: Detected API-key and token secrets can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make detection and redaction share the same recognised forms, and add generic redaction for common assignment/header/flag forms such as `--api-key value`, `api_key=value`, `token: value`, and `secret=value`. Prefer failing closed if sensitive data is detected but no mutation occurred.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The regression test only covers a password assignment that the current replacement regex handles. It does not cover detector-only cases such as generic api-key or token flags.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `kindling-service.redaction.test.ts` with spy-store cases for `curl --api-key abc123`, `token=abc123`, and `Authorization: token abc123`, asserting the persisted JSON contains none of the original values.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/sensitive-data-validator.ts` and the redaction regression tests.

items.title: OpenAPI generation script uses an undeclared runner
items.recommendation: Declare `tsx` in this package's devDependencies, or rewrite the script to use a declared runtime path. Keep the README and script command aligned.
items.reproduction: In a clean install containing only this package's declared dependencies, run `pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-kindling-integration generate:openapi`; the shell cannot resolve `tsx`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked Vitest suite does not execute package lifecycle scripts, and the package has no test that verifies the OpenAPI generator command is runnable from declared dependencies.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight script smoke check in package validation, or include generate:openapi in the relevant package CI command after adding the missing devDependency.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/package.json devDependencies and, if needed, the README command.

items.title: AnvilKindlingAdapter bypasses observation validation and redaction
items.recommendation: Validate the Anvil observation and redact sensitive fields before JSON.stringify in `AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit`; reject or drop observations that cannot be made safe, and set the core redaction metadata accurately when mutation occurs.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included redaction test exercises only `KindlingService.emit` with an `IKindlingStore`. There is no adapter test proving sensitive Anvil observations are validated and redacted before `appendObservation`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an adapter test with a fake Kindling core service that captures `appendObservation` input, then emit an `action_executed` observation containing a secret and assert the appended `content` is redacted and invalid rows are rejected.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/adapter.ts` and add focused adapter validation/redaction tests.

items.title: Validation helpers return blank errors for field-level schema failures
items.recommendation: Use result.error.issues to build path-aware messages, or return the ZodError/flattened fieldErrors so callers receive actionable validation diagnostics.
items.reproduction: Call validateQueryRequest({ scope: 'session', shape: 'timeline', format: 'json' }) or validateObservation({ kind: 'session_start' }); the parse fails, but the returned error string is empty because only root _errors are joined.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests only assert that invalid inputs are rejected; they do not assert that the returned error payload is non-empty or identifies the failed field.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add assertions that invalid query and observation inputs return an error containing the relevant field path, such as `session_id` or `timestamp`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change validateQueryRequest, validateQueryResponse, and validateObservation error formatting; update affected tests to check diagnostic content.

items.title: command.invoked observations are accepted on write but rejected by the query response contract
items.recommendation: Add `command.invoked` to the query response observation kind enum and the OpenAPI generator, or explicitly wrap usage rows under a documented query payload shape that validates consistently.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: `command-invoked.test.ts` validates only the write-side schema. The query response tests use empty or non-usage observation arrays, so they never prove usage rows can be read back.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `validateQueryResponse` test containing a returned observation with `kind: 'command.invoked'`, plus an OpenAPI generation assertion that the enum includes that kind.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `src/query-contract.ts`, `scripts/generate-openapi.ts`, and query-response contract tests.

items.title: Detected sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make detection and redaction use the same rule set. Either reject observations whenever a detected sensitive value cannot be redacted, or add redaction rules for every contract-level sensitive pattern and verify the redacted observation no longer triggers validateNoSensitiveData before calling store.emit.
items.reproduction: Emit an action_executed observation with details.command like `tool --api_key=abc123` or `ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host` through KindlingService using a fake store. The sensitive check is positive, but the stored observation still contains the original sensitive marker/value when it only matched the contract-level detector.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The malicious AI suite asserts that containsSensitiveData detects these cases, but it never exercises KindlingService.emit or redactSensitiveFields to prove the persisted observation is actually scrubbed.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingService.emit test with an in-memory IKindlingStore that records the emitted observation. Use commands containing `--api_key=abc123` and `~/.ssh/private_key`, then assert the stored JSON no longer contains the original sensitive substrings and either passes validateNoSensitiveData or is rejected.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/kindling-integration/src/sensitive-data-validator.ts and KindlingService.emit; add focused tests in packages/kindling-integration/src/malicious-ai.test.ts or a new service test.

items.title: Modules-prefixed H2 headings can make leaf specs skip task validation
items.recommendation: Make index detection require an exact canonical Modules heading, or parse enough index structure to distinguish a real module index before skipping leaf validation. Also reset index section state when leaving the Modules H2 section.
items.reproduction: Validate a leaf APS document with an H1, a "## Modules impacted" section, then "## Work Items" containing a task missing **Intent:**. The detector classifies it as an index and the task-intent rule is not evaluated.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover canonical Work Items and the leaf empty-section boundary, but they do not include a leaf document with a non-index H2 whose title starts with "Modules".
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture with "## Modules impacted" plus a "## Work Items" task missing **Intent:** and assert validatePlanningDoc reports task-intent rather than treating the file as an index.
items.minimumFixScope: Update detectIndexFile and validateIndexStructure section tracking in the validator, with one focused regression fixture.

items.title: Skipping path-containment still allows recursive load to fail on the same unsafe link
items.recommendation: When a skipped rule makes recursive graph loading unsafe or impossible, either bypass the dependent recursive load for that rule or document and enforce that callers must set recursive:false. Prefer adding a targeted branch so skipRules behaves consistently for the named validator rule.
items.reproduction: Call validatePlanningDoc on the path-containment fixture with { skipRules: ['path-containment'] } and recursive left at its default. The explicit path-containment issue is suppressed, but recursive load can still make the result invalid via plan-loadable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The skipRules test asserts only that no path-containment error is present; it does not assert result.valid or absence of replacement errors from recursive loading.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend the path-containment skipRules test to assert the expected validity contract, or add a separate test documenting that recursive loading is disabled/required when skipping containment checks.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the recursive validation path around skipped path-containment and update the skipRules test expectation.

items.title: Auth routes have no linked tests for security-critical OAuth behaviours
items.recommendation: Add Vitest coverage for the auth routes covering redirect construction, nonce cookie attributes, state round-trip handling, validateNext integration, all callback result statuses, logout cookie clearing, and failure branches.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature's linked tests array is empty, so there is no first-class evidence of intended behaviour for these routes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create route-level Vitest tests that mock @/lib/state, @/lib/next-url, and @/lib/bauth, invoke GET with NextRequest instances, and assert Location plus Set-Cookie headers for success and error cases.
items.minimumFixScope: Add tests under the docs-shell app for app/auth/login/route.ts, app/auth/callback/route.ts, and app/auth/logout/route.ts.

items.title: OAuth callback does not consistently clear the nonce cookie on failed callbacks
items.recommendation: Wrap every terminal callback error response in clearNonce, including missing_params and invalid_state. Consider making a helper that always clears the nonce for callback failures so future branches cannot miss it.
items.reproduction: Start a login to set oauth-nonce, then request /auth/callback without code/state or with an invalid state value. The response redirects to /auth/error, but does not set oauth-nonce with maxAge=0.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test asserts Set-Cookie behaviour for OAuth callback error paths.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add route tests that seed oauth-nonce and verify missing_params, invalid_state, csrf_mismatch, provider error, pending, auth error, and success callback responses all clear oauth-nonce where appropriate.
items.minimumFixScope: .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/apps/docs-shell/app/auth/callback/route.ts plus targeted route tests for callback cookie cleanup.

items.title: Warning result consistency validation ignores blocking and suppression summary fields
items.recommendation: Recompute and compare byCategory, suppressed, and blocking inside validateWarningResultConsistency. Also reject missing or extra severity/category counts if those are not intended to be tolerated.
items.reproduction: Construct a WarningResult with one unsuppressed severity 'error' warning, summary.total = 1, summary.bySeverity.error = 1, but summary.blocking = 0. validateWarningResultConsistency returns true even though createWarningResult would produce blocking = 1.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided tests cover APS and feature flag schemas only; no linked test exercises warning summary consistency or malformed WarningResult summaries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add warning schema tests that alter blocking, suppressed, and byCategory in a createWarningResult output and assert validateWarningResultConsistency returns false for each mismatch.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/warning.schema.ts plus a focused warning schema test file or existing contracts schema test coverage.

items.title: Feature flag targeting rules can reference missing variants
items.recommendation: Extend FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.check to collect variant keys and reject every targeting rule whose variant is not present in variants, with the issue path pointing at targeting[i].variant.
items.reproduction: Validate a flag with variants enabled/disabled and targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'typo' }]. FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema.safeParse currently succeeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked feature flag tests verify valid targeting rules, empty rule fields, and defaultVariant validation, but they never exercise a targeting rule that references a non-existent variant.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FeatureFlagDefinitionSchema test that uses validFlag({ targeting: [{ conditions: [{ attribute: 'environment', operator: 'equals', value: 'prod' }], variant: 'missing' }] }) and expects safeParse(...).success to be false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/contracts/src/schemas/feature-flags.schema.ts plus the associated feature-flags schema test.

items.title: No tests cover early-access install authorization outcomes
items.recommendation: Add focused route-handler tests that mock fetch and exercise missing accessKey, malformed JSON, upstream network failure, upstream 4xx, upstream 5xx, valid-but-not-Edict, and valid Edict token responses.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists an empty tests array, and no included test file asserts the route contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create a Vitest test for app/api/early-access/install/route.ts that constructs Request objects and stubs global fetch for each authorization outcome, asserting status codes and JSON bodies.
items.minimumFixScope: Add route-level tests for POST in the website app.

items.title: Pool cap behaviour is not covered by the library test
items.recommendation: Add a regression test that validates the cap in an isolated process before any other rayon consumer can initialise the global pool. If direct global-pool testing is too fragile for unit tests, factor the cap calculation into a small pure helper and test that helper, then add one integration or subprocess smoke test for `init_global` applying it first.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The sole included test only calls `init_global()` twice and asserts no panic by implication; its own comment states that it does not assert the resulting thread count.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Run a subprocess or dedicated integration binary that calls `eddacraft_anvil_rayon_init::init_global()` before any `par_iter`, then asserts `rayon::current_num_threads() == (num_cpus::get() / 2).max(1)`.
items.minimumFixScope: Add focused coverage for the cap calculation and first-initialisation behaviour in `crates/anvil-rayon-init`.

items.title: Root leaf plans with “Modules …” headings are loaded as indexes
items.recommendation: Apply the same parseIndex probe used for nested modules before taking the root index path, or narrow root index detection to the exact APS index shape rather than any heading prefix beginning with `modules`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included false-positive test loads `false-positive-modules/APS.md`, where the ambiguous heading is in a child leaf module; it does not load that leaf document directly as the root plan.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture leaf APS file with a `## Modules impacted` heading and assert `loadPlan(leafPath)` returns `isMultiModule: false` with its tasks loaded.
items.minimumFixScope: Change root index detection in `loadPlan` and add one root-level false-positive loader test.

items.title: Duplicate module IDs are silently overwritten when recursive loading is disabled
items.recommendation: Move the duplicate-ID check so it runs before insertion in both recursive and non-recursive paths, or factor module insertion through one helper that always validates uniqueness.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only `recursive: false` test covers the happy path and does not include duplicate module IDs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index fixture with two rows using the same module ID and assert `loadPlan(path, { recursive: false })` rejects with `ParseError`.
items.minimumFixScope: Add the duplicate module ID guard to the non-recursive branch and cover it with one focused loader test.

items.title: Freshness guard misses Rust engine and embedded registry inputs
items.recommendation: Include all local Rust dependency inputs that affect the NAPI binary in the freshness baseline, at minimum crates/anvil-checks source and generated/embedded registry artefacts, or replace the hand-maintained list with Cargo metadata/depfile-driven input discovery.
items.reproduction: Build the binding, modify a rule implementation or embedded registry content under crates/anvil-checks without touching Cargo.lock or crates/anvil-checks-napi files, then run pnpm --filter @eddacraft/anvil-checks-native test. The guard's inputMtime calculation can remain older than the .node and allow tests to run against the previously built engine.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests validate behaviour after importing the binding, and package.json runs the guard as pretest, but no linked test mutates a sibling Rust dependency or registry input and asserts that scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs fails before loading stale native code.
