items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused test for scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs using a temporary package/workspace layout where the .node is newer than crates/anvil-checks-napi/src but older than a mocked sibling Rust dependency or embedded registry input, and assert the guard exits non-zero.
items.minimumFixScope: scripts/check-binding-fresh.mjs plus a guard regression test covering sibling Rust dependency and embedded registry freshness

items.title: Non-recursive loading silently overwrites duplicate module IDs
items.recommendation: Move the duplicate-ID check before the recursive/non-recursive split, or add the same modules.has guard to the non-recursive branch before modules.set.
items.reproduction: Load an index containing two module headings with the same ID using loadPlan(path, { recursive: false }); the returned modules Map contains only the later entry for that ID.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The recursive=false test only verifies that a normal index skips loading task content; it does not cover duplicate module IDs in that mode.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a duplicate-module index fixture and assert loadPlan(fixture, { recursive: false }) rejects with ParseError matching duplicate module ID.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts duplicate guard placement plus one loader regression test.

items.title: Top-level leaf specs with “Modules …” headings are routed through the index loader
items.recommendation: Apply the same real-index probe at the root before calling loadMultiModulePlan, or make detectIndexFile only recognise actual index module sections and require parsed modules before selecting the multi-module loader.
items.reproduction: Create a valid single-file APS leaf document with an H1, valid task content, and an H2 named "Modules impacted". loadPlan(path) will take the index branch at packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts:91 instead of loadSingleFilePlan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing false-positive test loads an index whose child module contains "Modules impacted", so it exercises the nested fallback path only. There is no root-level single-file false-positive test.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a temporary or fixture single-file APS leaf with "## Modules impacted" and assert loadPlan returns isMultiModule=false with the expected module and tasks.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/aps/src/loader/index.ts root index detection plus one loader regression test.

items.title: Plan load failures are suppressed when earlier validation only produced warnings
items.recommendation: Change the catch guard to check for existing errors, not any issue, for example `if (!issues.some((issue) => issue.severity === 'error'))`, or always add a `plan-loadable` error unless a prior error from the same underlying rule already exists.
items.reproduction: Use a document that triggers a warning during shallow validation and then causes `loadPlan` to throw during recursive loading. The catch block suppresses `plan-loadable`, and the final result can remain valid because it has warnings but no errors.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests verify warnings-only documents are valid and verify some load failures with no prior warnings, but they do not cover a recursive load failure after a warning has already been recorded.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture that emits a warning before a recursive loader/parser failure and assert that `validatePlanningDoc` returns `valid: false` with a `plan-loadable` error.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the catch condition in `validatePlanningDoc` and add one focused regression test.

items.title: Task headings with an empty title pass validator-only mode
items.recommendation: After matching the heading, trim `title` and emit a `task-format` error when it is empty. Keep this check in the validator path, not only in the deeper loader/parser path.
items.reproduction: Validate a leaf spec with `recursive: false` whose task heading is `### TEST-001:` and whose body includes `Intent:`, `Expected Outcome:`, `Validation:`, and `Confidence:`. No task-format error is emitted.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included task-format tests assert lowercase IDs, non-3-digit numbers, and overlong scopes, but do not include `ID:` with no title.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validator test for a leaf fixture with `### TEST-001:` and `recursive: false`, expecting `valid` to be false and a `task-format` error mentioning the missing title.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `validateTaskFormat` to reject empty `title.trim()` and add one focused fixture/test.

items.title: Any heading starting with Modules is classified as an index section
items.recommendation: Use one shared, precise section predicate for root document classification and structure validation. If variants like `Modules & Scopes` are intentionally supported, make the allowed names explicit and ensure they are parsed consistently everywhere; otherwise require exact `modules`.
items.reproduction: Validate a document with `# Plan`, `## Modules impacted`, and no `## Tasks` section. It enters the index branch instead of the leaf branch, so the leaf required-section error is skipped.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The missing-modules test only covers a file with no Modules-like heading. There is no fixture for a non-index leaf section whose title starts with `Modules`.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture with `## Modules impacted` and no task section, then assert it is rejected as a leaf spec missing `## Tasks` or is otherwise not accepted as a valid index.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten `detectIndexFile` and `validateIndexStructure` section matching, then add one false-positive classification test.

items.title: Generated Vercel ignore command interpolates path arguments without shell-safe encoding
items.recommendation: Validate rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths with the same strictness as productionBranch, or shell-escape every argument before building defaultIgnoreCommand. Prefer a small helper with tests for branch, root directory, and extra watch path arguments.
items.reproduction: Instantiate VercelApp with rootDirectory set to "apps/web; echo injected" or extraWatchPaths containing "docs/o'clock" and inspect the Project ignoreCommand created by Pulumi mocks; the command is not safely escaped.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover shell metacharacter rejection for productionBranch and assert safe literal command fragments, but they do not exercise rootDirectory or extraWatchPaths containing spaces, quotes, or metacharacters.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add VercelApp tests that pass unsafe rootDirectory and extraWatchPaths values and assert they are rejected or emitted with correct shell escaping.
items.minimumFixScope: Update VercelApp default ignore command argument validation/escaping and add focused tests in vercel-app.test.ts.

items.title: Admin key provisioning check can race and create multiple live keys for one actor
items.recommendation: Enforce the invariant in the database with a partial unique index for active actor_email rows and handle unique-violation errors as a reviewed conflict, or serialize by actor with pg_advisory_xact_lock/serializable isolation before checking and inserting.
items.reproduction: Run two admin-key-manage.mjs create processes concurrently against the same database with the same ACTOR_EMAIL and different BEARER_HEX values; if the table lacks a partial unique constraint on active actor_email rows, both inserts can commit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise DNS and Vercel resource wiring only. No included test imports PerOperatorAdminKey or invokes admin-key-manage.mjs, and there is no concurrent create coverage for the admin key script.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test around admin-key-manage.mjs that attempts two concurrent creates for the same actor with different bearers and asserts only one active row can exist and the losing create fails deterministically.
items.minimumFixScope: Add database-backed uniqueness or transaction serialization for the create path, plus focused tests for duplicate/concurrent active-key creation.

items.title: Manifest now requires Node 24 while contributor contract still documents Node 22
items.recommendation: Either lower package.json engines.node back to the documented supported floor or update README/setup/CI documentation to make Node 24 the required baseline everywhere.
items.reproduction: Use Node 22.x and run an engine-enforcing install for this package; the manifest requires >=24.0.0 despite the README saying Node 22 is supported.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied for engine/documentation consistency, and the package scripts do not include a manifest-vs-README contract check.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs/metadata or package contract check that compares package.json engines.node against the README prerequisite text and setup-workspace baseline.
items.minimumFixScope: Align package.json engines.node and README prerequisite/setup wording in the same change.

items.title: README release status is stale relative to package version and changelog
items.recommendation: Update the README release status and shipped-baseline text to match the package/changelog release, or replace hard-coded release text with a checked/generated source if this field is meant to track the latest tag.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied for README release freshness, and the docs checks shown validate metadata/links/indexes rather than synchronising README release prose with package.json and CHANGELOG.md.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a release-doc freshness check that verifies README release status against package.json version and the newest non-Unreleased CHANGELOG entry.
items.minimumFixScope: Refresh the README release-status block and contributor baseline sentence to the current version.

items.title: Index module path placeholders produce ambiguous Markdown links
items.recommendation: Change path examples to avoid nested square brackets inside link syntax, for example `[./modules/module-name.aps.md](./modules/module-name.aps.md)` or `[module-name](./modules/module-name.aps.md)`, consistently across minimal, standard, and full index templates.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test checks only that some Markdown link-looking text exists and does not validate rendered/parsed Markdown or assert the exact placeholder-safe form.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that generated index templates do not contain bracketed placeholders inside Markdown link labels or destinations, or parse them with the same Markdown parser used by APS and verify the expected link URL/text.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the index template path lines in all variants and tighten the index path-link test.

items.title: Flags catalogue typecheck depends on contract exports that are missing from the resolved package API
items.recommendation: Publish/build the matching @eddacraft/anvil-contracts public declarations before typechecking this package, or update the flags-catalogue import path/API to one that is actually exported by the resolved contracts package. Add the dependency build/order to the project target so stale dist declarations cannot mask this in local or CI runs.
items.reproduction: Run `pnpm --dir packages/anvil/flags-catalogue typecheck`; it reports missing exports for FlagAudienceManifestSchema, FlagEnvironmentManifestSchema, FlagGroupManifestSchema, FlagSurfaceManifestSchema, FlagAudienceManifest, FlagEnvironmentManifest, FlagGroupManifest, and FlagSurfaceManifest from @eddacraft/anvil-contracts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import these schemas, but they are runtime tests and do not replace the package typecheck/build contract. In this checkout the typecheck fails before the library can be considered releasable.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI target that runs the flags-catalogue typecheck after building its referenced contracts dependency, or use `tsc -b` for the package graph so public declaration drift is caught deterministically.
items.minimumFixScope: Synchronise the contracts package public exports/build artefacts with the new flags-catalogue imports and wire flags-catalogue typecheck/build to depend on that output.

items.title: Published package omits the JSON manifests that runtime imports require
items.recommendation: Move or generate the flag JSON data into the package-owned source/dist tree, or generate a bundled TypeScript manifest module during build. Ensure the published package contains every runtime asset referenced by dist JavaScript.
items.reproduction: Build or pack packages/anvil/flags-catalogue, install the packed package outside the repo root, then import @eddacraft/anvil-flags-catalogue; the dist manifest import resolves to missing flags/*.json files outside the package contents.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import source files inside the monorepo where ../../../../flags/*.json exists, so they do not exercise the packed package layout or runtime import from dist.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a pack/install smoke test that runs `pnpm pack` for the package, installs it into a temporary project, and imports `@eddacraft/anvil-flags-catalogue` successfully.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust the catalogue build/package layout so the JSON manifests are package-local published assets, then add a packed-package smoke test.

items.title: Trace file creation can follow a raced symlink before validation
items.recommendation: Open trace files with no-follow semantics on Unix, for example OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW) plus create_new(true) for the absent-file path or an openat-style flow. Keep the post-open inode check, but make the open itself refuse symlinks.
items.reproduction: On Unix, set ANVIL_TRACE_SINK=file=<path in attacker-writable directory>. Race creation of <path> as a symlink after validate_existing_trace_file observes NotFound but before OpenOptions::open runs. The function can open the symlink target before returning TraceSink.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included Unix tests cover existing non-regular paths and private regular files, but they do not exercise the missing-path creation case or a symlink substitution race.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Unix test for a missing path where the final path is a symlink at open time, and assert open_trace_file returns an error without creating or opening the symlink target. If deterministic race injection is hard, factor the open path to make the NotFound-to-open transition testable.
items.minimumFixScope: crates/anvil-observability/src/lib.rs open_trace_file Unix opening flags and corresponding Unix tests.

items.title: As-built source globs can escape the repository root
items.recommendation: Apply the same repository-root boundary check to glob patterns before or after expansion. For each match, resolve it against root and reject the reference if any match is outside root; also reject glob patterns whose normalized base path escapes root.
items.reproduction: Add a governed As-built or Runbook source reference using a glob such as ../*; check-asbuilt-paths will accept it if the parent directory contains matches instead of reporting the same root-escape error used for non-glob paths.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature payload lists no linked tests, and no owned test file exercises escaped glob source references.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check fixture for check-asbuilt-paths with a governed document citing ../* and assert it emits an ERROR for escaping the repository root.
items.minimumFixScope: Update check-asbuilt-paths.mjs resolveSourcePath glob handling and add a focused fixture test for escaped glob references.

items.title: Docs index uses a narrower tag-catalogue contract than the tag validator
items.recommendation: Share one catalogue parser between check-tags.mjs and docs-index.mjs, or update docs-index collectApprovedTags to visit the full data row just like check-tags.
items.reproduction: Move the approved tag inline-code column in docs/governance/tags-catalogue.md from the first cell to another table column. check-tags still recognises the tags, but docs-index collectApprovedTags misses them and renderTagPage reports unknown tags.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature payload lists no linked tests, and the owned files do not include a contract test that compares approved-tag parsing across check-tags and docs-index.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a fixture catalogue with approved inline-code tags outside the first column and assert both check-tags and docs-index recognise the same approved set.
items.minimumFixScope: Align docs-index.mjs collectApprovedTags with check-tags.mjs and cover the shared catalogue parsing contract.

items.title: Absolute Markdown links are not percent-decoded before filesystem checks
items.recommendation: Run safeDecode on root-absolute rawPath before resolving it, and preserve the malformed percent-encoding error path for absolute links as well as relative links.
items.reproduction: Create docs/My Doc.md and link to it from another governed markdown file as /docs/My%20Doc.md. The absolute branch resolves the literal %20 path and reports the target missing, while the equivalent relative encoded link is decoded correctly.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature payload lists no linked tests, and no included evidence covers URL-encoded absolute internal links.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a check-links fixture containing an absolute internal link with %20 in the path and assert it passes when the decoded target exists.
items.minimumFixScope: Update check-links.mjs absolute path handling and add one encoded absolute-link regression fixture.

items.title: Glob source references can escape the repository root
items.recommendation: For glob references, resolve each match to an absolute path and reject any match whose relative path from root starts with '..' or is absolute. Also reject glob patterns that are themselves rooted outside the repository before executing globby.
items.reproduction: Use a governed As-built or Runbook document with a source reference '../*' while the repository parent contains any matching entry. The glob branch returns null for the match and never reaches the relPath(root, targetAbs) escape check.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and the current code path has no visible assertion for glob references that escape the repository root.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-check fixture for check-asbuilt-paths with a governed Runbook source reference '../*' and assert it emits a source path escapes repository root error even when the glob matches.
items.minimumFixScope: Update resolveSourcePath in check-asbuilt-paths.mjs and add a focused fixture test for escaping glob references.

items.title: Tag catalogue parsing is inconsistent between validation and index generation
items.recommendation: Share one catalogue parser between check-tags.mjs and docs-index.mjs, or make both scripts read the same explicit column by header name and reject inline-code tokens outside the approved tag column.
items.reproduction: Move the approved tag column away from the first catalogue table cell, or add an inline-code example in a non-tag cell. check-tags and docs-index will derive different approved-tag sets from the same catalogue.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test demonstrates agreement between check-tags and docs-index when catalogue columns are reordered or description cells contain inline code.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a shared fixture for tags-catalogue.md with a reordered tag column and an inline-code description example, then assert both surfaces derive the same approved tag set and reject the description example as a tag.
items.minimumFixScope: Extract or duplicate a single consistent catalogue-table parser in check-tags.mjs and docs-index.mjs, with fixture coverage for column order and non-tag inline code.

items.title: Generated indexes scan public docs that metadata governance explicitly excludes
items.recommendation: Add '!docs/public/**' to docs-index.mjs SOURCE_PATTERNS, or explicitly document and test that generated indexes intentionally cover public docs despite the metadata surface exclusion.
items.reproduction: Create docs/public/example.md with a DOCGOV metadata table. check-metadata will skip it because of '!docs/public/**', while docs-index will parse it and include it in docs/indexes outputs or report parse errors via index-freshness.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test fixture demonstrates docs/public/** staying out of docs-index generation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an index generation fixture with docs/public/public.md containing DOCGOV-shaped metadata and assert docs-index ignores it when rendering all index files.
items.minimumFixScope: Align docs-index.mjs SOURCE_PATTERNS with the metadata surface and add one fixture-level docs-index test.

items.title: Concurrent locks for different tasks can overwrite each other in state.json
items.recommendation: Serialize all state.json mutations behind a single state-file lock, or implement an atomic retry loop that re-reads current state and merges the task update immediately before the final write. Keep the per-task lock for same-task exclusion, but protect the shared state file as a separate shared resource.
items.reproduction: Run two TaskLocker instances against the same project root and plan, then call Promise.all([lockerA.lock('TEST-001'), lockerB.lock('TEST-002')]) from an empty state. Both task-level lock acquisitions can succeed, but the final .anvil/state.json may contain only one of TEST-001 or TEST-002 depending on the last writer.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The concurrency tests cover multiple attempts for the same task and direct lock-file acquisition. They do not exercise concurrent successful updates for different task IDs, which is the path where two writers can both proceed to updateTaskState.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TaskLocker test that concurrently locks TEST-001 and TEST-002 many times or with an injected write barrier, then asserts both lock results succeed and state.json contains both task records after the operations complete.
items.minimumFixScope: Change state file update semantics in packages/aps/src/state/index.ts and add a cross-task concurrent lock regression test in packages/aps/src/state/state.test.ts.

items.title: Literal pattern counting treats strings as regular expressions
items.recommendation: For string patterns, count literal occurrences without constructing a RegExp or escape the string before regex construction. For RegExp inputs, preserve caller-supplied flags while ensuring global iteration.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise registry lookup and detection selection only; no tests cover countOccurrences with literal metacharacters or flagged RegExp inputs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add utils tests asserting countOccurrences('a.b.c', '.') === 2, countOccurrences('[x]', '[') === 1, and countOccurrences('Foo foo', /foo/i) === 2.
items.minimumFixScope: Update countOccurrences in base/utils.ts and add focused utility tests.

items.title: File discovery exact-match scoring never applies to normal paths
items.recommendation: Pass entry.name or basename(fullPath) for exact filename scoring, while keeping directory-aware checks on the full path if needed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test file covers AdapterRegistry only; there are no included tests for discoverPlanningFiles, findBestPlanningFile, or confidence ranking.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a file-discovery test with root tasks.md and docs/design.md and assert tasks.md receives exact-match confidence and sorts first.
items.minimumFixScope: Adjust calculateFileConfidence to use basename for exact filename comparisons and add file-discovery ranking tests.

items.title: Merged parse results can report success without parsed data
items.recommendation: When merging, require at least one successful result with data before returning success, or return a structured parse error when all successful inputs lack data.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked registry tests only exercise registry behaviour and do not cover mergeParseResults or the parse-success-without-data case.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a utils test that calls mergeParseResults([{ success: true }, { success: true }]) and expects success false with a clear error code, plus a case where a later result supplies data and succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: Update mergeParseResults in base/utils.ts and add focused utility tests.

items.title: Published CLI reports a different version than the package
items.recommendation: Read the version from package metadata during build/runtime, inject it via a build constant, or keep a single source of truth so the CLI version tracks `tools/codemods/package.json`.
items.reproduction: Build the package and run `node tools/codemods/dist/cli.js --version`; it reports `0.0.1` while the package version is `0.3.0-beta`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CLI test that invokes `--version` and compares the output with `tools/codemods/package.json` version.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/cli.ts` version wiring or package build metadata so the Commander version matches `tools/codemods/package.json`.

items.title: Split imports drop aliases and type-only import qualifiers
items.recommendation: Preserve the full named import structure when grouping symbols: include `name`, `alias`, and type-only metadata from ts-morph, and set `isTypeOnly` on inserted import declarations when appropriate. Add explicit handling for mixed type/value imports if the AST API requires separate declarations.
items.reproduction: Apply the codemod to `import type { APSPlan as Plan, GateRunner } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';` or `import { APSPlanSchema as Schema, GateRunner } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';`. The recreated imports contain bare symbol names and no import kind preservation, so existing `Plan` or `Schema` references are no longer imported as written.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests for split imports containing aliases, `import type`, and `type` named specifiers, asserting the transformed source preserves aliases and type-only semantics.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `processSplitImports` in `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts` to group structured import specifier data instead of bare strings.

items.title: Bare core imports are counted and reported twice
items.recommendation: Handle bare `@eddacraft/anvil-core` imports in one place. Prefer running split-import logic before simple path rewrites, or make `processImportDeclaration` skip the bare core package when named imports are present so symbol-based splitting owns that case.
items.reproduction: Run the codemod against a file containing `import { APSPlanSchema, GateRunner, OPAExecutor } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core';`. Dry-run output includes the simple contracts rewrite plus split entries; applying the codemod rewrites the whole import to `@eddacraft/anvil-contracts` instead of splitting runtime and policy symbols.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this package, and the feature metadata lists an empty tests array.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a vitest covering a mixed bare core import and assert dry-run returns only the package-specific split changes and apply mode emits separate imports for contracts, runtime, and policy symbols.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `tools/codemods/src/transforms/rewrite-imports.ts` so bare core imports cannot be processed by both rewrite paths.

items.title: Common registry unregister loses removal status
items.recommendation: Change common AdapterRegistry.unregister to return boolean from this.adapters.delete(name), and align its tests with the linked registry unregister expectations.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests import ../registry.js from src/base, not src/common/registry.ts, so this common implementation can diverge without failing those tests.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a common registry test that registers an adapter, expects unregister(name) to return true and remove it, then expects unregister('missing') to return false.
items.minimumFixScope: Update .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/packages/adapters/src/common/registry.ts and add focused coverage for common AdapterRegistry unregister behavior.

items.title: Public declarations expose Buffer without publishing Node type support
items.recommendation: Either avoid the Node-global type in the public contract, for example by using Uint8Array or importing a type from node:buffer with the required type package declared, or add @types/node to the package's published dependency surface so consumers receive the declaration dependency automatically.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests exercise the package as an installed dependency from a consumer project without the repository root devDependencies. The local typecheck uses workspace-level Node typings, masking the missing manifest contract.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a declaration-consumer fixture that installs or links only @eddacraft/anvil-ports and runs tsc without root workspace devDependencies, asserting that importing IStorageProvider typechecks.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/anvil/ports/package.json and, if choosing to avoid Node globals, packages/anvil/ports/src/interfaces/storage.interface.ts.

items.title: weightedConfidence can produce out-of-range EmberConfidence values
items.recommendation: Constrain weights to positive or at least non-negative values, either by parsing with a small Zod schema or by throwing when any weight is negative. Also validate or clamp the final result before returning an EmberConfidence.
items.reproduction: weightedConfidence([{ score: 1 as EmberConfidence, weight: 2 }, { score: 0 as EmberConfidence, weight: -1 }]) returns 2 cast as EmberConfidence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only covers positive weights and the zero-length case indirectly through other utilities. It does not cover negative weights or verify the result still satisfies EmberConfidenceSchema.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that negative weights are rejected, and another that EmberConfidenceSchema.safeParse(weightedConfidence(validPositiveWeights)).success remains true.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/confidence.ts and confidence utility tests.

items.title: Extended memory contract diverges from the base EDDA-001 attribution contract
items.recommendation: Define MemoryObjectExtended as a true extension of the base MemoryObject type, or reuse AttributionSchema fields and add promotion-specific fields separately. Add a schema or type-level test proving the extended shape remains assignable to the base contract.
items.reproduction: A MemoryObjectExtended-shaped object with attribution.promoted_by and attribution.promoted_at lacks attribution.actor, attribution.timestamp, and attribution.method, so MemoryObjectSchema.safeParse(value).success is false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover MemoryObjectSchema and typed memory schemas, but no test imports or validates MemoryObjectExtended.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an edda-extended contract test that constructs an extended memory and asserts its core portion validates with MemoryObjectSchema, or add a TypeScript assignability test if the divergence is intentionally compile-time only.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/edda-extended.ts plus focused tests for compatibility with MemoryObjectSchema.

items.title: MemoryObjectExtended is not compatible with the EDDA-001 memory schema it claims to extend
items.recommendation: Define MemoryObjectExtended in terms of the base type, for example by importing type MemoryObject and using interface MemoryObjectExtended extends MemoryObject for additive fields. If the attribution shape intentionally changed, model it as a named migration or Omit<MemoryObject, 'attribution'> with clear schemas/tests rather than labelling it as core EDDA-001.
items.reproduction: Parse a valid EDDA-001 memory with MemoryObjectSchema, then try to add scope/authority/enforcement/review_policy and use it as MemoryObjectExtended. TypeScript rejects the attribution shape and required optional fields; at runtime, a MemoryObjectExtended-shaped attribution fails MemoryObjectSchema parsing.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise MemoryObjectSchema and related typed memory schemas, but there are no tests for edda-extended.ts or assignability/parse compatibility between MemoryObject and MemoryObjectExtended.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a type-level test or tsd-style fixture showing that a MemoryObject plus extension fields satisfies MemoryObjectExtended, and a runtime test that the shared core fields still parse through MemoryObjectSchema.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/edda-extended.ts and a focused compatibility test.

items.title: Proposal creation events can be emitted without source observations
items.recommendation: Change source_observation_ids to a non-empty observation ID array, preferably z.array(ObservationIdSchema).min(1), and keep the event contract aligned with ProvenanceSummarySchema.
items.reproduction: ProposalCreatedPayloadSchema.safeParse({ proposal_id: uuid, proposal_type: 'pattern', confidence: 0.5, summary: 'x', expires_at: ts, source_observation_ids: [] }).success is true, while the corresponding CandidateProposal provenance with observation_ids: [] is rejected.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: events.test.ts only covers a valid non-empty source_observation_ids array and invalid confidence; it does not assert that an empty source_observation_ids array is rejected.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an events.test.ts case asserting ProposalCreatedPayloadSchema.safeParse({...validPayload, source_observation_ids: []}).success is false.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/events.ts plus the focused event schema test.

items.title: buildEvolutionGraph can return dangling evolution links
items.recommendation: Make buildEvolutionGraph enforce referential integrity. Either reject missing endpoints during graph construction, include placeholder nodes with an explicit partial/incomplete marker, or skip out-of-set links when building a graph for a partial memory set. Keep EvolutionGraphSchema or a refinement aligned with that choice.
items.reproduction: Call buildEvolutionGraph with one parsed memory whose evolution.superseded_by is another valid MemoryId not included in the memories array. The returned graph contains one node and one link to a missing new_memory_id; validateEvolutionGraph(graph).valid is false, and findLatestMemory(graph) returns null.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: evolution.test.ts builds graphs where both sides of every supersedes/superseded_by relationship are present. It does not cover partial memory sets or missing link endpoints.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds a graph from a memory whose superseded_by target is absent and asserts the chosen contract: buildEvolutionGraph throws, omits the dangling link, or creates a validated placeholder node. Also assert findLatestMemory does not silently return null for a one-node partial graph.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/evolution.ts plus evolution graph tests.

items.title: mergeProvenanceChains can return an invalid ProvenanceChain for empty input
items.recommendation: Reject empty input with a clear error, change the signature to require a non-empty tuple, or return null/undefined for empty aggregation. Also parse or otherwise assert the returned object against ProvenanceChainSchema before returning.
items.reproduction: ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse(mergeProvenanceChains([])).success evaluates to false because kindling_sources is empty.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The mergeProvenanceChains tests only pass one or more non-empty chains. They do not assert behaviour for an empty merge request.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a mergeProvenanceChains([]) test that asserts the selected contract, preferably that the function throws a clear error instead of returning a schema-invalid ProvenanceChain.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/provenance.ts and provenance tests.

items.title: Merging zero provenance chains returns a value that violates the advertised return type
items.recommendation: Reject empty input explicitly, or change the return type to ProvenanceChain | null and require callers to handle the no-input case. If keeping the current return type, parse the returned object with ProvenanceChainSchema before returning.
items.reproduction: mergeProvenanceChains([]) returns an object with kindling_sources: [], and ProvenanceChainSchema.safeParse(mergeProvenanceChains([])).success is false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The merge tests cover multiple chains and a single chain with no optional relation fields, but never the empty input path.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a provenance.test.ts case for mergeProvenanceChains([]), asserting it throws a clear error or returns null depending on the chosen contract.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/provenance.ts and the mergeProvenanceChains test block.

items.title: Evolution link metadata depends on input order for reciprocal supersession records
items.recommendation: Build reciprocal link candidates first, then merge duplicates with a deterministic precedence rule that prefers the retired/superseded memory's retirement metadata when available. Alternatively normalise links from one authoritative side only.
items.reproduction: Call buildEvolutionGraph([newMemoryWithSupersedesOld, oldMemoryWithSupersededByNewAndRetirementMetadata]) and compare the link to buildEvolutionGraph([oldMemoryWithSupersededByNewAndRetirementMetadata, newMemoryWithSupersedesOld]); the first ordering keeps the generic/default metadata, the second keeps the retired metadata.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing buildEvolutionGraph tests always pass the older superseded memory before the newer memory, so the retired-side metadata wins and the order-dependent branch is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds the same reciprocal evolution chain in both input orders and asserts the resulting link reason, actor, and linked_at are identical and prefer the explicit retirement metadata.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/src/contracts/evolution.ts and the evolution graph utility tests.

items.title: Governance tables are accepted even when they are not immediately after the H1
items.recommendation: Replace collectTablesAfterH1 with logic that walks the immediate top-level nodes after the H1 and requires the next two meaningful nodes to be the metadata and relationships tables, rejecting any intervening paragraph, heading, list, code block, or unrelated table with a ParseError carrying the offending line.
items.reproduction: Parse a document with '# Title', then a paragraph or '## Later section', then otherwise valid metadata and relationships tables. parseDocGovernance will return a successful result instead of rejecting the misplaced governance block.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover a happy path with immediate tables and cases where tables are absent, but there is no negative test for valid-looking governance tables placed after intervening prose or a later section.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that inserts prose or a heading between the H1 and the metadata table, and another that inserts prose between the metadata and relationships tables; both should throw ParseError.
items.minimumFixScope: Update parse-metadata.ts table selection and add parser tests for non-immediate governance tables.

items.title: Post-query limit enforcement ignores smaller per-query limits
items.recommendation: Carry the effective request limits into post-query enforcement. Compute min(requested, config) for each query call and pass those limits to enforceQueryLimits for that response. Consider enforcing response limits inside KindlingService.query as well for lower-level callers.
items.reproduction: Use a service configured with query_limits.max_results = 100 and a store/query implementation that returns 50 observations regardless of the request. Calling querySession(validUuid, { max_results: 10 }) returns all 50 because applyLimits enforces 100.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests validate schema maximums and response metadata shapes, but they do not exercise KindlingQueryService with a mock service/store that returns more rows than the caller requested.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingQueryService test where the underlying service returns more observations than options.max_results and assert the returned response is truncated to the requested count with truncation metadata set.
items.minimumFixScope: query-service.ts limit plumbing plus a focused query-service regression test.

items.title: Mandatory plan, gate, and action IDs accept empty strings
items.recommendation: Use z.string().min(1) at minimum for plan_id, gate_eval_id, and action_id, and preferably encode the expected ID formats where they are known.
items.reproduction: PlanQuerySchema.safeParse({ scope: 'plan', plan_id: '', shape: 'entity' }) succeeds; the same applies to gate_eval_id and action_id with empty strings.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests reject missing IDs, but they do not cover empty-string IDs for plan, gate, or action queries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting PlanQuerySchema, GateQuerySchema, and ActionQuerySchema reject empty-string identifiers.
items.minimumFixScope: query-contract.ts schema refinements plus malicious-ai.test.ts coverage for empty identifiers.

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make sensitive handling fail closed: either reject observations when any detected issue cannot be redacted, or add redaction coverage for every containsSensitiveData class and verify the post-redaction payload no longer triggers detection. Also route AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit through the same validation/redaction path or mark/drop sensitive content before appendObservation.
items.reproduction: Use an enabled KindlingService with a mock store and emit an action_executed observation whose details.command is `ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host`; containsSensitiveData reports sensitive, but redactSensitiveFields has no private-key-path replacement, so the mock store receives the original command. Calling AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit with the same observation serializes it directly into content.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests assert containsSensitiveData detects sensitive payloads, but they do not exercise redactSensitiveFields, KindlingService.emit with a capturing store, or AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit output.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that emit the existing private_key and token-in-error fixtures through KindlingService.emit and AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, then assert the persisted content no longer contains the original sensitive substrings or that emission rejects the observation.
items.minimumFixScope: sensitive-data-validator.ts plus KindlingService/adapter emission paths; add focused tests in malicious-ai.test.ts or a service-specific test.

items.title: Sensitive observations can still be persisted unredacted
items.recommendation: Make sensitive handling fail closed: after redaction, re-run detection and reject/drop if any sensitive issue remains. Add redaction coverage for every class that containsSensitiveData reports, and route AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit through the same validation/redaction path or explicitly reject sensitive Anvil payloads before appendObservation.
items.reproduction: Emit an enabled action_executed observation whose details.command is `ssh -i ~/.ssh/private_key user@host` through KindlingService with a capturing store; the stored JSON still contains `private_key`. Emitting the same observation through AnvilKindlingAdapter serializes it directly into `content`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: kindling-service.redaction.test only exercises `--password=...`; malicious-ai.test only asserts private_key detection and does not assert that detected private_key payloads are redacted before persistence. No included test covers AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit redaction.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add store-boundary tests for the existing private_key fixture and a short token-in-error fixture through both KindlingService.emit and AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, asserting the persisted payload no longer contains the original sensitive substrings or that emission rejects.
items.minimumFixScope: sensitive-data-validator.ts, KindlingService.emit post-redaction verification, AnvilKindlingAdapter.emit, and focused redaction persistence tests.

items.title: Mandatory plan, gate, and action IDs accept empty strings
items.recommendation: Use z.string().min(1) at minimum for plan_id, gate_eval_id, and action_id. Prefer a stronger format where those ID formats are defined.
items.reproduction: PlanQuerySchema.safeParse({ scope: 'plan', plan_id: '', shape: 'entity' }) succeeds; GateQuerySchema and ActionQuerySchema likewise accept empty gate_eval_id/action_id.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests reject missing IDs but do not cover empty-string IDs for plan, gate, or action queries.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests asserting PlanQuerySchema, GateQuerySchema, and ActionQuerySchema reject empty-string identifiers.
items.minimumFixScope: query-contract.ts ID schema refinements plus malicious-ai.test coverage for empty identifiers.

items.title: Post-query limit enforcement ignores the caller's smaller per-query limits
items.recommendation: Carry the effective request limits into post-query enforcement. For each query method, compute effective limits as min(requested limit, config limit) and pass those limits to enforceQueryLimits for that response. Consider also applying response limits inside KindlingService.query for callers that use the lower-level service directly.
items.reproduction: Use a KindlingQueryService whose underlying service has config.query_limits.max_results = 100 and whose query method returns 50 observations regardless of request. Calling querySession(validUuid, { max_results: 10 }) returns all 50 because applyLimits enforces 100, not 10.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests validate schema maximums and manually validate truncation metadata, but they do not use KindlingQueryService with a store/service that returns more rows than the request asked for.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KindlingQueryService test with a mock service returning more observations than options.max_results and assert the returned response is truncated to the requested count with truncation metadata set.
items.minimumFixScope: query-service.ts limit application, with a focused query service regression test.

items.title: command.invoked observations cannot be represented in query responses
items.recommendation: Add `command.invoked` to the query response ObservationSchema kind enum, or explicitly exclude it from queryable storage and document that decision. Update the all-kinds tests to include the command.invoked read path if it is queryable.
items.reproduction: A QueryResponse whose observations[0].kind is `command.invoked` fails QueryResponseSchema.safeParse even though the same kind is accepted by ObservationSchema in observation-contract.ts.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: command-invoked.test only validates the write-side schema. malicious-ai.test's all-kinds coverage omits `command.invoked` and no test validates a QueryResponse containing a command invocation.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateQueryResponse test with an observation whose kind is `command.invoked` and payload contains the redacted command invocation fields.
items.minimumFixScope: query-contract.ts ObservationSchema plus query response coverage for command.invoked.

items.title: Redacted command arguments may still carry shape and length metadata
items.recommendation: Model ArgShapeSchema as a union or add a refinement: either redacted is present and shape/length/present are absent, or redacted is absent and the allowed shape metadata is present according to the non-sensitive contract.
items.reproduction: CommandInvokedObservationSchema.safeParse with a redacted arg that also includes shape, length, and present succeeds.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test asserts the sample redacted token lacks shape and length, but does not try to parse an invalid redacted argument that includes those fields.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test asserting CommandInvokedObservationSchema rejects a redacted argument with shape, length, or present fields.
items.minimumFixScope: ArgShapeSchema refinement/union plus command-invoked.test coverage.

items.title: Region builders allow schema-invalid zero line or column values
items.recommendation: Make invalid regions unrepresentable or rejected: use `NonZeroU32` for line/column inputs, return `Result` from checked constructors, or clamp only if that behaviour is explicitly acceptable for all producers.
items.reproduction: Construct `SarifLog::new(Run::new(vec![ReportingDescriptor::new("r")], vec![SarifResult::new("r", Level::Warning, "m").location(Location::new("a.rs", Some(Region::line(0).column(0))))]))` and validate it against the bundled SARIF schema; validation reports minimum violations for `startLine` and `startColumn`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The schema-validation and golden-shape tests only exercise positive line and column values (`42`, `5`, and `1`), so they never assert that the public builder rejects or prevents zero-valued regions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that attempts to create a zero-valued region through the public API and asserts it is rejected or impossible to construct; if using fallible constructors, also validate that no schema-invalid SARIF can be emitted for `startLine: 0` or `startColumn: 0`.
items.minimumFixScope: Change `Region` construction API and update this crate's tests plus any crate-local call sites that pass raw `u32` line or column values.

items.title: Adapter claims APS export support while serialize always fails
items.recommendation: Implement APS markdown serialization, or override canExport to return false for APS formats until serialization is available and update the tests to match that contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test suite asserts canExport but never calls serialize for APS markdown, so the advertised capability is not exercised end to end.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that builds a minimal valid APSPlan, asserts canExport('aps') is true only when serialize returns success, and verifies the emitted markdown can be parsed back or at least contains the expected APS task fields.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts and packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/__tests__/adapter.test.ts.

items.title: Detected APS index files parse into empty plans instead of preserving modules
items.recommendation: Either add an index parsing branch that preserves module links in the APSPlan representation, or stop detecting index files as parseable until index conversion is implemented. If index import is intentionally unsupported, return a parse error instead of an empty successful plan.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover index detection only; all parse tests use leaf specs or inline task documents.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that passes the existing Modules-section fixture through detect and parse, then asserts either a structured module representation is preserved or parse fails with an explicit unsupported-index error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/adapters/src/aps-markdown/adapter.ts parse/conversion logic plus aps-markdown adapter tests.

items.title: Air-gapped dry-run test accepts any normal process exit
items.recommendation: Assert the specific allowed exit codes instead of only checking for a non-signal exit. Import or duplicate the stable `EXIT_DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE` value used by the launcher and accept only `Some(0)` or `Some(EXIT_DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE)`. Include stderr in the failure message as it does today.
items.reproduction: Change `anvil-run --dry-run` to return any ordinary non-signal exit code under the harness, for example 101; `anvil_run_dry_run_exits_cleanly_with_no_network` would still pass because `status.code().is_some()` remains true.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test is the coverage for this behaviour, but its only assertion permits every normal exit code.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Update `anvil_run_dry_run_exits_cleanly_with_no_network` to assert `matches!(out.status.code(), Some(0) | Some(EXIT_DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE))`.
items.minimumFixScope: Tighten the assertion in `crates/anvil-run/tests/air_gapped_run.rs` and reference the launcher refusal code constant used by production code.

items.title: Index APS files are detected as supported but parse path is leaf-only
items.recommendation: Either implement an index parse branch using the APS index/loader API and map linked module tasks into the APSPlan, or stop detecting Modules-only index files as importable until parse supports them.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests cover index detection but every parse test uses a leaf spec fixture or inline Tasks document; no test calls parse() on a Modules index.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that passes the existing index-shaped content from the detection tests to parse() and asserts the intended result, either a populated plan from linked modules or an explicit unsupported-index error with detect() returning false for that input.
items.minimumFixScope: APSMarkdownAdapter.detect/parse plus aps-markdown adapter tests.

items.title: Adapter claims export support while serialize always returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED
items.recommendation: Until serialization exists, override canExport() to return false for these formats and update the canExport test accordingly. If export support is required now, implement serialize() and add round-trip coverage.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests assert canExport() only; they do not call serialize() after canExport() returns true.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that every format for which canExport(format) is true can successfully serialize a minimal APSPlan, or assert canExport('aps') is false while serialize remains unimplemented.
items.minimumFixScope: APSMarkdownAdapter serialize/canExport behaviour and the canImport/canExport test block.

items.title: Task list parsing loses block ownership and can drop Inputs lists
items.recommendation: Parse task content as an ordered stream of top-level blocks. When collecting a top-level list for a task, do not also collect its descendant paragraphs as task paragraphs. Associate an empty Inputs field only with the immediately following list block rather than with lists[0] after paragraph/list separation.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover inline Inputs, Inputs as the final field followed by a list, and list precedence over inline text, but they do not cover an Inputs list followed by another task field or parseDocument's real AST traversal collecting nested list item paragraphs.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add parseDocument coverage for a task containing Intent, empty Inputs, a two-item list, then Validation; assert both inputs and validation are present. Add a case where an Inputs list item contains bold text such as **Files:** note and assert it remains input text rather than setting task.files.
items.minimumFixScope: Update parser task-content collection and parseTaskFields list association logic, plus focused parser tests for ordered list-field adjacency.

items.title: Concurrent create can insert multiple active admin keys for one actor
items.recommendation: Enforce one live key per actor atomically, preferably with a partial unique index on actor_email where revoked_at IS NULL plus conflict handling, or by taking a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by actorEmail before the SELECT/INSERT. Also audit every row returned by revoke if multiple rows remain possible.
items.reproduction: Run two create invocations concurrently against an empty admin_keys table for the same ACTOR_EMAIL with different BEARER_HEX values; both transactions can pass the SELECT before either INSERT commits.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the context file is only package metadata; there is no included test that runs concurrent create/revoke flows against a database.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration test that starts two concurrent create commands for the same actor with different bearers and asserts that only one active admin_keys row exists and the losing command fails cleanly.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key create/revoke transaction logic plus the admin_keys schema or migration that defines active-row uniqueness.

items.title: Create stdout uses hashedKey while the documented JSON contract says hashed_key
items.recommendation: Emit the documented property name, or explicitly document and test hashedKey if that is the intended public contract. For compatibility, consider temporarily emitting both keys if downstream consumers may already rely on hashedKey.
items.reproduction: Run admin-key-manage.mjs create with valid environment variables and inspect stdout; the JSON contains hashedKey, not hashed_key.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no linked tests that execute the create command and assert the stdout schema.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a command-level test that runs create against a test database and asserts stdout contains id and the intended hash property name.
items.minimumFixScope: admin-key-manage.mjs stdout object and any downstream consumer or documentation that names the field.

items.title: DATABASE_URL substring check can silently disable TLS for remote databases
items.recommendation: Parse DATABASE_URL with new URL(), inspect hostname exactly, and only disable SSL for localhost, 127.0.0.1, and ::1. Prefer requiring an explicit local/dev override instead of inferring from a substring.
items.reproduction: Set DATABASE_URL to a remote PostgreSQL URL whose password or query string contains localhost; the Client is constructed with ssl undefined even though the hostname is remote.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included test asserts DATABASE_URL hostname classification or the pg Client ssl option.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add focused tests for remote host with localhost in password/query, localhost, 127.0.0.1, and a normal remote host, asserting the expected ssl option.
items.minimumFixScope: Replace the substring check in admin-key-manage.mjs and add URL-classification coverage.

items.title: File cache index overwrites concurrent provider updates
items.recommendation: Serialize index mutations across providers/processes or reload and merge the latest index before saving. A lock file around load-modify-save, append-only entry discovery, or compare-and-retry write protocol would avoid lost updates.
items.reproduction: Create two FileCacheProvider instances pointing at the same temp directory. Let both load the index before either save completes, then set different keys concurrently with Promise.all. Re-open a third provider and only one key may be present in index.json, depending on the final save order.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The file-cache tests use one provider instance for normal set/get paths and only create a second provider after the first set has completed for persistence. They do not exercise concurrent writers sharing one cache directory.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with two FileCacheProvider instances sharing one temp cache directory that concurrently set distinct keys, then verify a fresh provider can read both entries and stats/index entry count is 2.
items.minimumFixScope: Change FileCacheProvider index update/save logic to coordinate or merge concurrent mutations, and add multi-provider concurrency coverage.

items.title: All-gate invalidation pattern does not match real gate cache keys
items.recommendation: Change allGateInvalidationPattern() to return 'gate:**', or change provider wildcard semantics so 'gate:*' intentionally matches all remaining segments. Keep the helper and provider semantics aligned in tests.
items.reproduction: Set a cache entry under key 'gate:check:eslint:abc', then call invalidatePattern(allGateInvalidationPattern()). The pattern is 'gate:*', so patternToRegex builds /^gate:[^:]*$/ and the entry is not invalidated.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: cache-key.test.ts only asserts that allGateInvalidationPattern() returns the literal string 'gate:*'. Provider tests verify literal patterns directly, but no test passes allGateInvalidationPattern() to a provider with real generated gate keys.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a cache provider test that stores 'gate:check:eslint:abc', calls invalidatePattern(allGateInvalidationPattern()), and expects the entry count invalidated to be 1 for both memory and file providers.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the all-gate invalidation helper and its tests; add provider-level coverage for the exported helper.

items.title: README omits current device-confirm auth and public-key requirements
items.recommendation: Update the endpoint table to mark /auth/device/confirm as licence-authenticated, and add LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY plus LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY_KID, if operator-managed, to the environment variable table with the expected SPKI/KID contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The tests verify the implemented auth and key behaviour, but no documentation drift test checks that README endpoint auth and environment-variable tables match the route and health contracts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a lightweight docs contract check that asserts documented required env vars include LICENSE_PUBLIC_KEY and that the README auth table marks /api/v1/auth/device/confirm consistently with the route's requireAuth middleware.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/README.md endpoint and environment-variable sections, plus optional docs-contract coverage.

items.title: Published package omits its own operational scripts
items.recommendation: Either include the operational assets in package.json files, or remove package-level scripts that are only valid from the monorepo checkout. If the migration runner is supported from the package, ship scripts plus the SQL migration directory, or copy SQL assets into dist and update the runner path.
items.reproduction: Pack the package and inspect the tarball contents; package.json remains, but scripts/migrate.mjs, scripts/check-runtime-cjs.cjs, and src/db/migrations/*.sql are absent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests exercise migration logic from source fixtures, but there is no package contract test that packs @eddacraft/anvil-api and runs or verifies the advertised package scripts from the packed file set.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package smoke test that runs pnpm pack --dry-run --json for apps/anvil-api and asserts the tarball file list contains the migration runner, runtime CJS checker, and SQL migration assets required by the package scripts.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/package.json files allow-list and, if needed, the build/migration asset-copy path plus a package pack-content regression test.

items.title: Token consume queries can win stale validity races
items.recommendation: Move validity predicates into the atomic consume statements. Refresh-token consume should require consumed_at IS NULL, revoked_at IS NULL, and expires_at > now(); device-code consume should require confirmed_at IS NOT NULL and expires_at > now(). If callers need different response shapes, return a small result enum rather than relying on stale pre-checks.
items.reproduction: Session refresh race: request A reads an unrevoked refresh token, then an admin revoke transaction sets revoked_at before A calls consumeRefreshToken. A's UPDATE still matches because it only checks consumed_at, then A inserts a new refresh token and signs a licence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Route tests mock consumeRefreshToken and consumeDeviceCode, so they verify caller branching but not the SQL predicates. apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/queries.test.ts covers scope lookup and revoke-family transaction behaviour only; it has no assertions for the consume SQL.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add query-level tests with a recording tagged-template mock that assert consumeRefreshToken and consumeDeviceCode include the revoked/expiry validity predicates and return false/null when no row is consumed.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/queries.ts consume predicates, plus any route handling adjustments for newly failed consume attempts.

items.title: Dry-run migrations create the tracking table
items.recommendation: Make dry-run read-only. For dry runs, inspect the tracking table only if it already exists, treat a missing tracking table as zero applied migrations, and defer ensureTrackingTable to non-dry-run execution.
items.reproduction: Call runMigrations(runner, { dir, dryRun: true }) with a real database that has no _migrations table; the dry run creates _migrations before listing pending files.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The dry-run test only asserts BEGIN and COMMIT are absent. It does not assert CREATE TABLE is absent, and the fake runner accepts the tracking-table DDL during dry-run.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend the dry-run test to assert no CREATE TABLE call is recorded, and add a missing-tracking-table dry-run case that reports all files pending without creating _migrations.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/db/migrate.ts dry-run control flow and apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/migrate.test.ts coverage.

items.title: validateSpec accepts array-based element maps after normalisation
items.recommendation: Reject arrays before normalising: if Array.isArray(elements), return the original spec or fail validation explicitly. Keep the visible injection limited to plain record-like element maps.
items.reproduction: Call validateSpec({ root: '0', elements: [{ type: 'Stack', props: {}, children: [] }] }); it returns { valid: true, errors: [] }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: schema-validator.test.ts covers a non-object root value and missing required fields, but it does not include an elements array case. specs.test.ts only validates fixture files, so it cannot catch malformed caller input.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a validateSpec test that passes root: '0' with elements as an array and expects valid to be false with at least one error.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/libs/render/src/schema-validator.ts plus a focused test in packages/libs/render/src/schema-validator.test.ts

items.title: Duration formatting can display impossible 60-second remainders
items.recommendation: Round or floor the total seconds before splitting into minutes and seconds, then derive minutes and remainder from that single normalised total. Define the intended fractional-second behaviour in the test.
items.reproduction: Render MetricCard with { label: 'Runtime', value: '119.6', format: 'duration' }; the displayed value is '1m 60s'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included MetricCard tests validate only schema acceptance through validateSpec. They do not render MetricCard or exercise duration formatting edge cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a MetricCard render test for value '119.6' with format 'duration' and assert the output is normalised, for example '2m 0s', and does not contain '60s'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/libs/render/src/components/metric-card.tsx plus a focused component formatting test

items.title: Warning IDs collide for multiple warnings on the same rule, file, and line
items.recommendation: Include enough location detail to make IDs unique when available, such as column, or detect collisions and append a deterministic disambiguator. Update parseWarningId/findWarningById and short-ID resolution consistently with the chosen format.
items.reproduction: Create two Warning objects with id 'AP-003', location.file 'src/a.ts', location.line 10, and different location.column values. indexWarningsById([w1, w2]) returns a Map of size 1 and one warning is no longer reachable by ID.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: warning-id.test.ts only indexes warnings with distinct rule/file/line combinations and does not include same-line warnings with different columns.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a warning-id test with two warnings sharing rule/file/line but different columns and assert generated IDs remain distinct and both map entries are retained.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/warnings/warning-id.ts plus warning-id tests

items.title: Exported warning ID pattern disagrees with parser about valid line numbers
items.recommendation: Change WARNING_ID_PATTERN to require a positive line number, for example using `(?:[1-9]\d*)`, or derive validation from parseWarningId to avoid duplicate rules.
items.reproduction: WARNING_ID_PATTERN.test('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns true, while parseWarningId('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns null and isValidWarningId('AP-003-file.ts:0') returns false.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Tests cover parseWarningId and isValidWarningId for line 0, but there are no assertions for the exported WARNING_ID_PATTERN.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Assert that WARNING_ID_PATTERN rejects 'AP-003-file.ts:0' and accepts a positive-line ID.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/warnings/warning-id.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/warnings/warning-id.test.ts

items.title: SpecKit v2 import adapter is not reachable through the package entrypoint
items.recommendation: Export SpecKitImportAdapterV2 through the public SpecKit/root entrypoint, or add an explicit package subpath export if the v2 adapter is meant to be separate.
items.reproduction: Consume @eddacraft/anvil-adapters and try to import SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from the package root; it is not exported. A package subpath import is also blocked by the exports map.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The v2 tests import the internal module directly, so they verify implementation behavior but not the published package API exposed by src/index.ts and package.json.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an entrypoint test that imports SpecKitImportAdapterV2 from ../index.js or the built package root and asserts it is constructible and supports the v2 formats.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the public export surface and add one public-entrypoint regression test.

items.title: impact affected-symbol cap is input-order dependent despite deterministic report contract
items.recommendation: Deduplicate and sort the non-absolute changed-file seeds before collecting affected symbols, then apply MAX_AFFECTED_SYMBOLS in SymbolIdentity order or another documented deterministic order. Reuse that sorted seed list for the dependent frontier.
items.reproduction: Use two changed files that each define more than half of MAX_AFFECTED_SYMBOLS symbols. Calling collect_impact with ["a.ts", "b.ts"] versus ["b.ts", "a.ts"] will select a different capped affected-symbol subset, even though project_impact sorts both outputs afterwards.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing deterministic impact test uses a small uncapped change set, and the affected-cap test verifies later files still seed dependents but does not compare capped affected-symbol output across input orders.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a capped impact test that builds enough symbols in two files to exceed MAX_AFFECTED_SYMBOLS, calls run_impact with the same paths in opposite orders, and asserts identical affected_symbols and summary output.
items.minimumFixScope: Normalise changed-file seeds in collect_impact before affected-symbol collection and add capped-order regression coverage.

items.title: find_dependents silently hides dependents when the lock-held walk hits its node cap
items.recommendation: Return a collected dependents wrapper that carries both candidates and a walk_truncated flag, and propagate that into the projection summary. If RedactionSummary.truncated must remain the page-more signal, add an explicit budget/truncation field to the dependents projection instead of overloading it silently.
items.reproduction: Construct a DependencyGraph with more than MAX_DEPENDENTS_WALK direct importers of one file, call collect_dependents for that file at depth 1, then paginate project_dependents through all returned candidates. The final projection will report no next_cursor and truncated=false while dependents beyond the cap are absent.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing dependents tests cover depth truncation, pagination, deterministic ordering, cursor rejection, and absolute-path drops, but none creates more than MAX_DEPENDENTS_WALK dependents or asserts a budget-cap signal.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test with MAX_DEPENDENTS_WALK + 1 direct importers of src/a.ts, verify only MAX_DEPENDENTS_WALK results are materialised and the projection exposes that the walk was budget-truncated even on the final page.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the collect_dependents return type and project_dependents input/summary handling, plus update call sites in save_time.rs and tests.

items.title: Public root package entrypoint lacks smoke coverage
items.recommendation: Add a root entrypoint smoke test that imports representative public symbols from src/index.ts, and optionally a build smoke test against dist/index.js for package publication confidence.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing tests import from ./index.js within submodule folders, direct implementation files such as ./parse-document.js, or sibling modules such as ../loader/index.js; none load the package root src/index.ts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add src/index.test.ts importing { parseDocument, parseIndex, loadPlan, filterPlan, validatePlanningDoc, TaskLocker, generateAllTemplates, ParseError } from './index.js' and assert each binding is defined with the expected runtime type.
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only change covering the root barrel entrypoint.

items.title: Website builds can pass while TypeScript is broken
items.recommendation: Either remove `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` or add a website `typecheck` target/script and make the Nx/package build pipeline depend on it before `next build`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and the included package/project configuration does not show a build-time typecheck gate.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a CI/project check that runs the website typecheck target and fails on an intentionally introduced `.tsx` type error, separate from `next build`.
items.minimumFixScope: Website Next config plus website package/project build targets.

items.title: Telemetry default is described inconsistently across public policy pages
items.recommendation: Align both pages to the actual CLI behaviour: either state that telemetry is disabled by default and how to opt in, or state that it is enabled by default and how to opt out.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and no included test asserts consistency between privacy/security policy claims.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a content consistency test or snapshot assertion for the telemetry default wording on `/privacy` and `/security`.
items.minimumFixScope: Privacy and security page copy for the telemetry section.

items.title: Public security page publishes a placeholder PGP fingerprint
items.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with the real fingerprint and ensure the advertised `.well-known/pgp-key.txt` endpoint is present, or remove the PGP section until the key is available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and there is no included content validation that rejects placeholder security material.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a content test that renders `/security` and fails if the PGP fingerprint contains placeholder text such as `XXXX` or if the advertised key URL is not configured.
items.minimumFixScope: Security page content and the corresponding public key asset/route.

items.title: Fenced code closes on opening fences with info text
items.recommendation: Use separate open and close handling. Keep opening fences permissive enough for info strings, but when fenceMarker is set only close on the same marker character with length >= the opener and no non-whitespace text after the marker.
items.reproduction:
Call extractSections on "## Real
```
```ts
## Not a heading
```
after". The expected result is one section because ## Not a heading is inside the original fence; the current implementation exits the fence at ```ts and returns an extra section.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Existing fence tests cover bare closing fences, different marker characters, and too-short closing fences, but not an in-fence same-length marker followed by non-whitespace text.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add an extractSections test where a fenced block contains a line beginning with the same fence marker plus info text, followed by an H2-looking line, and assert it remains inside the original section body.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/anvil/core/src/anvil-format/sections.ts and packages/anvil/core/src/anvil-format/sections.test.ts

items.title: TTL config validates each field but not the configured bounds relationship
items.recommendation: Add an object-level refine/superRefine requiring min_ttl_days <= max_ttl_days and min_ttl_days <= default_ttl_days <= max_ttl_days after defaults are applied.
items.reproduction: TtlConfigSchema.safeParse({ default_ttl_days: 30, min_ttl_days: 90, max_ttl_days: 7 }).success is true even though no TTL can satisfy the configured range.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing test only checks defaults; it does not cover invalid min/default/max relationships.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests rejecting min_ttl_days > max_ttl_days and default_ttl_days outside the configured bounds while preserving the current default parse behaviour.
items.minimumFixScope: TtlConfigSchema refinement and focused schema tests.

items.title: Provenance expansion can emit undefined session IDs
