items.recommendation: Make the audit insert conditional on the update result, for example by using a CTE that inserts audit rows only from the updated row, or by splitting the flow so no audit insert is issued when UPDATE ... RETURNING is empty.
items.reproduction: Delete the beta_users row after findUserByEmail succeeds but before the transaction executes. The transaction can return an empty update result and a populated audit result, then the handler returns 404 while the audit row remains committed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The deletion-race test asserts the 404 response, but it mocks a transaction result that includes an audit row and does not fail on the false audit side effect.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a deletion-race test that proves no user.email.updated audit statement is committed when UPDATE beta_users returns zero rows, ideally through a fake transaction executor or SQL-shape assertion that the audit insert is conditional.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/admin.ts and the focused POST /admin/user/email-update tests.

items.title: No regression coverage for the new /security route
items.recommendation: Add a focused website test or build-time route smoke check for /security that verifies the route renders and includes the expected title, disclosure email, scope, and PGP/fingerprint content.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The provided feature metadata has an empty tests list, and none of the included context files define a test target or test file for this route.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Render the /security page with the website test setup and assert it exposes ANVIL-SECURITY(7), security@eddacraft.ai, and a non-placeholder PGP fingerprint.
items.minimumFixScope: Add one focused test for apps/website/app/security/page.tsx or include /security in an existing website route smoke test.

items.title: Security page advertises a placeholder PGP key fingerprint
items.recommendation: Publish the real PGP fingerprint and ensure it matches the key served at /.well-known/pgp-key.txt, or remove the encrypted-communications section until a verifiable key is available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the included files contain no route/content test that asserts the PGP fingerprint is real rather than a placeholder.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a website route/content test for /security that fails if the PGP fingerprint contains placeholder tokens such as XXXX and, if feasible, verifies the displayed fingerprint against the static well-known key fixture.
items.minimumFixScope: Update .claude/worktrees/feat+usage-002/apps/website/app/security/page.tsx and the served well-known PGP key asset so the displayed fingerprint and published key are consistent.

items.title: Callback route has no direct tests for success, CSRF, or error paths
items.recommendation: Add focused Vitest coverage for the route by mocking decryptState and exchangeGithubCode. Cover missing params, provider denial, invalid state, nonce mismatch, pending/error exchange results, and successful session issuance with the expected cookie attributes and redirect URL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and none of the provided files contains a callback route test. The Vitest config only shows that such tests would be discovered if present.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create app/auth/callback/route.test.ts that constructs NextRequest instances for each callback branch, mocks @/lib/state and @/lib/bauth, then asserts response status, Location, Set-Cookie values, and nonce clearing behaviour.
items.minimumFixScope: Add route-level tests under apps/docs-shell/app/auth/callback without changing production behaviour.

items.title: Anvil card hard-codes the production docs host
items.recommendation: Use a site-relative cross-app route such as /anvil/overview unless the product requirement is explicitly to leave every environment for production. If production-only navigation is intended, document that in the route or configuration so previews do not treat it as an accidental host escape.
items.reproduction: Run the docs-public site or a preview deployment on any non-production host and click the Anvil card; navigation goes to https://docs.eddacraft.ai/anvil/overview instead of the current host's /anvil/overview route.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and the owned page has no route/link assertion that would catch host-specific navigation regressions.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a docs-public page rendering test or lightweight link integrity test that asserts the Anvil card points at /anvil/overview rather than an absolute production URL.
items.minimumFixScope: Change the Anvil section href in apps/docs-public/src/pages/index.tsx and add a focused assertion for the homepage card links.

items.title: Backward-compatibility activation tombstone has no regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add a focused regression check that asserts /auth/activate renders the tombstone content and still resolves when a code query string is present.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no tests, and the inspected website package manifest has no test script covering this route.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route smoke test or e2e check for /auth/activate and /auth/activate?code=legacy that expects a 200 response and visible CLI guidance such as "Activation has moved into the CLI" and "anvil auth login".
items.minimumFixScope: Test-only coverage for the activation tombstone route; no production code change is required unless the test exposes an existing routing failure.

items.title: Confirmed device code is consumed before token persistence succeeds
items.recommendation: Make the consume-and-issue operation transactional or reorder it so the code is only irreversibly consumed after all required persistence succeeds. If the database helper cannot cover JWT signing, at least persist the refresh token and mark/consume in one atomic database transaction with rollback on failure.
items.reproduction: Mock consumeDeviceCode to return { user_id: 'user-1' }, findUserById to return an active user, and insertRefreshToken to reject. POST /auth/device/poll returns 500, and a subsequent retry would hit the already-consumed path and return { status: 'expired' }.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The poll tests cover the happy confirmed path and the already-consumed sibling path, but they do not simulate a failure after consumeDeviceCode succeeds and before insertRefreshToken completes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a poll test where consumeDeviceCode succeeds and insertRefreshToken rejects; assert the route either leaves the code retryable or performs all persistence atomically rather than returning an unrecoverable consumed state.
items.minimumFixScope: apps/anvil-api/src/routes/auth-device.ts plus the database helper/transaction layer used by consumeDeviceCode and insertRefreshToken if needed.

items.title: robots.txt route lacks regression coverage for crawler policy
items.recommendation: Add a focused Vitest test for the route handler that imports `GET`, calls it, and asserts status 200, `Content-Type`, `Cache-Control`, the `/anvil/` and `/auth/` disallow rules, and the sitemap URL.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no tests, and the docs-shell Vitest configuration would only run matching `*.test.ts` or `*.test.tsx` files; none are linked for this route.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create `.claude/worktrees/rs005-ast/apps/docs-shell/app/robots.txt/route.test.ts` that awaits `GET()`, reads `response.text()`, and asserts the expected crawler directives and response headers.
items.minimumFixScope: One route-level Vitest test file; no production code change is required unless the test exposes an intended contract change.

items.title: Crawler exclusion misses the /anvil root path
items.recommendation: Emit a directive that covers the root path too, for example `Disallow: /anvil` or both `Disallow: /anvil` and `Disallow: /anvil/`, and keep it aligned with the `/anvil/:path*` header rule.
items.reproduction: Fetch `/llms.txt`; the only exclusion is `Disallow: /anvil/`, leaving the exact `/anvil` path outside that directive.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, so there is no assertion that the generated policy covers both the Anvil root and descendants.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test that calls `GET()` and asserts the response body excludes `/anvil` as well as descendant Anvil paths.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the static BODY in the route and add a focused route test.

items.title: No route test pins the llms.txt response contract
items.recommendation: Add a small Vitest test for `GET()` that verifies status 200, `Content-Type`, `Cache-Control`, and the expected policy body.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature has no linked tests, and no included test file covers this route.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create `app/llms.txt/route.test.ts` importing `GET`, then assert the response status, headers, and body text.
items.minimumFixScope: Add one focused test file under the docs-shell app.

items.title: Footer year can stay stale after a long-running server crosses into a new year
items.recommendation: Compute the year inside `HomePage()` or render it from a request-time/server-time value so forced dynamic rendering actually reflects the current year.
items.reproduction: Start the docs-shell server before midnight on December 31, keep the same process alive past January 1, then request `/` and observe that the footer can still render the prior year.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, and the existing Vitest configuration only defines test discovery; it does not include a time-bound rendering test for the homepage footer.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a homepage render test that freezes system time and verifies the footer uses the render-time year, not a module-initialisation year.
items.minimumFixScope: Move `new Date().getFullYear()` into `HomePage()` or an equivalent render-time helper in `apps/docs-shell/app/page.tsx`.

items.title: Next build can publish the route even when TypeScript is broken
items.recommendation: Remove `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` or add a package/Nx typecheck target and make the website build pipeline require it before `next build` can pass.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, and the package manifest only exposes build, dev, lint, and start scripts for the website app.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a website typecheck CI target, then introduce a temporary type error in an imported route component and assert the website release check fails before deployment.
items.minimumFixScope: Website Next config plus the website package/Nx build or CI target wiring.

items.title: Login route has no direct regression coverage
items.recommendation: Add focused Vitest coverage for GET that sets required environment variables, calls the route with and without a next parameter, and asserts the GitHub redirect URL contains client_id, redirect_uri, scope, and state while the response sets an httpOnly, secure, lax oauth-nonce cookie scoped to /auth/callback.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature declares no linked tests, and the provided Vitest configuration only shows which files would be discovered, not any existing route test for apps/docs-shell/app/auth/login/route.ts.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Create apps/docs-shell/app/auth/login/route.test.ts that mocks or exercises encryptState deterministically, invokes GET with a NextRequest for /auth/login?next=/anvil, and verifies the redirect and nonce cookie contract.
items.minimumFixScope: Add a route-level test file under apps/docs-shell covering /auth/login GET behaviour.

items.title: Auth routes are only excluded by robots.txt, not by noindex headers
items.recommendation: Add a matching header rule for /auth/:path* in next.config.ts, or otherwise ensure auth routes emit X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow at the response level.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included for this route or for the Next headers contract, so there is no assertion that every robots-disallowed private route also has a noindex response header.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test around next.config.ts headers() asserting both /anvil/:path* and /auth/:path* receive X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, and a route test asserting robots.txt still lists both disallowed paths.
items.minimumFixScope: Update docs-shell next.config.ts to cover /auth/:path* and add focused tests for the robots/header contract.

items.title: React preset drops upstream settings
items.recommendation: Preserve the complete relevant upstream flat config fields, at minimum by adding settings: recommendedTsConfig.settings ?? {} to the exported React config. Prefer spreading the upstream config first and then overriding only files if that matches the intended contract.
items.reproduction: With the installed dependencies, inspect @eslint-react/eslint-plugin.configs['recommended-typescript'].settings and then import packages/tooling/eslint-config/react.mjs; reactConfig[0] has no settings field.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are provided for this feature, and the package script only runs eslint over the package; it does not assert the exported flat config shape or compare it with the upstream preset.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Vitest test that imports reactConfig and @eslint-react/eslint-plugin, then asserts reactConfig[0].settings equals the recommended-typescript settings while keeping the intended JSX/TSX files filter.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/tooling/eslint-config/react.mjs and add a focused export-shape test for the React config.

items.title: Scope lookup rejects Postgres array literals that sibling token parsing accepts
items.recommendation: Reuse TextArraySchema for ScopeSchema.scopes, e.g. scopes: TextArraySchema.default(['beta']), so findActiveScopesForUser accepts the same text[] result shapes as AccessTokenSchema.
items.reproduction: Call findActiveScopesForUser with a mocked sql result of [{ active_token_count: 1, scopes: '{preview,beta}' }]; ScopeSchema.parse rejects the string even though AccessTokenSchema would normalise the same database type.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: queries.test only mocks scopes as JavaScript arrays and does not cover the string literal form that TextArraySchema was added to handle elsewhere in the same file.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a findActiveScopesForUser test with mockSql([{ active_token_count: 1, scopes: '{preview,beta}' }]) expecting ['preview', 'beta'].
items.minimumFixScope: Update findActiveScopesForUser's local ScopeSchema and add the focused regression test in apps/anvil-api/src/__tests__/queries.test.ts.

items.title: Config module is not exported from the published package
items.recommendation: Add a `./config` entry to `packages/anvil/core/package.json` pointing to `./dist/config/index.d.ts` and `./dist/config/index.js`, or remove the config barrel if it is intentionally private and keep all callers on the root export.
items.reproduction: Build and pack the package, then from a separate ESM consumer attempt `import { ConfigLoader } from '@eddacraft/anvil-core/config'`; Node package resolution will reject the missing subpath export.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included config tests import via relative source paths, so they do not exercise the package export map used by published consumers.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package exports smoke test that imports `@eddacraft/anvil-core/config` from the built package or validates the export map includes the config subpath.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the core package export map and add a focused package-level import/export regression test.

items.title: Application preset inherits composite while disabling declaration emit
items.recommendation: Either remove composite from base.json and enable it only in presets that need project references/declaration output, or override app.json with composite: false if application packages should not be composite projects.
items.reproduction: Create a tsconfig.json extending @eddacraft/anvil-tsconfig/app.json and run tsc --project tsconfig.json; TypeScript reports that composite projects may not disable declaration emit.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or config validation fixtures are included for this package, so the invalid inherited compiler option combination is not exercised.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level validation test that runs tsc --showConfig or tsc --noEmit against fixture tsconfigs extending each exported preset, including app.json.
items.minimumFixScope: Update the shared tsconfig presets so app.json no longer combines composite: true with declaration: false, and add a focused validation fixture for exported presets.

items.title: Documented config subpath is not exported by the package
items.recommendation: Add a `./config` entry to package.json exports with `types: ./dist/config.d.ts` and `import: ./dist/config.js`, or change the module documentation and intended import surface so config is only exposed through an existing exported entrypoint.
items.reproduction: After building the package, attempt `import { StackConfigSchema } from '@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/config'` from a consumer project; Node ESM resolution will reject the subpath because package.json does not define `exports["./config"]`.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: config.test.ts imports `./config.js` directly from source, bypassing package.json exports and therefore cannot detect missing packaged subpath exports.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level export smoke test that builds or resolves `@eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/config` through the package exports map and imports `StackConfigSchema`.
items.minimumFixScope: Update packages/edda-stack/package.json exports and add a focused package-export regression test.

items.title: Config module is not exported from the package export map
items.recommendation: Add a './config' entry to packages/edda-stack/package.json pointing to './dist/config.js' and './dist/config.d.ts', or remove the subpath module contract and ensure the root export re-exports the config API intentionally.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: config.test.ts uses a relative source import, so it bypasses the package exports map and cannot detect a missing published subpath.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package-level export smoke test that imports @eddacraft/anvil-edda-stack/config after build, or checks the package exports map includes './config'.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/edda-stack/package.json export map plus a package API smoke test

items.title: Earlier unusable config file prevents loading later valid config
items.recommendation: Continue to the next configured filename when a file is absent, non-object, missing the kindling section, unreadable, or invalid for Kindling, unless the intended precedence contract is explicitly first-existing-file-wins. If invalid Kindling config should be fatal, surface a typed error instead of silently defaulting.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked test file exercises query and observation safety contracts but does not import loadKindlingConfig or cover multiple config-file precedence/fallback cases.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a config loader test that creates both .anvilrc without a kindling section and anvil.config.json with {"kindling":{"enabled":true}}, then asserts loadKindlingConfig(projectRoot).enabled is true.
items.minimumFixScope: packages/kindling-integration/src/config.ts plus focused tests for loadKindlingConfig precedence and fallback behaviour.

items.title: database_path accepts paths outside the project root
items.recommendation: Constrain database_path to a non-empty, project-relative path. Reject absolute paths and normalise then reject any path that escapes the project root before handing it to a store implementation.
items.reproduction: KindlingConfigSchema.parse({ enabled: true, database_path: '/tmp/outside.db' }) succeeds, as does a traversal value like '../../outside.db'.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked tests only parse enabled/disabled config defaults and exercise service redaction/query contracts; they do not test loadKindlingConfig or invalid database_path values.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add config tests that assert absolute, empty, and parent-traversal database_path values fail validation while '.anvil/kindling.db' succeeds.
items.minimumFixScope: Update KindlingConfigSchema database_path validation and add focused config schema tests.

items.title: test script invokes undeclared Vitest binary
items.recommendation: Declare `vitest` in `apps/anvil-api/package.json` devDependencies, or replace the package script with a documented workspace-level test command if this package is intentionally not independently testable.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests or package-manifest validation were provided for this feature, and running tests from the fully bootstrapped workspace would not catch an undeclared package-local binary if the root workspace happens to provide it.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Add a package manifest validation that each script command requiring a local bin is declared by the package itself or appears in an explicit workspace-bin allowlist.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `apps/anvil-api/package.json` to include the missing test runner dependency or adjust the script/manifest policy for package-local test scripts.

items.title: SURFENV-003 fixture test does not assert two expected findings by key or indicator
items.recommendation: Assert the exact expected finding set, for example by comparing keys and indicators for DATABASE_URL/prod host, FEATURE_FLAGS_ENV/production value, SECRET_PROD/key suffix, and LEGACY_HOST/suppressed.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertions leave two of the four documented positive cases implicit behind findings.len() == 4.

items.minimumFixScope: Tighten assertions in crates/anvil-checks/tests/surfenv_prod_value.rs.

items.title: Only the first diagnostic is validated as a diagnostic envelope payload
items.recommendation: Iterate over every diagnostic and assert the required payload fields and category type for each one, then collect categories with a hard failure on missing or non-string values.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test validates one representative diagnostic and uses `filter_map`, which skips malformed category fields instead of failing.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Change the diagnostic assertions to loop over `diagnostics.iter().enumerate()` and assert `schema_version`, `mode`, `id`, `severity`, `summary`, `category`, `source.rule_id`, `source.source_module`, and `location.file` for every element.
items.minimumFixScope: Strengthen the assertions in `crates/anvil-cli/tests/ai_guardrail_profile.rs` so all returned diagnostics are validated.

items.title: AI profile integration test does not verify the process exit status
items.recommendation: Assert the expected blocking exit behaviour explicitly, for example by checking `!output.status.success()` and comparing `parsed["exit_code"]` to `output.status.code()` when available.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current assertions parse stdout and validate the envelope shape, but they do not inspect `output.status` after the command completes.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend `ai_profile_emits_diagnostic_envelope_in_json_mode` to assert that the empty-workspace AI profile exits non-zero and that the envelope exit_code equals the process exit code.
items.minimumFixScope: Update `crates/anvil-cli/tests/ai_guardrail_profile.rs` to validate process status alongside the JSON envelope exit_code.

items.title: Known residual test does not assert the documented certify outcome
items.recommendation: Add a certify assertion for the same delta using ChangeKind::ContentModify and a dependency graph, matching the documented clean certification outcome, or remove the certifies-clean claim from the test documentation if it is no longer part of the contract.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing assertion stops at export_surface_diff and never calls certify for the residual overload churn case.
items.suggestedRegressionTest: Extend identity_count_preserving_overload_churn_is_a_known_residual to assert matches!(certify(&g, &DependencyGraph::new(), &ChangeKind::ContentModify, &delta, 64), Certifiability::Certified { .. }).
items.minimumFixScope: Update crates/anvil-graph-cache/tests/identity.rs in the residual test only.

items.title: Delete/recreate test comment contradicts asserted behaviour
items.recommendation: Update the doc comment to state the actual asserted contract: delete/recreate preserves stable identities for comparable surfaces, while the create delta itself reports the recreated public surface as added.
items.whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The test asserts identity equality and added symbol count, but the stale doc comment is not checked by any test and can mislead future changes.
items.minimumFixScope: Edit the doc comment above identity_delete_recreate_yields_identical_identities in crates/anvil-graph-cache/tests/identity.rs.

items.title: Windows wire-up test accepts any string as the daemon-read content hash
items.recommendation: Assert the exact expected hash for the bytes written by workspace(), for example by importing anvil_intercept::validate_paths::content_hash and comparing against content_hash(b"export const value = 1;\n").
items.reproduction: Modify the save-time response path to return any fixed string for evaluated[0].content_hash while preserving the rest of the response shape; this test would still pass the content-hash assertion.
